'''Alvin Toles''' (born March 23, 1963) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[New Orleans Saints]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) from 1985 until 1988, when a knee injury ended his career. He played [[college football]] at the [[University of Tennessee]], initially as a [[fullback (American football)|fullback]] before switching to linebacker his junior year. He was the Saints' 1st-round pick in the [[1985 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Toles played high school football at [[Mary Persons High School]] in [[Forsyth, Georgia]], under long-time coach Dan Pitt. Playing as a fullback, he rushed for 1,663 yards during his senior season in 1980,<ref name=heeter>Jonathan Heeter, "[http://www.macon.com/2012/07/22/2098082/the-numbers-game-the-40s.html The Numbers Game: The 40s] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120727040940/http://www.macon.com/2012/07/22/2098082/the-numbers-game-the-40s.html |date=July 27, 2012 }}", ''The Telegraph'' (Macon), July 22, 2012. Retrieved: July 31, 2013.</ref> leading the Bulldogs to the Class AA state championship and a 15–0 season.<ref name=81bio>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=194&pg=60 1981 Tennessee Signees] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304035235/http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=194&pg=60 |date=March 4, 2016 }}", ''1981 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1981), p. 58.</ref> He rushed for 149 yards and 2 touchdowns in the Bulldogs' 34–6 victory over [[Duluth High School|Duluth]] in the title game.<ref>"[https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=348&dat=19801214&id=wdlMAAAAIBAJ&sjid=yjQDAAAAIBAJ&pg=4614,2258058 Bulldogs, Woodward Claim Prep Grid Titles]", ''Rome News-Tribune'', December 14, 1980, p. 5C.</ref> He earned All-State honors, and was named the "All-Middle Georgia Player of the Year" by the ''[[The Telegraph (Macon)|Macon Telegraph]]''.<ref name=heeter /> He was ranked among the top 33 recruits in the state of [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]] by the ''[[Atlanta Constitution]]''.<ref name=81bio />

==College career==
Toles joined the Tennessee Volunteers in 1981, part of a signing class that included [[Reggie McKenzie (linebacker)|Reggie McKenzie]], [[Raleigh McKenzie]], [[Johnnie Jones]], [[Alan Cockrell]] and [[Carl Zander]].<ref name=81bio /> Playing as a fullback during his freshman year, he rushed for 220 yards on 47 carries while splitting time with junior Doug Furnas.<ref>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=742&pg=58 1982 Tennessee Squad]", ''1982 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1982), p. 57.</ref> During his sophomore year in 1982, he rushed for 135 yards on 46 carries.<ref>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=198&pg=87 1982 Offensive Statistics]", ''1983 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1983), p. 89.</ref>

With 250-pound sophomore Sam Henderson poised to take over the starting slot at fullback at the start of the [[1983 Tennessee Volunteers football team|1983 season]], Toles switched to linebacker at the request of head coach [[Johnny Majors]].<ref name=hix>Tim Hix, "[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=196&pg=51&catid=45&s=alvin%20toles Vol Profile: Alvin Toles]", ''Tennessee vs. LSU Football Program'' (University of Tennessee, 1983), pp. 47-48.</ref> In spite of never having played defense, Toles had a breakout season, registering a team-leading 135 tackles (72 solo), including 8 tackles-for-loss (1 less than All-American teammate [[Reggie White]]).<ref>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=747&pg=94 1983 Defensive Statistics] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114000928/http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=747&pg=94 |date=November 14, 2013 }}", ''1984 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1984), p. 92.</ref> In the Vols' season-opening loss against [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh]], Toles had 19 tackles, one of which broke the [[clavicle|collarbone]] of Panthers quarterback John Cummings.<ref name=hix /> In Tennessee's loss to [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn]], he had 17 tackles, including 4 tackles-for-loss.<ref name=hix /> He also had 18 tackles (8 solo) against [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]], 14 tackles (8 solo) against [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets football|Georgia Tech]], and 20 tackles (7 solo) against [[Ole Miss Rebels football|Ole Miss]].<ref name=84bio>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=747&pg=62 1984 Tennessee Squad]", ''1984 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1984), p. 60.</ref> In Tennessee's 30–23 victory over [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland]] in the 1983 [[Florida Citrus Bowl]], Toles stuffed Terrapins running back [[Rick Badanjek]] at the 1-yard line to prevent a touchdown on the opening drive, and he had a fumble recovery and an interception — both of which led to scores — in the fourth quarter.<ref>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=747&pg=92 Victory Over Terps In Florida Citrus Bowl Climaxes Best UT Campaign Since 1972] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114000824/http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=747&pg=92 |date=November 14, 2013 }}", ''1984 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1984), p. 90.</ref> He finished the game with 6 tackles, and he was named the game's "Outstanding Defensive Player."<ref name=84bio />

Toles was expected to have a big year as a senior in 1984, but broke his ankle during the game against Auburn and missed the rest of the season.<ref>Rick Redding, "[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=335&pg=15&catid=46&s=alvin%20toles Gators Offer Big Challenge for Vols]", ''Tennessee vs. Florida Football Program'' (University of Tennessee, 1984), p. 11.</ref> In just four games, he had 43 tackles (26 solo), broke up a pass and recovered a fumble.<ref>"[http://diglib.lib.utk.edu/fbpro/main.php?bid=738&pg=104 1984 Defensive Statistics]", ''1985 Tennessee Volunteers Football Guide'' (University of Tennessee, 1985), p. 102.</ref> He finished his career at Tennessee with 178 tackles (98 solo), 8 of which were for a loss, to go along with the 355 yards rushing on 93 carries he had amassed while playing fullback.<ref>[http://www.utsports.com/sports/m-footbl/fball-stats/t.htm Football Career Statistics], UTSports.com. Retrieved: July 31, 2013.</ref>

==Professional career==
Toles was selected by the New Orleans Saints in the first round (24th overall pick) in the [[1985 NFL draft]], one of three Vol linebackers (the others being [[Carl Zander]] and [[Reggie McKenzie (linebacker)|Reggie McKenzie]]) to be drafted that year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1985 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1985/draft.htm |access-date=October 9, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played 55 games over four seasons for the Saints, much of it on [[special teams]] as he competed with [[Sam Mills]] and [[Vaughan Johnson]] for playing time at linebacker.<ref>[https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=iTZDAAAAIBAJ&sjid=nqwMAAAAIBAJ&pg=2095,4579481&dq=alvin-toles+1986&hl=en NFL capsules], ''Altus Times'', August 7, 1987, p. 7.</ref> In the Saints' 24–22 loss to [[San Francisco 49ers|San Francisco]] on October 25, 1987, Toles returned a blocked punt for a touchdown, temporarily giving the Saints the lead.<ref>"[https://news.google.com/newspapers?id=qphhAAAAIBAJ&sjid=DA4NAAAAIBAJ&pg=5412,2205340&dq=alvin-toles+touchdown&hl=en 49ers 24, Saints 22]", ''Bangor Daily News'', October 26, 1987, p. 18.</ref> During the Saints' 14–10 victory over the [[Los Angeles Rams]] on November 13, 1988, he suffered a serious knee injury.<ref>"[http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=AD&p_theme=ad&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB4751AE1E0E3CB&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM Toles' Knee Injury Is Grim Reminder of Risks Players Face]", ''Baton Rouge Advocate'', November 18, 1988.</ref> He was waived by the Saints in 1990.<ref>"[http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=AD&p_theme=ad&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&p_topdoc=1&p_text_direct-0=0EB475EFE6B2B6CB&p_field_direct-0=document_id&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&s_trackval=GooglePM Saints Release Jordan, 7 Others on Final Cutdown]", ''Baton Rouge Advocate'', September 4, 1990.</ref>

==Personal life==
Toles' son, [[Andrew Toles]], was a [[professional baseball]] player.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lewis |first=Barry |date=June 9, 2016 |title=Driller to watch: Andrew Toles |url=http://www.tulsaworld.com/sportsextra/drillers/driller-to-watch-andrew-toles/article_912e2ac3-5f45-5936-81fa-b877cfa9055b.html |access-date=July 8, 2016 |website=Tulsa World}}</ref>
His daughter, Morgan Toles, is a former Seminole basketball standout.

Wright, a [[nose tackle]], played with the [[National Football League]] (NFL)'s [[Los Angeles Rams]] from 1986 to 1991 and was [[All-Pro]] in 1990. ==Early life and college== Wright graduated from Randolph County High School in 1980 after leading the football team to the state playoff finals in 1979 and earned a [[Athletic scholarship|football scholarship]] with [[Jacksonville State University]] in [[Alabama]]. Wright was [[Gulf South Conference]] Freshman of the Year in 1980 and Defensive Player of the Year in 1981. He earned Honorable Mention All-America honors after the 1981 season. Wright lettered four years at Jacksonville State and had 200 career solo tackles, 388 total tackles, and 30 [[quarterback sacks]]. Wright led the Gamecocks to two Gulf South conference championships and three trips to the NCAA Division II playoffs.{{Cite web |url=http://www.jsugamecocksports.com/mobile/hof.aspx?hof=34 |title=Jsugamecocksports.com Mobile - Hall of Fame |access-date=October 7, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171008080318/http://www.jsugamecocksports.com/mobile/hof.aspx?hof=34 |archive-date=October 8, 2017 |url-status=dead }} ==Professional career== After college, Wright was drafted in the 14th round by the [[Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United States Football League|USFL]]. Rather than report to the Stallions, Wright went undrafted by the NFL and later signed as an [[undrafted free agent]] with the Rams in 1985. He briefly left the Rams' camp, but returned in 1986 and spent most of that season on the injured list with a knee injury.{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1988-09-30-sp-3159-story.html|title=Archives|website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=September 30, 1988 }} Wright was the first Rams player to cross the picket line during the [[1987 NFL players' strike]] and started his first career game against the [[New Orleans Saints]] in Week 3.{{Cite web|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1987-10-01-sp-11384-story.html|title=Archives|website=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=October 1987 }} He played 84 career games over seven seasons, starting 62, and recording 163 career solo tackles, 71 assists, and eight [[quarterback sacks]]. Wright led all Rams defensive linemen in tackles for four consecutive seasons and started 50 consecutive games from 1988 to 1991.{{Cite web |url=http://www.jsugamecocksports.com/mobile/hof.aspx?hof=34 |title=Jsugamecocksports.com Mobile - Hall of Fame |access-date=October 7, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171008080318/http://www.jsugamecocksports.com/mobile/hof.aspx?hof=34 |archive-date=October 8, 2017 |url-status=dead }} ==Personal life== Wright had a wife named Sherri Wright (Baldy) and has two children, Brittany Shantelle Wright and Eric Pool (Wright). ==Football career==
Powell spent the 1984 [[USFL]] season with the [[Oklahoma Outlaws]] based in [[Tulsa]] and then moved with the team in 1985 to become one of the [[Arizona Outlaws]] based in [[Tempe, Arizona]], after Oklahoma had merged with the [[Arizona Wranglers]]. He blocked for among others, quarterback [[Doug Williams (quarterback)|Doug Williams]] who would later win [[Super Bowl XXII]] with the [[Washington Redskins]].
Powell was drafted into the NFL in 1984 by the Seattle Seahawks, in the second round of the [[1984 NFL Supplemental Draft of USFL and CFL Players]] (49th overall).<ref>{{Cite web |title=1984 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1984/draft.htm |access-date=2023-10-10 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name=profootballreference>{{cite web

He joined the [[Miami Dolphins]] in 1989, but only played in two games<ref name=databasefootball /> before resigning.<ref name=savingstationap />

He played with the [[London Monarchs]] of the [[World Football League]] from 1991 to 1992.<ref name=imdb>{{cite web

In his first season with the Seattle Seahawks (1987), he was involved in three [[Kickoff (American football)|kickoff]]s, gaining 23 yards. However, 14 of those came from one kickoff. He also [[fumble]]d the ball once. After that season, he never was involved in another NFL kickoff. In 1987, he played in a career-high twelve games.<ref name=databasefootball /> That number sank to six the next year, and to two by 1989.

'''Amari Spievey''' (born April 15, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Iowa Hawkeyes football|Iowa Hawkeyes]]. He was considered one of the top cornerback prospects for the [[2010 NFL draft]] and was selected by the Lions in the third round.<ref>[http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=84467&draftyear=2011&genpos=CB NFL Draft Scout]</ref> 

==Early life==
Spievey attended [[Xavier High School (Middletown, Connecticut)|Xavier High School]], where he played cornerback and running back, and finished his career as the all-time leading rusher in school history. He rushed for 3,606 yards and 50 touchdowns in his career, along with 53 receptions for 858 yards and eight touchdowns.

On defense, Spievey made 87 career tackles and 16 interceptions, including two returned for touchdowns. He was a two-time coaches all-state selection and was named the Connecticut Player of the Year as a senior in 2005, the year the team won the Class LL state championship.

Regarded as a two-star recruit by ''[[Rivals.com]]'', Spievey was listed as the #15 prospect from [[New England]].<ref>{{Citation |url=https://footballrecruiting.rivals.com/viewrank.asp?ra_key=1352 |title=Postseason New England top 20 2006 |date=January 21, 2006 |work=Rivals.com }}</ref>

==College career==

===Iowa Central Community College===
Spievey [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his initial year at Iowa to preserve a year of eligibility. Spievey transferred to Iowa Central Community College after being academically ineligible for his sophomore season. There he recorded seven pass [[interception]]s and 242 return yards. He returned two of those interceptions for [[touchdown]]s and also scored two touchdowns on [[Kickoff (American football)|kickoff]] returns and recorded four blocked [[Punt (gridiron football)|punt]]s. Iowa Central CC posted 9–2 overall record to earn a No. seven national ranking, and Spievey earned junior college All-American honors.

===Iowa===
In his redshirt sophomore season at Iowa, Spievey started all games at right cornerback and ranked third on the team with 68 tackles, including 43 solo tackles and 25 assists. He also had four pass interceptions and six pass break-ups. The Big Ten coaches named him Second-team All-Big Ten afterwards.  The following year, he was named to the First-team.

==Professional career==

By mid-season of 2009, ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'s'' [[Tony Pauline]] listed Spievey as one of the "risers" for the [[2010 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Citation |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/football/nfl/11/23/risers.sliders/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104201116/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2009/football/nfl/11/23/risers.sliders/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=November 4, 2012 |title=Notre Dame's Golden Tate in 2010 NFL Draft risers and sliders |last=Pauline |first=Tony |work=Sports Illustrated |date=November 23, 2009 }}</ref> On January 11, 2010, Spievey announced that he would forgo his senior season and enter the NFL Draft.<ref>{{cite web |last=Rittenberg |first=Adam |author-link=Adam Rittenberg |date=January 11, 2010 |title=Iowa's Spievey declares for draft |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/bigten/post/_/id/9212/iowas-spievey-declares-for-draft |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100115154618/http://espn.go.com/blog/bigten/post/_/id/9212/iowas-spievey-declares-for-draft |archive-date=15 January 2010 |access-date=January 11, 2010 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> Spievey was selected by the Detroit Lions as the 2nd pick of the 3rd round (66th overall) of the 2010 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2010 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2010/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-13 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Although he played [[cornerback]] in college, Spievey was moved to [[Safety (American and Canadian football position)|safety]] by the Lions to take advantage of his tackling ability and instincts.<ref>{{cite web | last=Kowalski | first=Tom | title=Lions move rookie Amari Spievey to safety | website=mlive | date=2010-08-26 | url=https://www.mlive.com/lions/2010/08/lions_move_rookie_amari_spieve.html | access-date=2025-07-06}}</ref>

Spievey opened the 2011 NFL season as a starter at safety for the Lions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kowalski |first=Tom |date=2011-07-29 |title=Amari Spievey is starting safety as Detroit Lions open camp |url=https://www.mlive.com/lions/2011/07/amari_spievey_is_starting_safe.html |access-date=2024-05-22 |website=mlive.com |language=en}}</ref>

On August 31, 2013, he was released by the Lions.<ref>{{cite web | last=Rogers | first=Justin | title=Safety Amari Spievey, former third-round pick, released by Detroit Lions | website=mlive | date=2013-08-31 | url=https://www.mlive.com/lions/2013/08/safety_amari_spievey_former_th.html | access-date=2026-03-29}}</ref>

'''Anderson Russell''' (born May 30, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Safety (American football position)|safety]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He was signed by the [[Washington Redskins]] as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2010. He played [[college football]] for the [[Ohio State Buckeyes football|Ohio State Buckeyes]].

==Professional career==

===Washington Redskins===
Russell was signed by the [[Washington Redskins]] as a drafted free agent in 2010. He appeared in two games in 2010 before being placed on IR. He was released before the start of the 2011 season.<ref>{{cite web|last=Fitzgerald|first=Gary|title=Redskins' Roster Is At 53 After Final Cuts|url=http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Roster-Is-At-53-After-Final-Cuts/e68e2fb9-0775-43db-be72-1d48b0a0c819|publisher=Redskins.com|accessdate=February 28, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120802090355/http://www.redskins.com/news-and-events/article-1/Redskins-Roster-Is-At-53-After-Final-Cuts/e68e2fb9-0775-43db-be72-1d48b0a0c819|archive-date=August 2, 2012|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>

===Miami Dolphins===
Russell was signed to the [[Miami Dolphins]]' [[practice squad]] on September 7, 2011. He was promoted to the 53 man roster on November 3, 2012, but was released soon after.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kelly|first=Omar|title=Dolphins promote safety Anderson Russell to 53-man roster|url=http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2012-11-03/sports/sfl-dolphins-promote-safety-anderson-russell-to-53man-roster-20121103_1_53-man-roster-jonathan-amaya-reshad-jones|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407061858/http://articles.sun-sentinel.com/2012-11-03/sports/sfl-dolphins-promote-safety-anderson-russell-to-53man-roster-20121103_1_53-man-roster-jonathan-amaya-reshad-jones|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 7, 2014|publisher=Sun Sentinel|accessdate=February 28, 2014}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
Russell was signed to the [[Carolina Panthers]] practice squad shortly after his release from the Dolphins. He was promoted to the 53 man roster on December 11, 2012. He was released after three games. He re-signed in time to appear at the Panthers 2013 training camp, but was released before the start of the 2013 season.

On February 27, 2014, Russel was re-signed to the Panthers roster.<ref>{{cite web|last=Crabtree|first=Chris|title=Panthers re-sign safety Anderson Russell|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/02/27/panthers-re-sign-safety-anderson-russell/|accessdate=February 28, 2014}}</ref>

'''Aminiasi Silatolu''' (born September 16, 1988) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was an [[Guard (American and Canadian football)|offensive guard]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Midwestern State Mustangs football|Midwestern State Mustangs]] from 2010 to 2011. He was selected by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the second round of the [[2012 NFL draft]].<ref name=SilatoluDrafted>{{cite news|title=Panthers pick OG Amini Silatolu from Division II Midwestern State in 2nd round of NFL draft|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/redskins/panthers-pick-og-amini-silatolu-from-division-ii-midwestern-state-in-2nd-round-of-nfl-draft/2012/04/27/gIQArH1PmT_story.html|access-date=April 28, 2012|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|date=April 27, 2012}} {{dead link|date=June 2021|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref>

==Early life==
A native of [[Redwood City, California]], Silatolu attended [[Merrill F. West High School]] in [[Tracy, California]], where he was a lineman on both sides of the ball. The 2005 team went to the Sac-Joaquin Section Division I championship game and finished as runner-up, and in 2006 they got as far as the section semifinals.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://tracypress.com/view/full_story/18381371/article-Alumni-Report--West-grad-gets-the-call-?instance=sports_lead_story_left_column |title=Alumni Report: West grad gets the call |first=Bob |last=Brownne |newspaper=Tracy Press |date=April 27, 2012 }}</ref> Silatolu was not recognized by any recruiting service.

==College career==
After graduating from high school in 2007, Silatolu took the [[junior college]] route to [[San Joaquin Delta College]], where he was a heralded offensive tackle.<ref name=SilatoluHunger/> After starting nine of ten games at left tackle as a freshman, he had a dominant sophomore season earning California Community College Coaches' Association first-team All-America, first-team Region II All-California and first-team All-Valley Conference honors in addition to capturing All-Valley Conference Offensive Lineman of the Year. Despite his accomplishments, Silatolu was regarded as only a two-star recruit by both [[Rivals.com]] and [[Scout.com]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Aminiasi Silatolu|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/recruiting/player-Aminiasi-Silatolu-93116|publisher=Rivals.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Aminiasi Silatolu Profile|url=http://recruiting.scout.com/a.z?s=73&p=8&c=1&nid=3828971|publisher=Scout.com}}</ref> He drew interest from [[California Golden Bears football|California]], [[Hawaii Warriors football|Hawaii]], [[San Jose State Spartans football|San Jose State]], and [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee]],<ref name=SilatoluHunger>{{cite news|last=Barrows |first=Matthew |title=Lineman Silatolu, eyed by 49ers, driven by his football hunger |url=http://www.sacbee.com/2012/04/24/4436924/lineman-silatolu-eyed-by-49ers.html |access-date=April 28, 2012 |newspaper=[[The Sacramento Bee]] |date=April 24, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120427000651/http://www.sacbee.com/2012/04/24/4436924/lineman-silatolu-eyed-by-49ers.html |archive-date=April 27, 2012 }}</ref> before signing with [[Nevada Wolfpack football|Nevada]]. However, he did not qualify academically and had to sit out the 2009 season.<ref name=SilatoluDrafted/><ref>{{cite news |url=http://jcfootball.scout.com/2/1181218.html |title=Silatolu remembers his roots |work=Scout.com |date=April 26, 2012 |access-date=April 8, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140419232905/http://jcfootball.scout.com/2/1181218.html |archive-date=April 19, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Silatolu transferred to [[NCAA Division II|Division II]] Midwestern State, where he dominated the competition with his aggressive play, and was a two-time All-American in 2010 and 2011. Protecting the blind side of quarterback [[Zack Eskridge]], Silatolu draw the attention of NFL scouts.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.deltacollegian.net/2012/04/27/former-mustang-to-be-considered-in-draft/ |title=Former Mustang to be considered in draft |date=April 27, 2012 |work=San Joaquin Delta Collegian }}</ref> He delivered 182 knockdowns and 43 touchdown-resulting blocks, and allowed just one-half sack and one quarterback pressure in 560 pass plays. He was selected as the [[Lone Star Conference]] Offensive Lineman of the Year both of his seasons at MSU,<ref name=PanthersSilatolu>{{cite news|last=Gholson|first=Nick|title=Panthers select Silatolu: MSU lineman makes history as No. 40 pick |url=http://www.timesrecordnews.com/news/2012/apr/28/panthers-select-silatolu/ |access-date=May 3, 2012|newspaper=[[Times Record News]]|date=April 28, 2012}}</ref> and in 2011 finished as runner-up in voting for the [[Gene Upshaw Award]], which is presented to the nation's top Division II lineman. He was invited to participate in the [[2012 Senior Bowl]]—the first MSU player to ever receive an invitation—but was unable to play due to an injury.<ref>{{cite news |last=Clements |first=Ron |url=http://www.timesrecordnews.com/news/2012/feb/27/silatolu-has-his-nfl-audition-ex-msu-star-wows/ |title=Silatolu has his NFL audition: Ex-MSU star wows observers |date=February 27, 2012 |work=Times Record News}}</ref> Besides [[Rishaw Johnson]], Silatolu was the only D-II player invited to the 2012 Senior Bowl.

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
Projected as a late-first to second-round prospect,<ref>{{cite web|title=Amini Silatolu {{!}} Midwestern State, OG : 2012 NFL Draft Scout Player Profile|url=http://www.nfldraftscout.com/ratings/dsprofile.php?pyid=96449&draftyear=2012&genpos=OG|publisher=nfldraftscout.com|access-date=May 3, 2012}}</ref> Silatolu was considered one of the top offensive linemen available in the [[2012 NFL draft]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/tony_pauline/02/25/combine.offensive.line/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140525213346/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/tony_pauline/02/25/combine.offensive.line/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=May 25, 2014 |title=Glenn, Kalil lead impressive group of offensive linemen at combine |work=[[SI.com]] |date=February 25, 2012 |first=Tony |last=Pauline }}</ref> and drew comparisons to [[Jahri Evans]].<ref>{{YouTube|sdqMemBv6P8|PFW's #22 NFL Draft Prospect: Midwestern State OG Amini Silatolu}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers (first stint)===
Silatolu was selected in the second round with the 40th overall pick by the [[Carolina Panthers]], the first Midwestern State player ever selected in the 2012 NFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2012 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2012/draft.htm |access-date=2023-05-14 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name=PanthersSilatolu/> He is the highest-selected offensive lineman from Division II since [[Jermane Mayberry]] in [[1996 NFL draft|1996]],{{Citation needed|date=May 2012}} and the highest-selected player from the Lone Star Conference since Mayberry. Silatolu, Mayberry, and [[Gene Upshaw]] are the only offensive linemen from LSC teams ever selected in the first two rounds.<ref>{{cite web|title=Heads Carolina! Silatolu drafted in second round by Panthers|url=http://msumustangs.com/news/2012/4/27/FB_0427123000.aspx|publisher=Midwestern State Mustangs Athletics|access-date=May 3, 2012|date=April 27, 2012}}</ref>

Silatolu was the first interior lineman selected in the first two rounds by the Panthers since [[Ryan Kalil]] in [[2007 NFL draft]]. On May 11, 2012, Silatolu was signed by the Panthers to a four-year contract worth $4.9 million that included a $2 million signing bonus.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://network.yardbarker.com/nfl/article_external/source_panthers_agree_to_terms_with_amini_silatolu_with_four_year_deal/10769741|title=Scout.com: Amini Silatolu Profile|website=network.yardbarker.com|access-date=July 24, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/nfcsouth/post/_/id/34977/nfc-south-rookie-contract-numbers |title=NFC South rookie contract numbers |work=ESPN.com |date=May 15, 2012 }}</ref> He started the first 15 games for the Panthers at left guard, before dislocating his wrist in a game against the [[2012 Oakland Raiders season|Oakland Raiders]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2012/12/24/3802002/nfl-injury-report-nfc-south-week-16|title=NFC South injury report: Jonathan Stewart questionable for Week 17|last=Sherman|first=Rodger|date=December 25, 2012|access-date=July 23, 2016}}</ref> For his solid rookie season he was named to ''[[Pro Football Weekly|Pro Football Weekly′s]]'' 2012 All-Rookie team.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballfocus.com/2012-pff-all-rookie-team/|title=2012 PFF All-Rookie Team|website=profootballfocus.com|date=January 15, 2013|access-date=July 24, 2016}}</ref> On October 16, 2013, Silatolu was placed on injured reserve for a torn right ACL.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nfl/2013/10/7/4813570/amini-silatolu-panthers-torn-acl|title=Panthers OL Amini Silatolu out for year with torn ACL|last=Dator|first=James|date=October 7, 2013|access-date=July 24, 2016}}</ref> On November 25, 2015, he was placed on injured reserve for a torn left ACL.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/silatolu-out-for-season-norwell-set-to-return-16357583|title=Silatolu out for season; Norwell set to return|last=Strickland|first=Bryan|date=November 23, 2015|website=Carolina Panthers|access-date=July 24, 2016}}</ref>

On February 7, 2016, Silatolu's Panthers played in [[Super Bowl 50]]. In the game, the Panthers fell to the [[2015 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]] by a score of 24–10.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201602070den.htm|title=Super Bowl 50 - Denver Broncos vs. Carolina Panthers - February 7th, 2016|work=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|access-date=August 7, 2017}}</ref>

===Chicago Bears===
On July 20, 2016, Silatolu signed with the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web|work=NFL.com|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/guard-amini-silatolu-signs-with-chicago-bears-0ap3000000675769|title=Guard Amini Silatolu signs with Chicago Bears|first=Tyler|last=Dragon|date=July 20, 2016|access-date=July 20, 2016}}</ref>
On September 5, 2016, he was released by the Bears.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bears swap out long snappers, cut Amini Silatolu|url=http://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2016/09/05/bears-swap-out-long-snappers-cut-amini-silatolu/|author=Alper, Josh|website=ProFootballTalk.NBCSports.com|date=September 5, 2016}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers (second stint)===
On February 17, 2017, Silatolu signed a one-year contract with the Panthers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henson |first=Max |date=February 17, 2017 |title=Panthers sign Amini Silatolu |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-sign-amini-silatolu-18569461 |access-date=2024-08-03 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> He played in 14 games with three starts for the Panthers in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amini Silatolu 2017 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/SilaAm00/gamelog/2017/ |access-date=2024-12-26 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

On March 26, 2018, Silatolu re-signed with the Panthers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Henson |first=Max |date=March 26, 2018 |title=Panthers re-sign Amini Silatolu |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-re-sign-amini-silatolu-20488562 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> On August 7, 2018, Silatolu suffered a torn meniscus in his left knee which required surgery.<ref>{{cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=August 7, 2018 |title=Amini Silatolu tears meniscus in left knee |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2018/08/07/amini-silatolu-tears-meniscus-in-left-knee/ |access-date=April 19, 2026 |work=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref> On December 7, Silatolu was placed on injured reserve with a knee injury.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers sign kicker Chandler Catanzaro, Amini Silatolu to Injured Reserve|url=https://www.catscratchreader.com/2018/12/7/18130693/panthers-sign-kicker-chandler-catanzaro-graham-gano-amini-silatolu-injured-reserve|author=Walker, Clement|work=Cat Scratch Reader|publisher=SB Nation|date=December 7, 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Silatolu is of [[Tongan American|Tongan descent]]; his parents, Saia and Lupe Silatolu, immigrated from [[Tonga]] to the [[San Francisco Bay Area]] in 1985, where Amini was born and raised.<ref name=SilatoluHunger/><ref name="Paves to the Pros">{{cite news|url=http://www.charlotteobserver.com/2012/05/05/3219838/carolina-panthers-blocker-amini.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130119052835/http://www.charlotteobserver.com/2012/05/05/3219838/carolina-panthers-blocker-amini.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 19, 2013 |title=Carolina Panthers blocker Amini Silatolu paves path to pros |newspaper=Charlotte Observer |date=May 5, 2012 |first=Joseph |last=Person }}</ref> His younger brother Paul Silatolu, a Naval petty officer, served on board the [[USS New York (LPD-21)|USS ''New York'']].<ref name="Paves to the Pros" />

'''Amari Cooper''' (born June 17, 1994) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] who played 10 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama Crimson Tide]], winning the [[Biletnikoff Award]] as the nation's top receiver and earning [[unanimous All-American]] honors in 2014. Cooper was selected by the [[Oakland Raiders]] in the first round (fourth overall) of the [[2015 NFL draft]].

After successful rookie and sophomore seasons that included back-to-back 1,000-yard campaigns and two [[Pro Bowl]] appearances, Cooper struggled in his third season with the Raiders, totaling just 680 yards. Midway through the [[2018 NFL season|2018 season]], Cooper was traded to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] and his play began to flourish again, including a 217-yard performance, and as a result, he was voted to the third Pro Bowl of his career. Cooper also had successive 1,000-yard seasons in 2019 and 2020, making the Pro Bowl in 2019. In 2022, he was traded to the [[Cleveland Browns]]. Cooper had 1,000-yard seasons in 2022 and 2023, becoming the first Browns wide receiver in team history with multiple 1,000-yard seasons.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/amari-cooper-becomes-first-browns-wr-to-record-multiple-1-000-yard-seasons-browns-lead-7-0 |title=Amari Cooper becomes first Browns WR to record multiple 1,000-yard seasons, Browns lead 7–0 |work=NBC Sports |last=Simmons |first=Myles |date=December 24, 2023 |access-date=January 2, 2024}}</ref> He was traded to the [[Buffalo Bills]] midway through the 2024 season, spending one season with the team before retiring in 2025.

==Early life==
Cooper was born on June 17, 1994, in [[Miami, Florida]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Cooper Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoopAm00.htm |access-date=September 11, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="x994">{{cite web | last=Fisher | first=Mike | title=Dolphins at Dallas: Amari Cooper leads his boyhood team against his 'Boys | website=SI.com | date=September 22, 2019 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/cowboys/news/dolphins-at-dallas-amari-cooper-leads-his-boyhood-team-against-his-boys | access-date=September 11, 2024}}</ref> where he attended [[Miami Northwestern Senior High School]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rankin |first=Duane |date=September 26, 2014 |title=Bridgewater impressed with prep teammate Cooper's play at Alabama |url=http://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/alabama/2014/09/26/bridgewater-impressed-with-prep-teammate-coopers-play-at-alabama/16268101/ |access-date=January 3, 2018 |work=The Montgomery Advertiser |archive-date=March 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150324201045/http://www.montgomeryadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/alabama/2014/09/26/bridgewater-impressed-with-prep-teammate-coopers-play-at-alabama/16268101/ |url-status=live }}</ref> As a junior, Cooper missed much of the season with an injury, but still managed to be one of quarterback [[Teddy Bridgewater]]'s primary targets and had 16 [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] for 175 yards and four [[touchdowns]]. Cooper was dominant on the 7-on-7 circuit at various college campuses before his senior season. Cooper had a show-out performance at [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama's]] summer camp,<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 21, 2016 |title=Why elite receivers from south Fla. keep ending up at Alabama |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2016/why-elite-receivers-from-south-fla-keep-ending-up-at-alabama |access-date=September 12, 2021 |work=USA Today High School Sports |archive-date=February 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190205151237/https://usatodayhss.com/2016/why-elite-receivers-from-south-fla-keep-ending-up-at-alabama |url-status=live }}</ref> and that quickly led to an offer from [[Nick Saban]] and the Crimson Tide. As a senior, Cooper had in 33 receptions for 722 yards and six touchdowns. He was a first-team [[Florida High School Athletic Association|FHSAA]] 8A All-State selection, as well as the number-four player on ''[[Orlando Sentinel]]''{{'}}s Florida Top 100.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Potter |first=Charlie |date=September 24, 2014 |title=Road to Stardom: Amari Cooper |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/article/road-to-stardom-amari-cooper-31437959/ |access-date=September 12, 2021 |website=24/7 Sports |archive-date=September 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903160236/https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/Road-to-Stardom-Amari-Cooper-31437959/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Cooper was invited to play at the [[Under Armour All-America Game|2012 Under Armour All-America Game]], where he had a 75-yard touchdown reception and a 93-yard [[punt return]] for a score. ====2016 season====
Cooper put together a solid second season in the NFL. During the season opener against the [[New Orleans Saints]], he had six receptions for 137 yards in a narrow 35–34 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at New Orleans Saints – September 11th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110nor.htm |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=January 3, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180103194930/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201609110nor.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> During Week 5 against the [[San Diego Chargers]], he had six receptions for 138 yards and a touchdown in a 34–31 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Diego Chargers at Oakland Raiders – October 9th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610090rai.htm |access-date=January 3, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=September 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903160513/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610090rai.htm |url-status=live }}</ref> Three weeks later against the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]], he had his best game of the season with 12 receptions for 173 yards and a touchdown in a 30–24 overtime road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Oakland Raiders at Tampa Bay Buccaneers - October 30th, 2016 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201610300tam.htm |access-date=September 5, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Cooper finished his second professional season with 83 receptions for 1,153 yards and five touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Engelage |first=Christopher |date=May 22, 2017 |title=Raiders WR Amari Cooper has been historic in first two seasons |url=http://raiderswire.usatoday.com/2017/05/22/raiders-wr-amari-cooper-has-been-historic-in-first-two-seasons/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903160518/https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/2017/05/22/raiders-wr-amari-cooper-has-been-historic-in-first-two-seasons/ |archive-date=September 3, 2022 |access-date=June 13, 2017 |website=Raiders Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He was named to his second consecutive Pro Bowl on December 20, 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 20, 2016 |title=NFL announces 2017 Pro Bowl rosters |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/nfl-announces-2017-pro-bowl-rosters-0ap3000000760503 |website=NFL.com |access-date=December 26, 2016 |archive-date=November 17, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181117075658/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000760503/article/nfl-announces-2017-pro-bowl-rosters |url-status=live }}</ref> Cooper was also ranked 53rd by his peers on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2017]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2017-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=May 11, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220511024213/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2017-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
====2018 season====
On October 22, 2018, Cooper was traded to the [[Dallas Cowboys]] in exchange for a first-round pick (27th overall, [[Johnathan Abram]]) in the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archer |first=Todd |date=October 22, 2018 |title=Oakland Raiders to trade Amari Cooper to Dallas Cowboys |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/25055195/oakland-raiders-trade-amari-cooper-dallas-cowboys |access-date=October 22, 2018 |website=[[ESPN]] |archive-date=October 22, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181022232703/http://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/25055195/oakland-raiders-trade-amari-cooper-dallas-cowboys |url-status=live }}</ref>

In his first game with the Cowboys on November 5, Cooper led the team with five receptions for 58 yards and a touchdown as the Cowboys lost to the Titans by a score of 28–14.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 6, 2018 |title=Titans top Cowboys 28–14 in Amari Cooper's Dallas debut |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/raiders-nfl/titans-top-cowboys-28-14-in-amari-coopers-dallas-debut-1520145/ |access-date=May 1, 2019 |website=Las Vegas Review-Journal |language=en-US |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=May 1, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190501193202/https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/raiders-nfl/titans-top-cowboys-28-14-in-amari-coopers-dallas-debut-1520145/ |url-status=live }}</ref> On [[NFL on Thanksgiving Day|Thanksgiving]], Cooper had eight receptions for 180 yards and two touchdowns, including a 90-yard touchdown catch in the third quarter as the Cowboys defeated the [[Washington Redskins]] by a score of 31–23. He was named the NFC Offensive Player of the Week for his performance.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 28, 2018 |title=Philip Rivers, Amari Cooper among Players of the Week |url=http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000993457/article/philip-rivers-amari-cooper-among-players-of-the-week |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=December 31, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231021240/https://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000993457/article/philip-rivers-amari-cooper-among-players-of-the-week |url-status=dead }}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], Cooper had 10 receptions for a career-high 217 yards and three touchdowns. His final touchdown, in overtime, came off a deflection from [[Rasul Douglas]] as the Cowboys won 29–23. Cooper's 217 receiving yards were the most by one player for a single game in the 2018 season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Most receiving yards, single game, 2018 season |url=http://pfref.com/tiny/7GJvv |access-date=March 1, 2019 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=September 3, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220903160521/https://stathead.com/tools/tiny.fcgi?id=7GJvv |url-status=live }}</ref> For his performance, Cooper earned his second NFC Offensive Player of the Week award.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Knoblauch |first=Austin |date=December 12, 2018 |title=Derrick Henry, Amari Cooper among NFL Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/derrick-henry-amari-cooper-among-nfl-players-of-the-week-0ap3000000998979 |access-date=March 16, 2019 |website=NFL.com |archive-date=December 13, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181213091413/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000998979/article/derrick-henry-amari-cooper-among-nfl-players-of-the-week |url-status=live }}</ref>

During the season opener against the [[New York Giants]], Cooper had six receptions for 106 yards and a touchdown in the 35–17 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 8, 2019 |title=Prescott lightens Elliott's load as Cowboys top Giants 35–17 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128007 |access-date=September 8, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=September 9, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190909070154/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128007 |url-status=live }}</ref> During Week 5, Cooper caught 11 passes for a career-high 226 yards and a touchdown as the Cowboys lost to the [[Green Bay Packers]] by a score of 34–24.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 6, 2019 |title=Rodgers, Packers rule at home of Cowboys again in 34–24 win |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128029 |access-date=October 6, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=October 8, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191008032614/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128029 |url-status=live }}</ref> During Week 10 against the [[Minnesota Vikings]] on [[NBC Sunday Night Football|''Sunday Night Football'']], he recorded 11 receptions for 147 yards and a touchdown in the 28–24 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 10, 2019 |title=Cook leads Vikings to 28–24 primetime road win over Cowboys |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128041 |access-date=November 10, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=March 16, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210316014219/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401128041 |url-status=dead }}</ref> During Week 14 against the [[Chicago Bears]] on ''Thursday Night Football'', Cooper had six receptions for 83 yards and a touchdown in the 31–24 road loss. During the game, he reached 1,000 receiving yards on the season.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 5, 2019 |title=Mitchell Trubisky helps Bears beat Cowboys 31–24 |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127871 |access-date=December 5, 2019 |website=ESPN.com |agency=Associated Press |archive-date=January 8, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210108032706/https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401127871 |url-status=live }}</ref> Cooper was named to his fourth career Pro Bowl for his performance in 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2019/probowl.htm |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=June 27, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220627030242/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2019/probowl.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

Cooper finished the 2019 season with 79 receptions for a career-high 1,189 yards and eight touchdowns in 16 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Cooper 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoopAm00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=January 30, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was ranked 49th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2020]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2020-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=April 8, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220408124719/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2020-nfl-top-100.htm |url-status=live }}</ref>

====2020 season====
On March 17, 2020, Cooper signed a five-year contract extension with the Cowboys worth $100 million, which featured $60 million guaranteed, $40 million at signing, and a $20 million injury designation that becomes fully guaranteed in 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Helman |first=David |date=March 17, 2020 |title=Cooper Agrees To Terms on $100 Million Deal |url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cooper-agrees-to-terms-on-100-million-deal |access-date=March 17, 2020 |website=DallasCowboys.com |archive-date=March 18, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200318030105/https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/cooper-agrees-to-terms-on-100-million-deal |url-status=live }}</ref>

The 2020 season saw Cooper reach at least 100 receiving yards in four games. Despite having four quarterbacks start over the season due to injuries, Cooper finished the season with a career-high 92 receptions for 1,114 yards and five touchdowns in 16 games and 15 starts.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walker |first=Patrik |date=November 5, 2020 |title=Cowboys' Ezekiel Elliott reacts to fourth starting QB in 2020, shrugs off individual stats: 'We need a win' |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/cowboys-ezekiel-elliott-reacts-to-fourth-starting-qb-in-2020-shrugs-off-individual-stats-we-need-a-win/ |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en |archive-date=October 26, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211026095959/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/cowboys-ezekiel-elliott-reacts-to-fourth-starting-qb-in-2020-shrugs-off-individual-stats-we-need-a-win/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2020 Dallas Cowboys Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/dal/2020.htm |access-date=September 2, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=August 6, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220806182740/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/dal/2020.htm |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Cooper 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoopAm00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=September 12, 2021 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |archive-date=September 12, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210912150751/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoopAm00/gamelog/2020/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Cleveland Browns===
====2022 season====
On March 16, 2022, Cooper was traded to the [[Cleveland Browns]] in exchange for a fifth-round pick (#155-[[Matt Waletzko]]) and a swap of sixth-round picks in the [[2022 NFL draft]].<ref name="Poisal">{{Cite web |last=Poisal |first=Anthony |date=March 16, 2022 |title=Browns acquire WR Amari Cooper in trade with Cowboys |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-acquire-wr-amari-cooper-in-trade-with-cowboys |access-date=March 16, 2022 |website=Cleveland Browns |archive-date=March 16, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220316202144/https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-acquire-wr-amari-cooper-in-trade-with-cowboys |url-status=live }}</ref>

During Week 11 against the Bills, Cooper recorded eight receptions for 113 yards and two touchdowns in the 31–23 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Buffalo Bills – November 20th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202211200buf.htm |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During Week 17 against the Commanders, he had three receptions for 105 yards and two touchdowns in the 24–10 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cleveland Browns at Washington Commanders – January 1st, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202301010was.htm |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Cooper finished the 2022 season with 78 receptions for 1,160 yards and a career-high nine touchdowns in 17 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Cooper 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoopAm00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2023 season====
[[File:Amari Cooper (53142413151).jpg|thumb|upright=0.7|Cooper in 2023]]
On December 24, 2023, Cooper had 11 receptions for a career-high 265 yards in a 36–22 victory over the [[Houston Texans]], which also broke the Browns single-game receiving record previously held by [[Josh Gordon]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trotter |first=Jake |author-link=Jake Trotter |date=December 24, 2023 |title='Savant' Cooper bags Browns receiving record |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/39179285 |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> Furthermore, Cooper became just the second player in NFL history to record a 200+ yard game for three different teams, along with Terrell Owens.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Werner |first=Barry |date=December 24, 2023 |title=Amari Cooper joins Terrell Owens in elite receiver company |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/2023/12/24/amari-cooper-joins-terrell-owens-in-elite-receiver-company/72025452007/ |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> Cooper was named AFC Offensive Player of the Week for his historic game against the Texans.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Week 16 Leaders & Scores |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/week_16.htm |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Cooper was also named as a Pro Bowler for the fifth time.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/probowl.htm |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Cooper finished the 2023 season with 72 receptions for a career-high 1,250 yards and five touchdowns in 15 games and starts. He had five games with over 100 receiving yards on the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Cooper 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoopAm00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=February 11, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Cooper became the first wide receiver to record consecutive 1,000-yard seasons for the Browns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Louallen |first=Doc |date=December 24, 2023 |title=WR Amari Cooper becomes first Browns receiver to break the 1,000-receiving yard mark in consecutive seasons |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/amari-cooper-back-to-back-1000-receiving-yard-seasons-first-browns-player |access-date=May 31, 2024 |website=ClevelandBrowns.com |language=en-US}}</ref> He was ranked 70th by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2024]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2024-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=September 26, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

====2024 season====
In six games with the Browns, Cooper struggled to connect with quarterback [[Deshaun Watson]] as the Browns started the season with a 1–5 record.<ref>{{cite news |last=Barnwell |first=Bill |author-link=Bill Barnwell |date=October 14, 2024 |title=It's time for the Browns to bench Deshaun Watson: Here's why |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41778436/browns-bench-deshaun-watson-poor-qb-play-contract-future-cut |access-date=October 16, 2024 |work=ESPN}}</ref> Cooper caught 24 of 53 targets for 250 yards and two touchdowns, both of which came in a Week 3 loss to the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Davis |first=Nate |title=Amari Cooper trade grades: Did Bills or Browns ace deal for standout receiver? |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/columnist/nate-davis/2024/10/15/amari-cooper-trade-grades-bills-browns-deshaun-watson/75690958007/ |access-date=October 16, 2024 |work=USA Today |date=October 15, 2024}}</ref>

===Buffalo Bills===
On October 15, 2024, the Browns traded Cooper and a 2025 sixth-round pick to the [[Buffalo Bills]] in exchange for a 2025 third-round pick and a 2026 seventh-round pick.<ref>{{cite news |title=Browns trade Amari Cooper to Bills |url=https://www.clevelandbrowns.com/news/browns-trade-amari-cooper-to-bills |access-date=October 15, 2024 |work=ClevelandBrowns.com |date=October 15, 2024}}</ref>

Cooper was able to suit up for the Week 7 matchup against the Titans, catching four passes for 66 yards and a touchdown in his Bills debut as the Bills won 34–10.<ref>{{cite news |last=Getzenberg |first=Alaina |title=Amari Cooper stars in debut as Buffalo Bills roll at home |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/41911952/amari-cooper-stars-debut-buffalo-bills-roll-home |access-date=October 21, 2024 |work=ESPN |date=October 20, 2024}}</ref> He missed Weeks 9 and 10 with a wrist injury.<ref>{{cite news |last=Gonzales |first=Christian |title=Bills WR Amari Cooper (wrist) active vs. Chiefs |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/bills-wr-amari-cooper-wrist-active-vs-chiefs |access-date=November 18, 2024 |work=NFL.com |date=November 17, 2024}}</ref> During a Week 13 victory over the [[San Francisco 49ers]], Cooper received a pass from quarterback [[Josh Allen]] and lateraled the ball back to Allen for a touchdown, giving Allen both a passing touchdown and receiving touchdown on the same play.<ref>{{cite news |last=Owens |first=Jason |title=Bills' Josh Allen throws and catches TD on same play for spectacular snow-game score like you've never seen |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/bills-josh-allen-throws-and-catches-td-on-same-play-for-spectacular-snow-game-score-like-youve-never-seen-035159208.html |access-date=December 2, 2024 |work=Yahoo Sports |date=December 1, 2024}}</ref>

Cooper finished the 2024 season with 44 receptions for 547 yards and four touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Cooper 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CoopAm00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=January 22, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===Las Vegas Raiders===
On August 25, 2025, Cooper signed a one-year, $3.5 million contract with the [[Las Vegas Raiders]], reuniting him with the team that drafted him.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Gordon |first1=Grant |date=August 25, 2025 |title=WR Amari Cooper returning to Raiders, who drafted him in 2015 first round, on one-year deal |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/wr-amari-cooper-returning-to-raiders-on-one-year-deal |access-date=August 26, 2025 |website=NFL}}</ref>

On September 4, 2025, Cooper announced his retirement from the NFL after 10 seasons.<ref>{{cite web | last=Shook | first=Nick | title=Five-time Pro Bowl WR Amari Cooper to retire from NFL one week after Raiders reunion | website=NFL.com | date=September 4, 2025 | url=https://www.nfl.com/news/five-time-pro-bowl-amari-cooper-to-retire-from-nfl-after-raiders-reunion | access-date=February 2, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McFadden |first=Ryan |date=September 4, 2025 |title=WR Cooper informs Raiders he's retiring from NFL |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/46157479/source-amari-cooper-tells-raiders-retiring-nfl |access-date=September 5, 2025 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Cooper is an avid [[chess]] player. He was first captivated by the game as an elementary school student in northwest Miami, and as a football player, Cooper related chess strategies to his play on the field.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roy |first=Tory Z. |date=August 29, 2020 |title=The source of Cowboys wide receiver Amari Cooper's deception: chess |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/29745212/the-source-cowboys-wide-receiver-amari-cooper-deception-chess |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=ESPN.com |language=en |archive-date=July 5, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220705211700/https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/29745212/the-source-cowboys-wide-receiver-amari-cooper-deception-chess |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Spurr |first=AJ |date=June 13, 2021 |title=Amari Cooper demolishes rookie in chess after being challenged |url=https://rolltidewire.usatoday.com/2021/06/13/dallas-cowboys-amari-cooper-defeats-rookie-micah-parsons-in-game-of-chess/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211017181849/https://rolltidewire.usatoday.com/2021/06/13/dallas-cowboys-amari-cooper-defeats-rookie-micah-parsons-in-game-of-chess/ |archive-date=October 17, 2021 |access-date=July 5, 2022 |website=Roll Tide Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> Cooper played in [[Chess.com]]'s BlitzChamps, a [[Fast chess|rapid]] tournament for NFL players, and came in second place behind [[Chidobe Awuzie]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodgers |first=Jack |date=July 11, 2022 |title=Chidobe Awuzie Takes Revenge On Amari Cooper, Wins BlitzChamps 2022 |url=https://www.chess.com/news/view/2022-blitzchamps-awuzie-wins |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220718205005/https://www.chess.com/news/view/2022-blitzchamps-awuzie-wins |archive-date=July 18, 2022 |access-date=July 18, 2022 |website=Chess.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

|first=Drew |date=October 10, 2014 |title=Homewood band spells 'Fear Ameer' honoring alum and Nebraska star Ameer Abdullah 2010 Mississippi-Alabama All-Star Classic, he scored the winning touchdown in overtime.{{Cite web |last=Suttles |first=Aaron |date=December 11, 2010 |title=UA commits shine at Classic |url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/2010/12/12/ua-commits-shine-at-classic/28364039007/ |access-date=October 14, 2022 |work=The Tuscaloosa News}} Also a track star at Homewood, he ran a career-best time of 11.15 seconds in the [[100 meters]] at the 2011 AHSAA 6A Section 3 Championships, placing 7th in the prelims. He also competed in the [[long jump]]; he had a career-best leap of 6.60 meters.{{Cite web |title=Ameer Abdullah – Feed |url=https://al.milesplit.com/athletes/1294725-ameer-abdullah/feed |access-date=October 14, 2022 |work=AlabamaRunners}} ==College career== ===College decision=== Abdullah was offered football scholarships from several schools, but schools such as [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|Alabama]] and [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn]] wanted him to play [[cornerback]], while he wanted to be a [[running back]].{{Cite magazine |last=Hamilton |first=Brian |date=November 16, 2012 |title=Overlooked for his size, Alabama Abdullah proving his critics wrong |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/brian_hamilton/11/16/ameer-abdullah-nebraska/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140111191433/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/writers/brian_hamilton/11/16/ameer-abdullah-nebraska/ |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 11, 2014 |access-date=January 11, 2014 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} Nebraska coach [[Bo Pelini]], however, while making no guarantees, told him that they would put him in a position that would maximize his talent. Pelini's view was the critical factor in Abdullah choosing Nebraska. ===2011=== Abdullah was one of six [[true freshman]] to play for Nebraska in the 2011 season. His best game was against [[Fresno State Bulldogs football|Fresno State]] when he had 228 return yards. He had 211 [[kickoff return]] yards including a 100-yard touchdown return.{{Cite web |title=Fresno State at Nebraska Box Score, September 10, 2011 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-09-10-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} Abdullah's total kickoff return yards broke the previous Nebraska record. His best running total was 36 yards and his longest run was 24 yards, both against the [[Wyoming Cowboys football|Wyoming Cowboys]].{{Cite web |title=Nebraska at Wyoming Box Score, September 24, 2011 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-09-24-wyoming.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} On November 12, against Penn State, he had his first collegiate rushing touchdown.{{Cite web |title=Nebraska at Penn State Box Score, November 12, 2011 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2011-11-12-penn-state.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} Overall, in the 2011 season, he finished with 150 rushing yards, three rushing touchdowns, 26 kick returns for 763 net yards and a touchdown, and 15 punt returns for 107 net yards.{{Cite web |title=Ameer Abdullah 2011 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/ameer-abdullah-1/gamelog/2011/ |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} ===2012=== After [[Rex Burkhead]] was injured, Abdullah started seven games. His first start was against [[UCLA Bruins football|UCLA]] and he rushed for 119 yards with two touchdowns.{{Cite web |title=Nebraska at UCLA Box Score, September 8, 2012 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-09-08-ucla.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} His longest run was for 45 yards against [[Arkansas State Red Wolves football|Arkansas State]] in a 167-yard and two-touchdown performance.{{Cite web |title=Arkansas State at Nebraska Box Score, September 15, 2012 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-09-15-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} In the next game against Idaho State, he had a punt return touchdown.{{Cite web |title=Idaho State at Nebraska Box Score, September 22, 2012 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-09-22-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} He had 252 all-purpose yards against [[Wisconsin Badgers football|Wisconsin]], which included five kickoffs totaling 142 yards, 10 rushes for 70 yards, and 22 yards receiving.{{Cite web |title=Wisconsin at Nebraska Box Score, September 29, 2012 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-09-29-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} Against [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]], he rushed for 116 yards and 1,000 rushing yards for the first time in his college career.{{Cite web |title=Penn State at Nebraska Box Score, November 10, 2012 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2012-11-10-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} His per game average of 134.5 all-purpose yards ranked fourth in the [[Big Ten Conference]] and his per game average of 81.2 rushing yards ranked ninth. Overall, he finished the 2012 season with 1,137 rushing yards, eight rushing touchdowns, 24 receptions, 178 receiving yards, two receiving touchdowns, and a punt return touchdown.{{Cite web |title=Ameer Abdullah 2012 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/ameer-abdullah-1/gamelog/2012/ |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} ===2013=== Abdullah rushed for over 100 yards in 11 of 13 games (including the [[Gator Bowl]]). The ten 100-yard games during the regular season placed him fourth in Nebraska school history. On August 31, he started the season with 114 rushing yards against Wyoming.{{Cite web |title=Wyoming at Nebraska Box Score, August 31, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-08-31-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} In the next game against Southern Miss, he had 114 rushing yards and two rushing touchdowns.{{Cite web |title=Southern Mississippi at Nebraska Box Score, September 7, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-07-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} After going for 98 yards against UCLA, he had 139 rushing yards and a touchdown against South Dakota State.{{Cite web |title=UCLA at Nebraska Box Score, September 14, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-14-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}}{{Cite web |title=South Dakota State at Nebraska Box Score, September 21, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-09-21-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} He achieved a career-high rushing against [[Illinois Fighting Illini football|Illinois]] of 225 yards.{{Cite web |title=Illinois at Nebraska Box Score, October 5, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-05-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} He followed that up with 126 rushing yards and a touchdown in the game against Purdue.{{Cite web |title=Nebraska at Purdue Box Score, October 12, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-12-purdue.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} In the next game, at Minnesota, he had 165 rushing yards.{{Cite web |title=Nebraska at Minnesota Box Score, October 26, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-10-26-minnesota.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} On November 9, against Michigan, he had 105 rushing yards, one rushing touchdown, and a receiving touchdown in the victory.{{Cite web |title=Nebraska at Michigan Box Score, November 9, 2013 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2013-11-09-michigan.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} In the next game, against Michigan State, he had 123 rushing average of 130.7 yards per game, which ranked him second in the Big Ten and seventh nationally. He had 232 yards in pass receptions and averaged 154.9 all-purpose yards per game, which also ranked him second in the Big Ten. He was placed on the All-Big Ten first-team by both the conference's coaches and media. He was a semifinalist for the [[Doak Walker Award]]. He finished the season with 122 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown victory over Georgia in the Gator Bowl.{{Cite web |title=Gator Bowl – Nebraska vs Georgia Box Score, January 1, 2014 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2014-01-01-georgia.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} Overall, in the 2013 season, he finished with 1,690 rushing yards, nine rushing touchdowns, 26 receptions, 232 receiving yards, and two receiving touchdowns.{{Cite web |title=Ameer Abdullah 2013 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/ameer-abdullah-1/gamelog/2013/ |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} After the Gator Bowl, Abdullah considered whether he should enter the [[2014 NFL draft]] as an underclassman.{{Cite news |last=Sipple |first=Steven M. |date=January 6, 2014 |title=Abdullah could enhance already splendid legacy |url=http://journalstar.com/sports/columnists/sipple/steven-m-sipple-abdullah-could-enhance-already-splendid-legacy/article_a9a7eb2f-c446-502b-bbd3-a3adcc66de23.html |access-date=January 11, 2014 |work=JournalStar.com}} On January 9, 2014, he decided to stay at Nebraska for his senior season, stating that
I have come to realize that life is bigger than football ... and that my chances of long-term success in life will be greatly enhanced by completing my college education. ... If playing in the NFL is truly in God's plans for me, then God will again present this opportunity to me after I complete my college education.{{Cite news |last=Maisel |first=Ivan |author-link=Ivan Maisel |date=10 January 2014 |title=3-point stance: Franklin's future |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/ncfnation/post/_/id/92996/3-point-stance-franklins-future |access-date=11 January 2014 |work=ESPN}}
===2014=== [[File:Ameer Abdullah running north to south during the first quarter of the FAU game.png|thumb|right|Ameer Abdullah running at [[Memorial Stadium (Lincoln)|Memorial Stadium]] on August 30, 2014]] ''[[Sporting News]]'' listed Abdullah among their top 10 candidates for the Heisman trophy in 2014{{Cite news |date=December 14, 2013 |title=10 Spot: Heisman candidates for 2014 |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2013-12-14/10-spot-heisman-candidates-for-2014-jameis-winston-marcus-mariota-braxton-miller-tre-mason/slide/10 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140502002658/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2013-12-14/10-spot-heisman-candidates-for-2014-jameis-winston-marcus-mariota-braxton-miller-tre-mason/slide/10 |archive-date=May 2, 2014 |access-date=May 1, 2014 |work=Sporting News}} and they listed Abdullah as the number 4 returning running back.{{Cite news |last=Bradley |first=Ken |date=February 26, 2014 |title=SN's top RBs: Todd Gurley leads talented position into spring |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2014-02-25/top-running-backs-2014-todd-gurley-tj-yeldon-melvin-gordon-ameer-abdullah/slide/4 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140606121214/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2014-02-25/top-running-backs-2014-todd-gurley-tj-yeldon-melvin-gordon-ameer-abdullah/slide/4 |archive-date=June 6, 2014 |access-date=May 25, 2014 |work=[[Sporting News]]}} In late September 2014, Eric Galko and Ian Wharton of ''Sporting News'' analyzed his running attributes. They concluded that even though his 40-yard time is not below 4.4 second and he does not possess the most power when running, he is a complete running back. He runs very low, below the pad level of defenders, making him very difficult to tackle. Abdullah has great balance, vision to find holes and the patience to wait for his blockers to those open holes. These running characteristics together with his burst, shiftiness in space, and ability to keep his legs moving when hit, make him "the most well-rounded tailback in the country".{{Cite magazine |last1=Galko |first1=Eric |last2=Wharton |first2=Ian |date=September 26, 2014 |title=Nebraska's Ameer Abdullah looks like an NFL running back |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2014-09-26/ameer-abdullah-scouting-report-nfl-draft-nebraska-running-back-big-ten |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140928074622/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-football/story/2014-09-26/ameer-abdullah-scouting-report-nfl-draft-nebraska-running-back-big-ten |archive-date=September 28, 2014 |access-date=September 29, 2014 |magazine=[[Sporting News]]}} In early September 2014, Nebraska sent out [[AA battery|AA batteries]] to members of the sports news media and created a website for Abdullah to promote his Heisman campaign.{{Cite news |last=Bennett |first=Brian |date=September 12, 2013 |title=Abdullah's Heisman campaign gets charge |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/bigten/post/_/id/107251/abdullahs-heisman-campaign-gets-a-charge |access-date=September 14, 2014 |website=[[ESPN.com]]}} Abdullah and 2013 Heisman Trophy winner [[Jameis Winston]] trained together at the same gym in [[Birmingham, Alabama]].{{Cite web |date=September 22, 2014 |title=Abdullah: Winston must grow up |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/11570167/nebraska-ameer-abdullah-says-jameis-winston-grow-up |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140925030403/http://espn.go.com/college-football/story/_/id/11570167/nebraska-ameer-abdullah-says-jameis-winston-grow-up |archive-date=September 25, 2014 |access-date=September 22, 2014 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} In December 2014, Abdullah received the [[Senior CLASS Award]] for the most outstanding senior college football player in [[Division I (NCAA)|Division I]] based on classroom performance, community contributions, personal character, and athletic achievements. Players were selected based on votes from [[NCAA Division I Football Bowl Subdivision|FBS]] football coaches, media, and fans.{{Cite web |date=December 27, 2014 |title=Ameer Abdullah of Nebraska selected as the 2014 Senior CLASS Award winner for football |url=http://www.seniorclassaward.com/news/view/ameer_abdullah_of_nebraska_selected_as_the_2014_senior_class_award_winner_f/ |access-date=October 14, 2022 |work=[[Senior CLASS Award]]}} Abdullah ran for a career-high 232 rushing yards on 21 carries for an average of 11 yards per carry in a [[2014 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team#Florida Atlantic|55–7 win]] over [[2014 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team#Florida Atlantic|Florida Atlantic]]. His longest run was 47 yards for a touchdown. He also caught one pass for 9 yards.{{Cite web |title=Florida Atlantic at Nebraska Box Score, August 30, 2014 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2014-08-30-nebraska.html |access-date=February 23, 2018 |work=[[Sports Reference]]}} On September 1, he won Big Ten offensive player of the week.{{Cite news |date=September 1, 2014 |title=Ameer Abdullah wins Big Ten Player of the Week honors |url=http://www.omaha.com/huskers/blogs/ameer-abdullah-wins-big-ten-player-of-the-week-honors/article_56320df8-31eb-11e4-8a66-001a4bcf6878.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180702190211/https://www.omaha.com/huskers/blogs/ameer-abdullah-wins-big-ten-player-of-the-week-honors/article_56320df8-31eb-11e4-8a66-001a4bcf6878.html |archive-date=July 2, 2018 |access-date=September 1, 2014 |work=[[Omaha World Herald]]}} Abdullah ran for 67 yards on 17 carries for an average of 3.2 yards per carry in a [[2014 Nebraska Cornhuskers football team#McNeese State|31–24 win]] over the [[McNeese State Cowboys football|McNeese State Cowboys]].
