'''Alvin Moore''' (born May 3, 1959) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] for five seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with the [[Indianapolis Colts|Baltimore/Indianapolis Colts]], [[Detroit Lions]] and [[Seattle Seahawks]]. He was selected by the Colts in the seventh round of the [[1983 NFL draft]] after playing [[college football]] for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State Sun Devils]].

==Early life==
Alvin Moore was born on May 3, 1959, in [[Randolph, Arizona]].<ref name="Pfa">{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/m/moor01200.html | title=Alvin Moore | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=10 December 2024}}</ref> He attended [[Coolidge High School]] in [[Coolidge, Arizona]].<ref name="Pfa"/>

==College career==
Moore was a member of the [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State Sun Devils]] from 1978 to 1982.<ref name="Pfa"/> He [[letterman (sports)|lettered]] in 1978, 1979, 1981, and 1982.<ref name="Pfa"/> He rushed 94 times for 448 yards and two touchdowns while catching nine passes for 69 yards in 1978.<ref name="Sr">{{cite web | url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alvin-moore-1.html | title=Alvin Moore | publisher=sports-reference.com | accessdate=10 December 2024}}</ref> He also threw a 54-yard touchdown that season.<ref name="Sr"/> In 1979, Moore totaled 68 carries for 274 yards and a touchdown, and six receptions for 51 yards.<ref name="Sr"/> In 1981, he rushed 67 times for 343 yards, and one touchdown while catching five passes for 35	yards.<ref name="Sr"/> He recorded 85 rushing attempts for 348 yards and three touchdowns his senior year in 1982 while also catching 12 passes for 88 yards.<ref name="Sr"/>

==Professional career==
Moore was selected by the [[Baltimore Colts]] in the seventh round, with the 169th overall pick, of the [[1983 NFL draft]].<ref name="pfr"/> He was also a territorial selection of the [[Arizona Wranglers]] of the [[United States Football League]] in 1983.<ref name="Pfa"/> He officially signed with the Colts on May 22.<ref name="transactions"/> He played in 15 games for the Colts during his rookie year in 1983, rushing 57 times for 205 yards and one touchdown while catching six passes for 38	yards.<ref name="pfr"/> He played in 13 games, starting two, for the newly-renamed Indianapolis Colts in 1984, recording 38 carries for 127 yards and two touchdowns, and nine receptions for 52 yards.<ref name="pfr"/>

On July 25, 1985, Moore was traded to the [[Detroit Lions]] for [[Robbie Martin]].<ref name="transactions"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://prosportstransactions.com/football/Search/SearchResults.php?Player=Alvin+Moore&Team=&BeginDate=&EndDate=&PlayerMovementChkBx=yes&submit=Search | title=Search Results | publisher=prosportstransactions.com | accessdate=11 December 2024}}</ref> Moore appeared in all 16 games, starting five, for the Lions during the 1985 season, rushing 80 times for 221 yards and four touchdowns while catching 19 passes for 154 yards and one touchdown as well.<ref name="pfr"/> He also returned 13	kicks for 230 yards that season.<ref name="pfr"/> He was released by the Lions on October 25, 1986, re-signed on November 8, and placed on injured reserve on December 29, 1986.<ref name="transactions"/> Overall, he played in 13 games during the 1986 season, totaling 19 rushing attempts for 73 yards and eight receptions for 47 yards.<ref name="pfr"/> Moore was released by the Lions on September 9, 1987.<ref name="transactions"/>

Moore was signed by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] during the [[1987 NFL players strike]] and appeared in one game for the team that season, rushing three times for 15 yards.<ref name="pfr">{{cite web | url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/M/MoorAl00.htm | title=Alvin Moore | publisher=pro-football-reference.com | accessdate=11 December 2024}}</ref><ref name="transactions"/> He was released on October 19, 1987, after the strike ended.<ref name="transactions">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/m/moor01200.html | title=Alvin Moore NFL Transactions | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=11 December 2024}}</ref>

He played [[college football]] at [[Montclair State University]]. He also played in the [[Canadian Football League]] for the [[BC Lions]] and in the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) for the [[Tampa Bay Storm]], [[Massachusetts Marauders]], [[San Jose SaberCats]], [[Orlando Predators]], [[Connecticut Coyotes]], [[New York CityHawks]] and [[New Jersey Red Dogs]]. ==Early life== Amod Lloyd Field was born on October 11, 1967, in [[Passaic, New Jersey]].{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/players/f/fiel00100.html | title=AMOD FIELD | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He attended [[Passaic High School]] in Passaic. ==College career== Field was a member of the [[Montclair State Red Hawks football]] team from 1985 to 1989. He caught 108 passes for 1,941 yards and 24 touchdowns during his college career. He also participated in track and field at Montclair State. He won the outdoor [[NCAA Division III]] title in the [[400 meter hurdles]] twice and was a Division III track and field All-American eight times. Field played one year of basketball as well, leading the team in points per game with 15.4 and also averaging nearly five rebounds per game. He was inducted into the Montclair State Athletics Hall of Fame in 2000.{{cite web | access-date=January 2, 2015 | archive-date=January 2, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150102224613/http://montclairathletics.com/hof.aspx?hof=153&path=&kiosk= | url=http://montclairathletics.com/hof.aspx?hof=153&path=&kiosk= | title=Amod Field | publisher=montclairathletics.com | url-status=dead}} ==Professional career== After going undrafted in the [[1990 NFL draft]], Field signed with the [[Phoenix Cardinals]] on April 30, 1990. He was released on September 3, signed to the Cardinals' practice squad on October 2, released again on October 10, and signed to the practice squad again on October 16. He was promoted to the active roster on December 5, 1990, but did not appear in any games for the team during the 1990 season. Field became a free agent after the season and re-signed with the Cardinals. He was released on August 26, 1991, but re-signed the next day. He played in two games for the Cardinals during the 1991 season before being released on September 18, 1991.{{Cite web |title=Amod Field Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/F/FielAm20.htm |access-date=2025-08-29 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}} He was listed as a wide receiver while with the Cardinals. Field was signed by the [[San Diego Chargers]] on April 10, 1992. He was released on May 7, 1992.{{cite web | url=http://www.profootballarchives.com/transactions/f/fiel00100.html | title=Amod Field NFL Transactions | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He played in nine games for the [[BC Lions]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] in 1992, totaling three receptions for 55 yards, two interceptions, 33 kick returns for 672 yards, five punt returns for 25 yards, nine defensive tackles, and three special teams tackles. He was listed as a defensive back while with the Lions. Field appeared in three games for the [[Tampa Bay Storm]] of the [[Arena Football League]] (AFL) in 1993, catching seven passes for 122 yards and two touchdowns. On August 21, 1993, the Storm beat the [[Detroit Drive]] in [[ArenaBowl VII]].{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/1993arfltb.html | title=1993 Tampa Bay Storm (Arena) | publisher=profootballarchives.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He played in 11 games for the [[Massachusetts Marauders]] of the AFL in 1994, recording 30 receptions for 358 yards and two touchdowns, 23 solo tackles, six assisted tackles, two pass breakups, and one fumble recovery. He played both offense and defense during his time in the AFL as the league played under [[ironman rules]]. Field appeared in nine games for the AFL's [[San Jose SaberCats]] in 1995, accumulating 24 catches for 305 yards and eight touchdowns, 16 solo tackles, one assisted tackle, two interceptions, and two pass breakups. He earned second-team [[All-Arena]] honors that season as a wide receiver/defensive back.{{cite web | url=https://www.arenafan.com/players/?page=players&player=501&pageview=bio | title=Amod Field | publisher=arenafan.com | accessdate=23 December 2024}} He played in two games for the SaberCats during the 1996 season, catching nine passes for 101 yards and posting one solo tackle. He played in three games for the [[New York CityHawks]] of the AFL in 1997, totaling eight receptions for 106 yards and two touchdowns, three solo tackles, and two kick returns for 25 yards. '''Amarlo Herrera''' (born September 20, 1991) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[linebacker]] for the [[Indianapolis Colts]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]], and was selected by the Colts in the sixth round of the [[2015 NFL draft]]. He was also a member of the [[Tennessee Titans]] and [[Washington Redskins]].

==College career==
Herrera played at the [[University of Georgia]] from 2011 to 2014.<ref>[http://www.news-daily.com/news/2014/nov/28/amarlo-herrera-is-the-leader-on-the-georgia/ Amarlo Herrera is the leader on the Georgia Bulldogs defense]</ref><ref>[http://www.timesfreepress.com/news/sports/college/story/2014/sep/05/georgias-herrera-overlooked-no-more/266338/ Georgia's Herrera overlooked no more]</ref><ref>[http://onlineathens.com/sports/college-sports/2014-11-21/georgia-lb-herrera-hits-hard-has-soft-demeanor-field Georgia LB Herrera hits hard, has a soft demeanor off the field]</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2013/06/27/2561587/herrera-is-aiming-to-be-a-big.html |title=Georgia's Amarlo Herrera is aiming to be 'a big-time playmaker' |access-date=May 6, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130701004315/http://www.ledger-enquirer.com/2013/06/27/2561587/herrera-is-aiming-to-be-a-big.html |archive-date=July 1, 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> During his career he started 43 of 54 games and recorded 334 [[Tackle (football move)#Gridiron football|tackles]], 3.5 [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] and three [[interceptions]].<ref>[http://www.news-daily.com/news/2015/jan/16/amarlo-herrera-looks-to-impress-nfl-scouts-in/ Amarlo Herrera looks to impress NFL scouts in East-West Shrine Game]</ref>

==Professional career==
===Indianapolis Colts===
Herrera was selected by the [[Indianapolis Colts]] in the sixth round (207th overall) of the [[2015 NFL draft]].<ref>[http://www.ajc.com/news/sports/college/colts-select-amarlo-herrera-in-sixth-round/nk7sS/ Colts select Amarlo Herrera in sixth round]</ref><ref>[http://www.news-daily.com/news/2015/may/04/former-north-clayton-and-uga-linebacker-herrera/ Former North Clayton and UGA linebacker Herrera drafted by the Indianapolis Colts]</ref> He agreed to terms with the Colts on May 6.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.colts.com/2015/05/06/indianapolis-colts-agree-to-terms-with-five-draft-picks/|title=Indianapolis Colts agree to terms with five draft picks|work=blogs.colts.com|date=May 6, 2015|accessdate=May 6, 2015|archive-date=May 12, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150512020906/http://blogs.colts.com/2015/05/06/indianapolis-colts-agree-to-terms-with-five-draft-picks/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Herrera spent the first 5 weeks of the 2015 season on the [[practice squad]], and was elevated to the 53-man roster for Week 6. He was waived on October 20,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.colts.com/2015/10/20/indianapolis-colts-make-roster-moves-116/|title=Indianapolis Colts make roster moves|work=colts.com|date=October 20, 2015|accessdate=October 21, 2015|archive-date=October 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151021201014/http://blogs.colts.com/2015/10/20/indianapolis-colts-make-roster-moves-116/|url-status=dead}}</ref> and signed to the practice squad the following day.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.colts.com/2015/10/21/indianapolis-colts-make-practice-squad-move-4/|title=Indianapolis Colts make practice squad move|work=colts.com|date=October 21, 2015|accessdate=October 21, 2015}}</ref> On December 15, 2015, Herrera was waived by the Colts.<ref>{{Cite web|title = Andy Studebaker Signed by Colts|url = https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2599457-andy-studebaker-signed-by-colts-todd-herremans-amarlo-herrera-waived|website = Bleacher Report|access-date = December 17, 2015}}</ref> He was re-signed on December 29.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://blogs.colts.com/2015/12/29/indianapolis-colts-make-roster-moves-130/|title=Indianapolis Colts make roster moves|work=blogs.colts.com|date=December 29, 2015|accessdate=December 29, 2015|archive-date=December 30, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151230002420/http://blogs.colts.com/2015/12/29/indianapolis-colts-make-roster-moves-130/|url-status=dead}}</ref> 
On August 10, 2016, Herrera was released by the Colts.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts release 2015 sixth-round pick Amarlo Herrera|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/colts-release-2015-sixth-round-pick-amarlo-herrera-0ap3000000682581|last=Meyer|first=Max|website=NFL.com}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On August 12, 2016, Herrera was claimed off waivers by the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Claim LB Amarlo Herrera Off Waivers|url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Claim-LB-Amarlo-Herrera-Off-Waivers/f9cd7ec6-d44a-43fe-9da4-bf9b79c1bdb0|website=titansonline.com|accessdate=August 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160813134707/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Claim-LB-Amarlo-Herrera-Off-Waivers/f9cd7ec6-d44a-43fe-9da4-bf9b79c1bdb0|archive-date=August 13, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On August 28, 2016, Herrera was waived by the Titans.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Make First Round of Roster Cuts|url=http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Make-First-Round-of-Roster-Cuts/5cc39654-c023-4d06-9e37-336a50536431|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807022912/http://www.titansonline.com/news/article-4/Titans-Make-First-Round-of-Roster-Cuts/5cc39654-c023-4d06-9e37-336a50536431|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 7, 2017|website=TitansOnline.com|date=August 28, 2016}}</ref>

===Washington Redskins===
On September 19, 2016, Herrera was signed to the [[Washington Redskins]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Kedric Golston Placed On Injured Reserve, Matt Ioannidis On Active Roster|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Kedric-Golston-Placed-On-Injured-Reserve-Matt-Ioannidis-On-Active-Roster/1113255d-e6c2-4514-bd73-eb73b5842d6c|last=Czarda|first=Stephen|website=Redskins.com|access-date=September 19, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920132401/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Kedric-Golston-Placed-On-Injured-Reserve-Matt-Ioannidis-On-Active-Roster/1113255d-e6c2-4514-bd73-eb73b5842d6c|archive-date=September 20, 2016|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref> He was released from the Redskins' practice squad on September 27, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-John-Sullivan-Vinston-Painter-To-Active-Roster/5b4e7500-9bc3-4cf0-8b81-68ba592c72b2|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180425115143/http://www.redskins.com/news/article-1/Redskins-Sign-John-Sullivan-Vinston-Painter-To-Active-Roster/5b4e7500-9bc3-4cf0-8b81-68ba592c72b2|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 25, 2018|title=Redskins sign John Sullivan, Vinston Painter to active roster|work=Redskins.com|date=September 27, 2016|access-date=September 27, 2016}}</ref>

===WWE===
On June 17, 2017, it was reported on wwe.com that Herrera had attended a tryout for the [[WWE]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wwe.com/shows/wwenxt/article/wwe-performance-center-tryout-june-2017|title=CrossFit athletes, All-Americans, fighters and footballers attend WWE tryout|publisher=WWE|accessdate=June 18, 2017}}</ref>

'''Alvin Jerome Mitchell''' (born August 20, 1964) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[Fullback (American football)|fullback]] for one season with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]].

==Early life and college==
Alvin Jerome Mitchell was born on August 20, 1964, in [[Venice, Florida]].<ref name="pfa">{{cite web | url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/players/m/mitc01000.html | title=Alvin Mitchell | publisher=Pro Football Archives | accessdate=16 May 2025}}</ref> He attended [[Venice High School (Venice, Florida)|Venice High School]] in Venice.<ref name="pfa"/>

Mitchell played for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]] as a [[linebacker]], recording 121 career tackles.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1755&dat=19890901&id=tzUeAAAAIBAJ&sjid=Mb0EAAAAIBAJ&pg=3394,633314&hl=en | title=Buccaneers Release Venice's Mitchell | work=[[Sarasota Herald-Tribune]] | date=September 1, 1989 | access-date=October 23, 2015}}</ref> He was a four-year [[letterman (sports)|letterman]] from 1985 to 1988.<ref name="pfa"/>

==Professional career==
Mitchell signed with the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]] as a fullback on May 1, 1989, and spent the first eleven games of the [[1989 NFL season|1989 season]] on the practice squad.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.google.com/newspapers?nid=1755&dat=19890502&id=BDAeAAAAIBAJ&sjid=NL0EAAAAIBAJ&pg=6343,1595222&hl=en | title=Bucs Sign Venice's Mitchell | work=[[Sarasota Herald-Tribune]] | date=May 2, 1989 | access-date=October 23, 2015}}</ref><ref name="A">{{cite web|url=http://www.bucpower.com/alvin-mitchell.html |title=Alvin Mitchell |publisher=bucpower.com |access-date=October 23, 2015 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024000800/http://www.bucpower.com/alvin-mitchell.html |archive-date=October 24, 2015 }}</ref> He was then promoted to the active roster and played in the final five games of the season, catching one pass for 11 yards.<ref name="A"/> He was released by the Buccaneers on August 20, 1990.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1990/08/21/nfl-transactions/a88f7139-d71e-459e-af31-5ee99c35d7db/ |title=NFL TRANSACTIONS |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=August 21, 1990 |access-date=October 23, 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024001000/http://www.washingtonpost.com/archive/sports/1990/08/21/nfl-transactions/a88f7139-d71e-459e-af31-5ee99c35d7db/ |archive-date=October 24, 2015 }}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mitchell has worked as a minister and policeman.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://diverseeducation.com/article/59878/ |title=Worth of Athletic Scholarship Can Go Beyond Degree |publisher=diverseeducation.com |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=January 5, 2014 |access-date=October 23, 2015 |author1=Pells, Eddie  |author2=Armour, Nancy |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151024001343/http://diverseeducation.com/article/59878/ |archive-date=October 24, 2015 }}</ref>

'''Amara Darboh''' (born February 1, 1994) is a Sierra Leonean-born former [[American football]] [[wide receiver]]. He was selected by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the third round of the [[2017 NFL draft]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]]. A native of [[Sierra Leone]], Darboh was orphaned during the [[Sierra Leone Civil War]] and moved to Iowa at age seven. He enrolled at the [[University of Michigan]] and was the Wolverines' leading receiver with 58 catches in 2016.

==Early life==
Darboh was born in [[Sierra Leone]], Africa, in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://btn.com/2015/10/02/pregame-profile-learn-the-amazing-story-of-michigan-wr-amara-darboh/ |title=Learn the amazing story of Michigan WR Amara Darboh |date=October 2, 2015 |publisher=Big Ten Network}}</ref> At the age of two, Darboh's parents were killed, and he left the family's home in [[Freetown]] with his siblings to escape the violent [[Sierra Leone Civil War]] that left over 50,000 dead.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Drahold |first=Byron |date=May 1, 2017 |title=New Seahawks wide receiver Amara Darboh's amazing journey |url=http://seahawkswire.usatoday.com/2017/05/01/seahawks-new-wide-receiver-amara-darbohs-amazing-journey |access-date=May 26, 2017 |website=Seahawks Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref><ref name=GII/><ref name=Orphan/> The family lived for a time in [[Gambia]] and [[Senegal]].<ref name=AP/> The family settled in Iowa when Darboh was seven years old.<ref name="GII">{{Cite news |url=http://www.theindependent.com/sports/commentary/bob_hamar/hamar-darboh-is-an-american-success-story/article_01f0cd08-668f-11e6-8172-c70b613b6497.html |title=Darboh is an American success story |last=Bob Hamar |date=August 19, 2016 |work=The Grand Island Independent}}</ref><ref name=AP/> Darboh was taken in by the Schaefer family in [[Des Moines]] and attended Holy Trinity Catholic School and would go on to play [[high school football]] at [[Dowling Catholic High School]] in [[West Des Moines, Iowa]].<ref name="Orphan">{{Cite news |url=http://www.annarbor.com/sports/um-football/from-war-time-orphan-to-big-time-football-michigan-recruit-amara-darboh-tells-survivalist-tale/ |title=War-time orphan to big-time football: Michigan recruit Amara Darboh survives to become Freetown's Finest |last=Kyle Meinke |date=January 29, 2012 |work=The Ann Arbor News}}</ref>

==College career==
Darboh enrolled at the [[University of Michigan]] and has played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] starting in 2012. As a [[true freshman]] in 2012, he appeared in four games as a backup at [[wide receiver]] and 11 games on [[special teams]]. He then missed the 2013 season due to a foot injury sustained prior to the start of the season.<ref name="Bio">{{Cite news |url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/amara_darboh_811603.html |title=Amara Darboh Bio |work=Mgoblue.com |access-date=September 10, 2016 |publisher=University of Michigan}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2015/03/michigan_wr_amara_darboh_sense.html |title=Michigan WR Amara Darboh senses big opportunity, but still focused on helping others |last=Nick Baumgardner |date=March 26, 2015 |work=[[Mlive.com]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2014/08/amara_darboh_hoping_to_bring_a.html |title=Amara Darboh hopes to bring a little extra to the Michigan offense, in more ways than one |last=Brendan F. Quinn |date=August 13, 2014 |work=Mlive.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2014/03/michigan_wr_amara_darboh_feels.html |title=Michigan WR Amara Darboh feels 100 percent after foot injury but still limited in spring practice |last=Kyle Austin |date=March 27, 2014 |work=Mlive.com}}</ref>

Darboh saw his first significant playing time as a [[redshirted|redshirt]] sophomore in 2014. He appeared in 12 games, eight of them as a starter at wide receiver.<ref name=Bio/> His best game of the season was against Indiana on November 1, as he had nine [[football catch|receptions]] for 107 yards and a [[touchdown]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.michigandaily.com/sports/amara-darboh-michigan-footballs-best-kept-secret |title=Amara Darboh: Michigan football's best-kept secret |last=Alexa Dettelbach |date=November 4, 2014 |work=The Michigan Daily}}</ref> Over the course of the entire 2014 season, Darboh was Michigan's second leading receiver (trailing only [[Devin Funchess]]) with 36 receptions for 473 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/stats/112914aab.html |title=Michigan Football Statistics (12-game Totals) |date=November 29, 2014 |website=Mgoblue.com |publisher=University of Michigan |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160921013750/http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-footbl/stats/112914aab.html |archive-date=September 21, 2016 |access-date=September 10, 2016}}</ref>

As a redshirt junior in 2015, Darboh appeared in 13 games, including nine as a starter at wide receiver.<ref name=Bio/> In the season opener against Utah, Darboh had eight receptions for 101 yards and a touchdown.  Darboh also became a United States citizen in September 2016.<ref name="AP">{{Cite news |url=http://collegefootball.ap.org/article/michigans-darboh-becomes-us-citizen-and-makes-amazing-catch |title=Michigan's Darboh Becomes US Citizen and Makes Amazing Catch |last=Larry Lage |date=September 26, 2015 |publisher=Associated Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://michiganjournal.org/2015/09/29/lindsay-darbohs-wild-american-week/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150930102548/http://michiganjournal.org/2015/09/29/lindsay-darbohs-wild-american-week/ |url-status=usurped |archive-date=September 30, 2015 |title=Darboh's Wild, American Week |last=Ricky Lindsay |date=September 25, 2016 |work=The Michigan Journal}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=http://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2015/09/24/michigan-football-amara-darboh/72739304/ |title=U-M's Darboh finishes long journey to U.S. citizenship |last=Mark Snyder |date=September 27, 2015 |work=Detroit Free Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.si.com/college-football/2015/09/24/michigan-wolverines-amara-darboh-becomes-united-states-citizen |title=Michigan WR Amara Darboh grateful to become U.S. citizen |date=September 24, 2015 |publisher=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> Against Indiana on November 14, he had eight catches for 109 yards and a touchdown. === Seattle Seahawks (first stint)===
Darboh was drafted by the [[Seattle Seahawks]] in the third round, 106th overall, in the [[2017 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seattle-seahawks-select-michigan-wide-receiver-amara-darboh-with-no-106-o-186134 |title=Seattle Seahawks Select Michigan Wide Receiver Amara Darboh With No. 106 Overall Pick In 2017 NFL Draft |last=Yohannes, Aron |date=April 28, 2017 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref> On May 23, 2017, Darboh signed a four-year deal worth $3.175 million overall with a $706,288 signing bonus.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.fieldgulls.com/2017/5/25/15695012/seattle-seahawks-sign-malik-mcdowell-amara-darboh-nfl-news |title=Seahawks sign top draft choice Malik McDowell, as well as third-round pick Amara Darboh |last=Alexander, Mookie |date=May 26, 2017 |website=FieldGulls.com |publisher=SBNation |access-date=May 26, 2017}}</ref> On September 10, 2017, Darboh made his NFL debut in a 17–9 loss to the [[Green Bay Packers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709100gnb.htm |title=Seattle Seahawks at Green Bay Packers - September 10th, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |access-date=September 24, 2017}}</ref> In Week 2, against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], he had his first career reception, a 16-yard pass from quarterback [[Russell Wilson]], in the 12–9 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170sea.htm |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks - September 17th, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]] |access-date=October 28, 2017}}</ref>

Darboh was waived by the Seahawks on September 1, 2018.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-set-53-man-roster |title=Seahawks Set 53-Man Roster |date=September 1, 2018 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

=== New England Patriots ===
On September 2, Darboh was claimed off waivers by the [[New England Patriots]], but was waived two days with a failed physical designation.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-claim-two-players |title=Patriots claim two players |date=September 2, 2018 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.patriots.com/news/patriots-make-roster-moves |title=Patriots Make Roster Moves |date=September 4, 2018 |website=Patriots.com}}</ref>

===Seattle Seahawks (second stint)===
After being waived by the Patriots due to a failed physical, Darboh reverted to the Seahawks and was placed on [[injured reserve]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://247sports.com/nfl/seattle-seahawks/Article/Amara-Darboh-Seahawks-IR-return-121871838/ |title=Amara Darboh reverts back to Seahawks Injured Reserve |date=September 14, 2018 |website=247sports.com}}</ref> He was waived on August 27, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.seahawks.com/news/seahawks-make-roster-moves-adding-two-receivers |title=Seahawks Make Roster Moves, Adding Two Receivers |last=Boyle, John |date=August 27, 2019 |website=Seahawks.com}}</ref>

=== Tampa Bay Buccaneers ===
On September 16, 2019, Darboh was signed to the [[practice squad]] of the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-sign-wr-amara-darboh-to-practice-squad-roster-move |title=Bucs Sign WR Amara Darboh to Practice Squad |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=September 16, 2019 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 17, 2019.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/bucs-promote-amara-darboh-practice-squad-kahzin-daniels-roster-move |title=Bucs Promote WR Amara Darboh, Bring OLB Kahzin Daniels Back |last=Smith |first=Scott |date=October 17, 2019 |website=Buccaneers.com}}</ref> He was waived on November 5.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Williams |first=Charean |author-link=Charean Williams |date=November 5, 2019 |title=Bucs waive Amara Darboh |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2019/11/05/bucs-waive-amara-darboh/ |website=Pro Football Talk |publisher=NBC Sports}}</ref>

===Pittsburgh Steelers===
On November 18, 2019, Darboh was signed to the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://steelerswire.usatoday.com/2019/11/18/amara-darboh-quadree-henderson-steelers-nfl-week-12/ |title=Steelers continue to shuffle practice squad players |last=Popejoy |first=Curt |date=November 18, 2019 |website=Steelers Wire |publisher=USA Today |access-date=2019-11-26}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on December 16, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|title=Darboh promoted to active roster|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/darboh-promoted-to-active-roster|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=December 16, 2019}}</ref>

Darboh was waived on September 5, 2020, and was signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers make moves to get to 53-man roster|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-make-moves-to-get-to-53-man-roster|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=September 6, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Steelers add 14 to practice squad|url=https://www.steelers.com/news/steelers-add-14-to-practice-squad|author=Varley, Teresa|website=Steelers.com|date=September 6, 2020}}</ref> He was released on October 26, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dave|last=Bryan|title=Steelers Shuffle Practice Squad Wide Receivers On Monday|url=https://steelersdepot.com/2020/10/steelers-shuffle-practice-squad-wide-receivers-on-monday/|website=SteelersDepot.com|date=October 26, 2020}}</ref>

===Carolina Panthers===
On December 11, 2020, Darboh signed with the practice squad of the [[Carolina Panthers]].<ref>{{cite news |author=Bryan, Will |title=Three players activated from reserve/COVID-19 list |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/three-players-activated-from-reserve-covid-19-list |website=Panthers.com |date=December 11, 2020 |access-date=January 26, 2021}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with the Panthers on January 4, 2021,<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers sign 14 players to reserve future contracts for 2021|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-sign-14-players-to-reserve-future-contracts-for-2021|author=Bryan, Will|website=Panthers.com|date=January 4, 2021}}</ref> and was released on March 15, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Amara Darboh: Let go by Panthers |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/amara-darboh-let-go-by-panthers/ |website=CBSSports.com |date=March 15, 2021 |access-date=March 15, 2021}}</ref>

===Denver Broncos===
On June 17, 2021, Darboh signed with the [[Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{cite web |last=DiLalla |first=Aric |title=Broncos sign WRs Amara Darboh and De'Mornay Pierson-El|url=https://www.denverbroncos.com/news/broncos-sign-wrs-amara-darboh-and-de-mornay-pierson-el|work=Denver Broncos |date=June 17, 2021 |accessdate=June 17, 2021}}</ref> He was waived on August 6, 2021.<ref name="b836">{{cite web | last=Kelberman | first=Zack | title=Broncos Cut WR Amara Darboh, Activate S Jamar Johnson | website=SI.com| date=2021-08-06 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/broncos/news/broncos-cut-amara-darboh-activate-jamar-johnson | access-date=2025-01-18}}</ref>

'''Alvin Mentian Kamara''' (born July 25, 1995)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alvin Kamara (RB): Bio, News, Stats & more |url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/team/players-roster/alvin-kamara/ |access-date=August 19, 2022 |website=NewOrleansSaints.com |language=en-US |quote="Alvin Mentian Kamara was born July 25, 1995 in Atlanta, Ga." |archive-date=August 9, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220809144018/https://www.neworleanssaints.com/team/players-roster/alvin-kamara/ |url-status=live }}</ref> is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] for the [[New Orleans Saints]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|Tennessee Volunteers]] after transferring from [[Hutchinson Community College]] and was selected by the Saints in the third round of the [[2017 NFL draft]]. Kamara was named the [[National Football League Rookie of the Year Award|NFL Rookie of the Year]] in 2017, was named a [[Pro Bowl]]er in his first five NFL seasons, and is a two-time second-team [[All-Pro]]. In 2020, Kamara became the second player in NFL history to score six rushing touchdowns and 36 points in a single game.<ref name="Fact Book" /><ref name="singlegametie">{{Cite magazine |last=Pickman |first=Ben |date=December 25, 2020 |title=NFL Record With Six Rushing TDs vs. Vikings |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2020/12/26/alvin-kamara-saints-ties-record-vikings-six-touchdowns |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201226010529/https://www.si.com/nfl/2020/12/26/alvin-kamara-saints-ties-record-vikings-six-touchdowns |archive-date=December 26, 2020 |access-date=December 25, 2020 |magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> Four years later, he became the Saints' all-time rushing leader.<ref name="NORCareerRushing">{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints Career Rushing Leaders |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nor/career-rushing.htm |access-date=November 10, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

[[Rivals.com]] rated Kamara as the No. 6 player in Georgia.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2012 |title=Norcross' Alvin Kamara is an Under Armour All-American |url=http://usatodayhss.com/2012/norcross-alvin-kamara-is-an-under-armour-all-american |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180618002945/https://usatodayhss.com/2012/norcross-alvin-kamara-is-an-under-armour-all-american |archive-date=June 18, 2018 |access-date=February 28, 2018 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

Kamara received a scholarship offer from [[Syracuse University]] as a junior in high school.<ref>{{cite web | title=Tide of recruiting letters floods 4 Star recruits mailbox | website=Foxy 107.1-104.3 | date=February 18, 2012 | url=https://foxync.com/2558982/tide-of-recruiting-letters-floods-4-star-recruits-mailbox/ | access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref> He received 105 letters from Alabama on the same day.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Silvers |first=Blake |date=February 19, 2012 |title=Nick Saban Sends Georgia Running Back 105 Letters in One Day |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1072286-nick-saban-sends-georgia-running-back-105-letters-in-one-day |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141027041906/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1072286-nick-saban-sends-georgia-running-back-105-letters-in-one-day |archive-date=October 27, 2014 |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> His recruitment eventually came down to Georgia and Alabama.<ref>{{cite web | last=Gribble | first=Andrew | title=Alvin Kamara brings a 'quick twitch' to Crimson Tide backfield (Alabama signee profile) | website=al | date=February 7, 2013 | url=https://www.al.com/sports/2013/02/alvin_kamara_brings_a_quick_tw.html | access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref> He committed to play college football at the [[University of Alabama]] under head coach [[Nick Saban]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hewett |first=Trevor |date=February 6, 2013 |title=4-star RB Alvin Kamara commits to Alabama |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/4-star-RB-Alvin-Kamara-commits-to-Alabama-115393 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201118212646/https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Article/4-star-RB-Alvin-Kamara-commits-to-Alabama-115393/ |archive-date=November 18, 2020 |access-date=February 28, 2018 |website=BamaOnLine}}</ref>

==College career==

===University of Alabama===
Kamara's short time at [[Alabama Crimson Tide football|University of Alabama]] was "a rough experience".<ref name="undef">{{Cite web |last=Reid |first=Jason |date=April 25, 2017 |title=Tennessee's Alvin Kamara takes an unexpected path to NFL draft |url=https://andscape.com/features/tennessee-alvin-kamara-2017-nfl-draft/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200813001723/https://theundefeated.com/features/tennessee-alvin-kamara-2017-nfl-draft/ |archive-date=August 13, 2020 |access-date=April 1, 2020 |website=[[Andscape]]}}</ref> He had knee surgery during the preseason, then [[redshirted]] as a true freshman when he was unable to break into a recruitment class that featured three other future NFL running backs in [[Derrick Henry]], [[T. J. Yeldon]], and [[Kenyan Drake]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Suttles | first=Aaron | title=NOTEBOOK: Kamara has knee scoped, to miss several weeks | website=Tuscaloosa News | date=August 16, 2013 | url=https://www.tuscaloosanews.com/story/sports/2013/08/16/notebook-kamara-has-knee-scoped-to-miss-several-weeks/29909741007/ | access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Alabama 2013 Football Commits |url=https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Season/2013-Football/Commits/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118013721/https://247sports.com/college/alabama/Season/2013-Football/Commits/ |archive-date=January 18, 2021 |access-date=June 19, 2022 |website=247Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Boutwell |first=Josh |date=January 18, 2014 |title=Alabama RB Alvin Kamara To Transfer |url=https://bamahammer.com/2014/01/18/alabama-rb-alvin-kamara-to-transfer/ |archive-url=http://web.archive.org/web/20220703033610/https://bamahammer.com/2014/01/18/alabama-rb-alvin-kamara-to-transfer/ |archive-date=July 3, 2022 |access-date=June 19, 2022 |website=Bama Hammer|publisher=FanSided |language=en-US}}</ref> Due to "behavioral issues", Saban banned Kamara from practicing with the team and suspended him from their bowl game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gribble |first=Andrew |date=December 19, 2013 |title=Alabama LB Xzavier Dickson, RB Alvin Kamara suspended for Sugar Bowl |url=http://www.al.com/alabamafootball/index.ssf/2013/12/alabama_lb_xzavier_dickson_rb.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181106092914/https://www.al.com/alabamafootball/index.ssf/2013/12/alabama_lb_xzavier_dickson_rb.html |archive-date=November 6, 2018 |access-date=February 28, 2018 |website=AL.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Hutchinson Community College===
In 2014, Kamara transferred from Alabama to [[Hutchinson Community College]] in [[Kansas]] for his redshirt freshman season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schmidt |first=Patrick |date=February 17, 2014 |title=Former Alabama back Alvin Kamara transfers to Hutchinson Community College |url=https://fansided.com/2014/02/17/former-alabama-back-alvin-kamara-transfers-hutchinson-community-college/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220619210323/https://fansided.com/2014/02/17/former-alabama-back-alvin-kamara-transfers-hutchinson-community-college/ |archive-date=June 19, 2022 |access-date=June 19, 2022 |website=FanSided |language=en-US}}</ref> In nine games, Kamara ran for 1,253 yards with 18 touchdowns and led the [[Hutchinson Blue Dragons|Blue Dragons]] with 1,477 yards of total offense and 21 touchdowns. Kamara was named [[NJCAA]] [[All-American]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alvin Kamara #1 RB Hutchinson Community College – Kansas Jayhawk Community College Conference |url=http://kjccc.org/sports/fball/2014-15/players/alvinkamara5f7p?view=gamelog&pos=rb |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180301044702/http://kjccc.org/sports/fball/2014-15/players/alvinkamara5f7p?view=gamelog&pos=rb |archive-date=March 1, 2018 |access-date=February 28, 2018 |website=Kansas Jay Community College Conference |language=en}}</ref> His successful season with Blue Dragons propelled Kamara to one of the top JUCO prospects in the nation.<ref>{{cite web | last=Donohue | first=Tyler | title=Power Ranking the Top 2015 JUCO Recruits | website=Bleacher Report | date=March 27, 2014 | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2007038-power-ranking-the-top-2015-juco-recruits | access-date=June 13, 2026}}</ref> Kamara earned a five-star rating from the Rivals.com and Scout.com recruiting networks. He was offered by both Tennessee and the Georgia Bulldogs before ultimately committing to the Volunteers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alvin Kamara Recruit Interests |url=https://247sports.com/Recruitment/Alvin-Kamara-50417/RecruitInterests/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170101042002/http://247sports.com/Recruitment/Alvin-Kamara-50417/RecruitInterests |archive-date=January 1, 2017 |access-date=January 31, 2019 |website=247sports.com}}</ref>

At the end of the [[2016 Tennessee Volunteers football team|2016 season]], Kamara decided to forgo his redshirt senior season and enter the [[2017 NFL draft]]. In his two seasons as a Volunteer, Kamara started in only eight of 24 games due to sharing the backfield with Jalen Hurd, but he amassed almost 2,000 yards from scrimmage and averaged a touchdown per game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brice |first=John |date=December 30, 2016 |title=Vols' Alvin Kamara to enter 2017 NFL Draft |url=http://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/football/2016/12/30/kamara-enter-2017-nfl-draft/96027128/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161231190100/http://www.knoxnews.com/story/sports/college/university-of-tennessee/football/2016/12/30/kamara-enter-2017-nfl-draft/96027128/ |archive-date=December 31, 2016 |access-date=July 26, 2017 |website=KnoxNews.com}}</ref>

===2017 season===
{{See also|2017 New Orleans Saints season}}
The Saints selected Kamara in the third round with the 67th overall pick in the 2017 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rapp |first=Timothy |date=April 28, 2017 |title=Saints Draft RB Alvin Kamara to Join Adrian Peterson and Mark Ingram |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2698726-saints-draft-rb-alvin-kamara-to-join-adrian-peterson-and-mark-ingram |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220619211306/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2698726-saints-draft-rb-alvin-kamara-to-join-adrian-peterson-and-mark-ingram |archive-date=June 19, 2022 |access-date=June 19, 2022 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> He was the second of six Tennessee Volunteers to be selected that year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/draft.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181003194309/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2017/draft.htm |archive-date=October 3, 2018 |access-date=February 28, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> Kamara was the fifth running back selected.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=April 28, 2017 |title=Saints add RB Alvin Kamara to loaded backfield |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/saints-add-rb-alvin-kamara-to-loaded-backfield-0ap3000000804350 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502095450/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000804350/article/saints-add-rb-alvin-kamara-to-loaded-backfield |archive-date=May 2, 2017 |access-date=April 28, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Running backs drafted in the 2017 NFL Draft |url=http://pfref.com/tiny/PRCt5 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730174628/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/play-index/tiny.fcgi?id=PRCt5 |archive-date=July 30, 2020 |access-date=February 10, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> {{As of|2021}}, he also serves as the Saints' emergency quarterback.<ref>{{Cite web |last=King |first=Peter |author-link=Peter King (sportswriter) |date=November 1, 2021 |title=FMIA Week 8: Trevor Siemian Leads Big Day For NFL Backups |url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/11/01/nfl-backups-trevor-siemian-fmia-peter-king/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211101191919/https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2021/11/01/nfl-backups-trevor-siemian-fmia-peter-king/ |archive-date=November 1, 2021 |access-date=November 1, 2021 |website=ProFootballTalk |publisher=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

Kamara split backfield duties with [[Mark Ingram II]] throughout the 2017 season, with fewer carries but more receptions than his teammate.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 New Orleans Saints Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nor/2017.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180329201656/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nor/2017.htm |archive-date=March 29, 2018 |access-date=June 27, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> During the season opener against the Vikings on ''[[Monday Night Football]]'', Kamara debuted with seven rushes for 18 yards, four receptions for 20 yards, and one kickoff return for 26 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Minnesota Vikings – September 11th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709110min.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180329072638/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709110min.htm |archive-date=March 29, 2018 |access-date=October 7, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In Week 2 against the [[New England Patriots]], his role in the passing game expanded with three receptions for 51 yards during the 36–20 loss; he also returned three kickoffs, but would return only one more until Week 16 of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New England Patriots at New Orleans Saints – September 17th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170nor.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180330142141/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201709170nor.htm |archive-date=March 30, 2018 |access-date=October 28, 2017 |website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]}}</ref> Kamara scored his first professional touchdown in Week 3 against the Panthers.<ref name="glog">{{Cite web |title=Alvin Kamara Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KamaAl00/gamelog/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171108032525/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KamaAl00/gamelog/ |archive-date=November 8, 2017 |access-date=November 3, 2017 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

During Week 4, he had 96 scrimmage yards, including 10 receptions for 71 yards and a 12-yard touchdown catch.<ref name="glog" /> This was followed by 10 carries for 75 yards in Week 5, and 107 yards from scrimmage in Week 6 against the [[Green Bay Packers]]. After the bye week, Kamara had a touchdown against the Bears, and then 68 rushing yards including a three-yard touchdown, along with 84 receiving yards including a 33-yard touchdown in a victory over the [[Tampa Bay Buccaneers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tampa Bay Buccaneers at New Orleans Saints – November 5th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711050nor.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201029234655/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201711050nor.htm |archive-date=October 29, 2020 |access-date=November 4, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

During a Week 12 loss to the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Kamara provided 101 receiving yards and 87 rushing yards including a 74-yard rushing touchdown. He became the first player since [[Herschel Walker]] in 1986 to compile 500 rushing and receiving yards in his first 11 career games,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Triplett |first=Mike |date=November 26, 2017 |title=Alvin Kamara show not enough as Rams snap Saints' win streak |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-orleans-saints/post/_/id/28613/alvin-kamara-show-not-enough-as-rams-snap-saints-win-streak |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171127131343/http://www.espn.com/blog/new-orleans-saints/post/_/id/28613/alvin-kamara-show-not-enough-as-rams-snap-saints-win-streak |archive-date=November 27, 2017 |access-date=November 27, 2017 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> and was the first non-quarterback to average over 7.0 yards per carry through 12 weeks since the merger.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Players with at seven yards per carry on at least 60 rushing attempts since 1970, NFL history |url=http://pfref.com/tiny/z7kVe |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703033613/https://stathead.com/tools/tiny.fcgi?id=z7kVe |archive-date=July 3, 2022 |access-date=May 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en |quote=Kamara was still the only non-quarterback rusher with 7.0+ yards per carry after Week 13. Note that running backs Lenny Moore (in 1956 and 1958) and Skeets Quinlan (in 1953) reached this mark in 12-game seasons pre-merger, along with Bo Jackson through six games in his strike-shortened 1987 season.}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], Kamara rushed for 60 yards and two touchdowns and caught five passes for 66 yards,<ref name="glog" /> becoming the fourth 600/600 rookie in NFL history,{{citation needed|date=February 2021}} and tying [[Todd Gurley]] for the league lead in total touchdowns with 11. However, Kamara suffered a concussion on the first drive and missed the rest of the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sessler |first=Marc |date=December 11, 2017 |title=Saints RB Alvin Kamara expects to play against Jets |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/saints-rb-alvin-kamara-expects-to-play-against-jets-0ap3000000891552 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200419002849/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000891552/article/saints-rb-alvin-kamara-expects-to-play-against-jets |archive-date=April 19, 2020 |access-date=May 1, 2020 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He returned the next week with 44 rushing yards and 45 receiving yards and a touchdown against the [[New York Jets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Jets at New Orleans Saints – December 17th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712170nor.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201205082506/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712170nor.htm |archive-date=December 5, 2020 |access-date=December 30, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

On December 19, 2017, Kamara was named to the [[Pro Bowl]] as a rookie alongside Mark Ingram II, becoming the first-ever pair of running backs from the same team to earn the honors.<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 19, 2017 |title=NFL announces 2018 Pro Bowl rosters |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/updated-player-rosters-for-2018-pro-bowl-in-orlando-0ap3000000895772 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171220125215/http://www.nfl.com/news/story/0ap3000000895772/article/nfl-announces-2018-pro-bowl-rosters |archive-date=December 20, 2017 |access-date=December 26, 2017 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> He was named to the NFL All-Rookie Team.<ref name="2017 NFL All-Rookie Team">{{Cite web |title=2017 NFL All-Rookie Team |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2017.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180402035636/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/nfl-all-rookie-2017.htm |archive-date=April 2, 2018 |access-date=April 1, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> After 32 rushing yards and 58 receiving yards in a Week 16 victory over the Falcons, Kamara had a 106-yard kick return for a touchdown, 44 rushing yards and another touchdown, and 84 receiving yards in the regular-season finale against the Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at New Orleans Saints – December 24th, 2017 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712240nor.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200414165220/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201712240nor.htm |archive-date=April 14, 2020 |access-date=January 7, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref>

In 2017, Kamara's 728 yards rushing and 826 yards receiving was the first 700/700 season by a Saint, third by an NFL rookie, and the 11th 700/800 season by any NFL player.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Players with at least 700 rushing yards and 700 receiving yards in a single season, NFL history |url=http://pfref.com/tiny/VrCgD |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730174635/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/play-index/tiny.fcgi?id=z7kVe |archive-date=July 30, 2020 |access-date=May 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> His 728 rushing yards finished third among rookies behind rushing leader [[Kareem Hunt]] and [[Leonard Fournette]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rookie Rushing Yard Leaders, 2017 Season |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/rookie-rushing-yard-leaders-2017 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220619211422/https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/rookie-rushing-yard-leaders-2017 |archive-date=June 19, 2022 |access-date=June 19, 2022 |website=StatMuse |language=en}}</ref> His 81 receptions on the season were first among all rookies and second in the league among running backs behind [[Le'Veon Bell]], and his 826 receiving yards finished first among running backs. Kamara and Ingram became the first running back duo in NFL history to each have over 1,500 scrimmage yards in the same season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McClure |first=Cody |date=December 31, 2017 |title=Former SEC RBs Mark Ingram, Alvin Kamara first teammates to each record 1,500+ scrimmage yards in NFL season |url=https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/sec-football/former-sec-rbs-mark-ingram-alvin-kamara-first-teammates-record-1500-scrimmage-yards-nfl-season/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220703033610/https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/sec-football/former-sec-rbs-mark-ingram-alvin-kamara-first-teammates-record-1500-scrimmage-yards-nfl-season/ |archive-date=July 3, 2022 |access-date=June 19, 2022 |website=Saturday Down South |language=en-US}}</ref> Among non-quarterbacks with 100+ carries, his 6.07 yards per rush was the most ever by an NFL rookie.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rookies with at least six yards per rush, NFL history |url=http://pfref.com/tiny/u236T |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730174640/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/play-index/tiny.fcgi?id=u236T |archive-date=July 30, 2020 |access-date=May 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> It also was the most ever by any Saints player, and the third most by any NFL player since 1980, trailing only [[Jamaal Charles]] (6.38 in 2010) and [[Barry Sanders]] (6.13 in 1997).<ref>{{Cite web |title=List of players with at least 100 rushing attempts, six yards per attempt, and fewer than ten pass attempts, NFL history |url=http://pfref.com/tiny/olg1C |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200730174638/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/play-index/tiny.fcgi?id=olg1C |archive-date=July 30, 2020 |access-date=May 1, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The Saints finished the 2017 season atop the [[NFC South]] with an 11–5 record and qualified for the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2017 New Orleans Saints Statistics & Players |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nor/2017.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180329201656/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/nor/2017.htm |archive-date=March 29, 2018 |access-date=January 18, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> In the [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#NFC: New Orleans Saints 31, Carolina Panthers 26|Wild Card Round]] against the Panthers, Kamara had 23 rushing yards, a rushing touchdown, and a 10-yard reception during the 31–26 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card – Carolina Panthers at New Orleans Saints – January 7th, 2018 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201801070nor.htm |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180110174558/https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/201801070nor.htm |archive-date=January 10, 2018 |access-date=January 18, 2018 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]]}}</ref> During the [[2017–18 NFL playoffs#NFC: Minnesota Vikings 29, New Orleans Saints 24|Divisional Round]] against the Vikings, he caught a 14-yard touchdown from [[Drew Brees]] in the fourth quarter to put the Saints up 21–20. ===2021 season===
{{See also|2021 New Orleans Saints season}}
[[File:Alvin Kamara 2021 (cropped).jpg|thumb|200px|right|Kamara in 2021]]
During Week 7 against the Seahawks, Kamara had 10 receptions for 128 yards and a touchdown to go along with 51 rushing yards in the 13–10 road victory, earning NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Seattle Seahawks - October 25th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202110250sea.htm |access-date=July 31, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=October 27, 2021 |title=Saints RB Alvin Kamara, Bengals WR Ja'Marr Chase lead Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2021-week-7-alvin-kamara-jamarr-chase |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211102023600/https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2021-week-7-alvin-kamara-jamarr-chase |archive-date=November 2, 2021 |access-date=June 18, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In the game, Kamara also reached 3,000 receiving yards in his career, becoming the fastest player in NFL history to reach 3,000 yards in both receiving and rushing. The previous record was 70 games, held by [[Roger Craig (American football)|Roger Craig]], while Kamara achieved the feat in 66 games.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hunte |first=Sydney |date=October 25, 2021 |title=Alvin Kamara breaks NFL record that has stood since the late 1980s |url=https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/nfl/alvin-kamara-breaks-nfl-record-that-has-stood-for-over-30-years/ |url-status=live ===2023 season===
{{See also|2023 New Orleans Saints season}}

On August 4, 2023, Kamara was suspended for three games due to violating the league's personal conduct policy, which stemmed from his involvement in a [[Alvin Kamara#Legal issues|physical altercation]] dating back to February 2022.<ref name="GrantGordon">{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=August 4, 2023 |title=Saints RB Alvin Kamara suspended three games |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/saints-rb-alvin-kamara-suspended-three-games-for-role-in-february-2022-incident- |access-date=August 4, 2023 |website=NFL.com}}</ref>

On September 25, Kamara finished his suspension and was able to prepare for the Saints' upcoming game against the Buccaneers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Smith |first=Michael David |date=September 25, 2023 |title=Alvin Kamara back with Saints after three-game suspension |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/alvin-kamara-back-with-saints-after-three-game-suspension |access-date=September 26, 2023 |website=NBC Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> In his first game back, Kamara had 13 receptions for 33 yards, setting an NFL record for the fewest receiving yards with at least 13 receptions.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Terrell |first=Katherine |date=October 3, 2023 |title=Saints leaned heavily on RB Alvin Kamara in his season debut |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-orleans-saints/post/_/id/36437/saints-lean-heavily-on-rb-alvin-kamara-in-his-season-debut |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> On October 8, Kamara scored a two-yard rushing touchdown against the Patriots. In doing so, he scored his 73rd career touchdown, passing [[Marques Colston]] to become the Saints' all-time touchdown leader.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schumpert |first=Ryan |date=October 8, 2023 |title=Alvin Kamara Makes Saints Franchise History |url=https://www.rockytopinsider.com/2023/10/08/alvin-kamara-makes-saints-franchise-history/ |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=Rocky Top Insider |language=en-US}}</ref> In Week 8 against the Colts, he had a rushing touchdown and receiving touchdown in the victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Indianapolis Colts – October 29th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202310290clt.htm |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He became the first player in franchise history to record 10,000 all-purpose yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Luke |date=October 29, 2023 |title=Alvin Kamara has done something no other Saints player has — and he also tied Jim Brown |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/saints-rb-alvin-kamara-reaches-10000-all-purpose-yards/article_565e0104-76b2-11ee-be4b-b7cb192e10e1.html |access-date=July 30, 2024 |website=NOLA.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 10 against the Vikings, Kamara recorded two two-point conversions, which tied [[Marshall Faulk]] for the most career two-point conversions with seven.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Trottier |first=Jeremy |date=November 12, 2023 |title=Alvin Kamara ties Marshall Faulk for most two-point conversions in NFL history |url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/2023/11/12/saints-alvin-kamara-two-point-conversions-record-marshall-faulk-hall-of-fame-history/ |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=Saints Wire |publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref> In Week 13 against the Lions, he had two rushing touchdowns in the loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at New Orleans Saints – December 3rd, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202312030nor.htm |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He passed [[Mark Ingram II|Mark Ingram]] for the most rushing touchdowns and Colston for the most scrimmage yards in franchise history.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Rose |first=Bob |date=December 4, 2023 |title=Alvin Kamara Makes More Saints History |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/saints/news/kamara-saints-records |access-date=January 25, 2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Johnson |first=Luke |date=December 3, 2023 |title=Alvin Kamara set a pair of Saints franchise records in a losing effort |url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/alvin-kamara-broke-two-saints-records-in-loss-to-lions/article_4fc38f7c-9236-11ee-8238-d345e8fab52e.html |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=NOLA.com |language=en}}</ref>

In 2023, Kamara appeared in 13 games and started 12. He had six games on the season going over 100 scrimmage yards. He finished with 180 carries for 694 yards and five touchdowns to go with 75 receptions for 466 yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alvin Kamara 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KamaAl00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=January 25, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===2024 season===
{{See also|2024 New Orleans Saints season}}

In Week 2, Kamara totaled 180 scrimmage yards, including 115 rushing yards and three touchdowns and 65 receiving yards and a touchdown in a 44–19 victory over the Dallas Cowboys, earning NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=September 18, 2024 |title=Saints RB Alvin Kamara, Bills RB James Cook highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2024-week-2-alvin-kamara-james-cook |access-date=October 14, 2024 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> On October 22, 2024, he signed a two-year, $24.5 million contract extension.<ref>{{cite web|title=RB Alvin Kamara agrees to two-year, $24.5 million contract extension with Saints|url=https://www.nfl.com/news/rb-alvin-kamara-agrees-to-two-year-24-5-million-contract-extension-with-saints|author=Baca, Michael|website=NFL.com|date=October 22, 2024}}</ref>

In Week 9 against the Carolina Panthers, Kamara had 29 carries for 155 yards and six receptions for 60 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New Orleans Saints at Carolina Panthers - November 3rd, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202411030car.htm |access-date=December 26, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In Week 10, against the Falcons, he passed Mark Ingram for the most rushing yards in franchise history.<ref>{{cite web | title=Alvin Kamara passes Mark Ingram to become New Orleans Saints all-time leading rusher | website=NewOrleansSaints.com | date=November 10, 2024 | url=https://www.neworleanssaints.com/news/alvin-kamara-running-back-new-orleans-saints-all-time-leading-rusher-mark-ingram-saints-records | access-date=January 9, 2026}}</ref> In Week 15 against the [[Washington Commanders]], he was part of a trick play that saw him score a touchdown on a 21-yard reception from [[Cedrick Wilson Jr.]]<ref name="h909">{{cite web | last=Gray | first=Darrion | title=WATCH: Saints use a trick play to score first TD of Week 15 | website=Saints Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=December 15, 2024 | url=https://saintswire.usatoday.com/2024/12/15/saints-washington-commanders-trick-play-alvin-kamara-touchdown-pass/ | access-date=February 18, 2025}}</ref> Kamara missed the last three games of the season with a groin injury.<ref name="r282">{{cite web | last=Johnson | first=Luke | title=Saints coach Darren Rizzi shares the latest on Derek Carr and Alvin Kamara injury rehab | website=NOLA.com | date=December 26, 2024 | url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/saints-derek-carr-alvin-kamara-injury-update-raiders/article_4ea0db76-c3d7-11ef-9a96-67b6f0f8ebe0.html | access-date=January 21, 2025}}</ref>

Kamara finished the 2024 season with 228 carries for 950 yards and six touchdowns to go along with 68 receptions for 543 yards and two touchdowns in 14 games and starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alvin Kamara 2024 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KamaAl00/gamelog/2024/ |access-date=January 21, 2025 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

===2025 season===
{{See also|2025 New Orleans Saints season}}
Kamara had two games in the 2025 season with over 100 scrimmage yards: Week 2 against the [[2025 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]] and Week 10 against the [[2025 Carolina Panthers season|Carolina Panthers]]. He missed the final six games of the season due to a [[medial collateral ligament|MCL]] sprain suffered in Week 12 against the [[2025 Atlanta Falcons season|Atlanta Falcons]].<ref>{{cite web | last=Johnson | first=Luke | title=Four takeaways from Mickey Loomis-Kellen Moore press conference: What will happen with the Saints' aging stars? | website=NOLA.com | date=January 7, 2026 | url=https://www.nola.com/sports/saints/takeaways-from-saints-season-ending-press-confeerence/article_f4718a70-12e4-451a-a9d5-7c8cd77c6372.html | access-date=January 9, 2026}}</ref> Kamara finished the year with 131 carries for 471 yards and one touchdown, paired with 33 receptions for 186 yards across 11 total appearances.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alvin Kamara 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/K/KamaAl00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=January 9, 2026 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

[[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland]] | undraftedyear = 2017 | pastteams = * [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] ({{NFL Year|2017}})* * [[Kansas City Chiefs]] ({{NFL Year|2017}})* * [[New York Giants]] ({{NFL Year|2017}}–{{NFL Year|2018}})* * [[Birmingham Iron]] ({{NFL Year|2018}})* * [[Houston Texans]] ({{NFL Year|2018}})* * Birmingham Iron ({{AAF Year|2019}}) * New York Giants ({{NFL Year|2019}}) * [[Ottawa Redblacks]] ({{CFL Year|2021}})* | highlights = * First-team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] ([[2016 Atlantic Coast Conference football season#All-conference teams|2016]]) | pfr = EttaAm00 }} '''Amba Etta-Tawo''' (born November 10, 1993) is a former [[gridiron football|American football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Maryland Terrapins football|Maryland]] from 2012 to 2015 and at [[Syracuse Orange football|Syracuse]] in 2016. ==College career== ===Maryland=== Etta-Tawo began attending [[University of Maryland|Maryland]] in 2012 and redshirted his first season. On August 31, 2013, Etta-Tawo made his collegiate debut and caught first career touchdown reception in a 43–10 victory over [[2013 FIU Panthers football team|FIU]]. On October 13, 2013, Etta-Tawo caught a season-high six passes for a career-high 109 receiving yards during a 34–10 loss to [[2013 Wake Forest Demon Deacons football team|Wake Forest]]. On November 23, 2013, he made four receptions for 57-yards and a touchdown during a 29–26 loss to [[2013 Boston College Eagles football team|Boston College]]. The following week, Etta-Tawo caught four passes for 106 receiving yards in a 41–21 victory over [[2013 NC State Wolfpack football team|NC State]]. He played in 12 games with seven starts with 32 receptions for 500-yards and two touchdowns.{{cite web |title= Syracuse Orange: Player Bio: Amba Etta-Tawo |url= http://cuse.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=12939 |accessdate= January 4, 2018 |website= Cuse.com}} Etta-Tawo returned in 2014 and played in 13 games, while starting the last six. On October 18, 2014, he caught a season-high three passes for 46-yards during a 38–31 victory to [[2014 Iowa Hawkeyes football team|Iowa]]. On November 29, 2018, Etta-Tawo caught a career-long 71-yard touchdown pass in Maryland's 41–38 loss to [[2014 Rutgers Scarlet Knights football team|Rutgers]]. He finished the season with ten receptions for 220 receiving yards and one touchdown. He started the first two games of the 2015 season before being used as a reserve for the remainder of the season. On September 12, 2015, Etta-Tawo caught a season-high five receptions for 49-yards during a 48–27 loss to [[2015 Bowling Green Falcons football team|Bowling Green]]. On November 14, 2015, Etta-Tawo tied his season-high of five receptions and also had a season-high of 63 receiving yards in a 24–7 loss to [[2015 Michigan State Spartans football team|Michigan State]]. Etta-Tawo completed the season with 20 receptions for 216 receiving yards and zero touchdowns in 12 games and two starts.{{cite web| title=Maryland Terrapins Player Bio: Amba Etta-Tawo| url=http://www.umterps.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=207327165| accessdate=January 4, 2018| website=umterps.com}} Head coach [[Randy Edsall]] was fired after Maryland started the season 2–4 and was replaced by [[D. J. Durkin]] when he announced his arrival with Maryland. On March 1, 2016, Etta-Tawo announced via [[Twitter]] his intention to transfer schools for the upcoming 2016 season after graduating in May.{{cite web| title=Maryland WR Amba Etta-Tawo will transfer| url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/terrapins-insider/wp/2016/03/01/maryland-wr-amba-etta-tawo-will-transfer/| accessdate=January 4, 2018| website=WashingtonPost.com| author=Roman Stubbs| date=March 1, 2016}} ===Syracuse=== On March 23, 2016, Etta-Tawo announced via [[Facebook]] that he had officially transferred to [[Syracuse University|Syracuse]] as a graduate transfer. He opted to transfer after having his playing time decreased and falling on Maryland's depth chart.{{cite web| title=Former Maryland WR Amba Etta-Tawo commits to Syracuse football as graduate transfer| url=https://www.syracuse.com/orangefootball/index.ssf/2016/03/amba_etta-tawo_syracuse_football_wide_receiver_maryland.amp| accessdate=January 4, 2018| website=Syracuse.com| date=March 23, 2016}}{{Dead link|date=September 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On September 2, 2016, Etta-Tawo made his official Syracuse Orange debut, catching a 12 passes for 210 receiving yards and a touchdown during a 33–7 routing over [[NCAA Division I|FCS's]] [[2016 Colgate Raiders football team|Colgate]]. On September 24, 2016, he made 12 receptions for a career-high 270 receiving yards and two touchdown receptions in Syracuse's 31–24 win over [[2016 Connecticut Huskies football team|UConn]]. On November 26, 2016, Etta-Tawo had a career-high 13 receptions for 178 receiving yards and a career-high five touchdown receptions during a 76–61 loss to [[2016 Pittsburgh Panthers football team|Pittsburgh]]. He finished his only season under Syracuse head coach [[Dino Babers]] with 94 receptions for 1,482 receiving yards and 14 receiving touchdowns in 12 games and 12 starts.{{cite web| title=Sports-Reference: Amba Etta-Tawo (2016)| url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/amba-etta-tawo-1/gamelog/2016/| accessdate=January 4, 2018| website=sports preference.com}} He led all ACC receivers with seven games with over 100+ receiving yards and set a Syracuse school record. His 14 receiving touchdowns tied [[Tommy Kane|Tommy Kane's]] school record set in 1987. His 1,482 receiving yards ranked eighth in the FBS and second in any power five conference behind only [[2016 Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma's]] [[Dede Westbrook]] (1,524). He was voted team captain at the end of the season and finished being ranked as the 15th best college player and second best wide receiver in the nation by [[ESPN]]. ==Professional career== '''Amani Horatio Oruwariye''' ({{IPAc-en|ɔːr|u|ˈ|w|ɑːr|i|ˌ|j|eɪ}} {{respell|or|oo|WAR|ee|YAY}};<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 Detroit Lions Media Guide |url=https://static.www.nfl.com/league/apps/league-site/media-guides/2022/DET.pdf |access-date=October 3, 2022 |website=NFL.com |publisher=National Football League}}</ref> born February 9, 1996) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Penn State Nittany Lions football|Penn State]].

==Early life==
Oruwariye lettered for three years at [[Gaither High School]] in Tampa, Florida.<ref name="o424">{{cite web | title=Gaither alum selected in NFL Draft | website=The Laker/Lutz News | date=2019-05-08 | url=https://lakerlutznews.com/gaither-alum-selected-in-nfl-draft/ | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref> As a senior, he was voted team MVP and invited to the Hillsborough County All-Star Game.<ref name="n006">{{cite web | title='Tampa Teaches You How to Be Cool Around Greatness': Local Ties in the 2019 Senior Bowl | website=Buccaneers.com| date=2019-01-26 | url=https://www.buccaneers.com/news/tampa-teaches-you-how-to-be-cool-around-greatness-local-ties-in-the-2019-senior-?campaign=sf%3Afanshare%3Afacebook | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref> He was ranked a three star recruit by all four major recruiting services, and 247Sports and Rivals rated him a top 100 prospect in the state of Florida. Oruwariye committed to Vanderbilt University early in his senior year before decommitting and following Head Coach James Franklin to Penn State.<ref name="p105">{{cite web | title=Penn State gets commitment from DB Oruwariye | website=LancasterOnline | date=2014-01-30 | url=https://lancasteronline.com/sports/local_sports/penn-state-gets-commitment-from-db-oruwariye/article_40dfa7d2-89e2-11e3-aa6b-0017a43b2370.html | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref>
