== College career ==
Oruwariye [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]] his true freshman season at Penn State, then appeared in mostly special teams action during his redshirt freshman year.<ref name="b451">{{Cite web |last1=Twentyman |first1=Tim |last2=OHara |first2=Mike |date=2019-04-27 |title=A CLOSER LOOK: Cornerback Amani Oruwariye |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/a-closer-look-cornerback-amani-oruwariye |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Detroit Lions}}</ref>

In 2016, Oruwariye saw more time en route to Penn State's first [[Big Ten]] Championship Game victory. He logged his first interception against Kent State, which he proceeded to return for a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schutte |first=Dustin  |date=September 3, 2016 |title=Amani Oruwariye gets a pick-six for Penn State |url=https://saturdaytradition.com/penn-state-football/amani-oruwariye-gets-pick-six-penn-state/ |access-date=January 30, 2019 |website=Saturday Tradition |language=en-US}}</ref> He finished the season with 23 total tackles.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://gopsusports.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1385|title=Amani Oruwariye - Football|website=Penn State University Athletics|language=en|access-date=January 30, 2019}}</ref><ref name=":1"/>

Oruwariye burst onto the national scene in 2017 due to his personal-best four interceptions, good for fourth in the Big Ten.<ref name="p465">{{cite web | last=McGonigal | first=John | title=Penn State ball-hawk Amani Oruwariye opened eyes in 2017. Now what? | website=Centre Daily Times | date=2018-07-06 | url=https://www.centredaily.com/sports/college/penn-state-university/psu-football/article214174459.html | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref><ref name=":0" /><ref name="j592">{{cite web | title=Penn State's Amani Oruwariye looking forward to leadership role in 2018 | website=Pittsburgh Post-Gazette | date=2018-07-24 | url=https://www.post-gazette.com/sports/psu/2018/07/24/amani-oruwariye-penn-state-defense-big-ten-media-days-2018/stories/201807240118 | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref> He earned recognition from both coaches and the media, who elected him second all-B1G.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://btn.com/2017/11/28/view-the-2017-all-big-ten-football-defensive-teams/|title=View the 2017 All-Big Ten Football Defensive Teams|website=Big Ten Network|date=November 28, 2017|language=en|access-date=January 30, 2019}}</ref> He appeared in all but one game as Penn State clinched its first [[Fiesta Bowl]] victory since 1997.

Oruwariye carried his junior year momentum into his redshirt senior year, starting in each of Penn State's 12 games, picking off three passes, and tallying a career highs in tackles, pass defenses, and forced fumbles.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/amani-oruwariye-1.html|title=Amani Oruwariye College Stats|website=[[Sports Reference]]|language=en|access-date=January 30, 2019}}</ref> His excellence was recognized by coaches, media, the Associated Press, and ESPN, all of whom named him to their All-B1G teams.<ref name="e955">{{cite web | last=Juliano | first=Joe | title=Amani Oruwariye on track to be first Penn State cornerback drafted in first round | website=Inquirer.com | date=2018-12-28 | url=https://www.inquirer.com/college-sports/penn-state/penn-state-nittany-lions-amani-oruwariye-nfl-draft-miles-sanders-20181228.html | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref> He received an invite to the [[Reese's Senior Bowl]] amidst discussions that he could potentially be a first round pick.<ref name="y176">{{cite web | last=Pickel | first=Greg | title=Penn State's Trace McSorley, Amani Oruwariye, accept Senior Bowl invitations | website=pennlive | date=2018-11-21 | url=https://www.pennlive.com/pennstatefootball/2018/11/penn-states-trace-mcsorley-amani-oruwariye-accept-senior-bowl-invitations.html | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
Oruwariye was drafted by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the fifth round (146th overall) of the [[2019 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2019 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2019/draft.htm |access-date=May 18, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the season with two interceptions and third on the Lions' depth chart.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2019/04/27/detroit-lions-armani-oruwariye-2019-nfl-draft/3599022002/ |title=Detroit Lions take Amani Oruwariye in Round 5 of 2019 NFL draft |newspaper=Detroit Free Press |first=Dave |last=Birkett |date=April 27, 2019 |access-date=April 27, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Amani Oruwariye 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OruwAm00/gamelog/2019/ |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Oruwariye was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the Lions on July 29, 2020,<ref>{{cite news |author=Rogers, Justin |title=Kenny Golladay, T.J. Hockenson among Lions placed on COVID reserve list |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2020/07/29/kenny-golladay-t-j-hockenson-among-detroit-lions-placed-covid-reserve-list/5540723002/ |website=DetroitNews.com |date=July 29, 2020 |access-date=July 30, 2020}}</ref> and was activated 10 days later.<ref>{{cite news |title=T.J. Hockenson among 3 Lions removed from COVID-19 reserve list |url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2020/08/08/hockenson-among-3-detroit-lions-players-removed-coronavirus-reserve-list/3328000001/ |website=DetroitNews.com |date=August 8, 2020 |access-date=August 11, 2020}}</ref>
In Week 11 against the [[Carolina Panthers]], Oruwariye recorded his first interception of the season off a pass thrown by [[P. J. Walker]] during the 20–0 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Carolina Panthers - November 22nd, 2020 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202011220car.htm |access-date=November 28, 2020 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2020 season, he appeared in 16 games and started 15. He finished with 53 total tackles (45 solo), one interception, and seven passes defended.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amani Oruwariye 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OruwAm00/gamelog/2020/ |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Oruwariye entered the 2021 season as a starting cornerback for the Lions. He started the first 14 games before suffering a thumb injury in Week 15. He was placed on injured reserve on December 25, ending his season.<ref name="k852">{{cite web | last=Birkett | first=Dave | title=Detroit Lions' Amani Oruwariye (thumb) on injured reserve | website=Detroit Free Press | date=2021-12-25 | url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2021/12/25/detroit-lions-amani-oruwariye-thumb-injury-ir/9017227002/ | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref> He finished the season with 57 tackles, and a team-leading 11 passes defensed and six interceptions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amani Oruwariye 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OruwAm00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was third in the NFL in interceptions at the time of his injury.

In the 2022 season, Oruwariye finished with 44 total tackles (36 solo), three passes defended, and one fumble recovery in 14 games and five starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amani Oruwariye 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OruwAm00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

===New York Giants===
On March 23, 2023, Oruwariye signed a one-year, $1.2 million contract with the [[New York Giants]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Citak |first=Matt |date=March 23, 2023 |title=Former Lions CB Amani Oruwariye joins Giants |url=https://www.giants.com/news/amani-oruwariye-contract-stats-signed-free-agency-nfl-detroit-lions-2023 |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> He was released on August 29, and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=August 29, 2023 |title=Giants announce 53-man roster for 2023 |url=https://www.giants.com/news/new-york-giants-roster-2023-nfl-season-joe-schoen-brian-daboll-transactions |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Giants.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Eisen |first=Michael |date=August 30, 2023 |title=Giants sign 12 players to practice squad |url=https://www.giants.com/news/new-york-giants-practice-squad-roster-nfl-2023-cole-beasley-darrian-beavers |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Giants.com}}</ref> Oruwariye was released on October 10.<ref name="w498">{{cite web | title=WR Cole Beasley restored to Giants practice squad | website=Giants.com| date=2023-10-10 | url=https://www.giants.com/news/cole-beasley-restored-to-practice-squad-roster-amani-oruwariye-cam-sims-bills | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref>

=== Jacksonville Jaguars ===
On October 16, 2023, Oruwariye was signed to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] practice squad.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 16, 2023 |title=Roster Moves: Jaguars Sign CB Amani Oruwariye to Practice Squad, Release OLB Derek Parish |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jaguars-sign-cb-amani-oruwariye-to-practice-squad-release-olb-derek |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref> He was active in one game in the 2023 season, Week 17 against the Panthers.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amani Oruwariye 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OruwAm00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Oruwariye signed a reserve/future contract with Jacksonville on January 8, 2024.<ref name="e792">{{cite web | last=Stites | first=Adam | title=Jaguars sign 11 players to reserve/future contracts | website=Jaguars Wire|publisher=USA Today | date=2024-01-08 | url=https://jaguarswire.usatoday.com/lists/jaguars-2024-reserve-future-contracts-deals-practice-squad/ | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref> He was released by the Jaguars on August 27.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Roster Moves: Jacksonville Jaguars Make The Following Roster Moves Hours Before 2024 Roster Deadline |url=https://www.jaguars.com/news/roster-moves-jacksonville-jaguars-make-the-following-roster-moves-hours-before-2024-roster-deadline |access-date=2024-11-04 |website=Jaguars.com}}</ref>

===Dallas Cowboys===
On August 29, 2024, Oruwariye was signed to the [[Dallas Cowboys]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Carl Lawson, Dalvin Cook headline list of Dallas Cowboys' practice squad signings|url=https://www.dallascowboys.com/news/carl-lawson-headlines-list-of-dallas-cowboys-practice-squad-signings|author=Walker, Patrik|website=DallasCowboys.com|date=August 28, 2024}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 26.<ref name="u137">{{cite web | last=Gurzi | first=Randy | title=Cowboys promote ball-hawking cornerback from practice squad to active roster | website=SI.com | date=2024-10-26 | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/cowboys/news/dallas-cowboys-promote-ball-hawking-cornerback-amani-oruwariye | access-date=2024-11-04}}</ref> In the Week 14 [[Monday Night Football]] game against the [[2024 Cincinnati Bengals season|Cincinnati Bengals]], with two minutes to go in a 20–20 game, Oruwariye muffed a [[blocked punt]], which was eventually recovered by the Bengals for a [[first down]]. The Bengals would score the winning touchdown soon after. Oruwariye refused to speak to the media after the game concluded, and wore a towel on his head while walking to the locker room.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Phillips |first=Ryan |date=December 10, 2024 |title=Cowboys Commit Disastrous Miscue on Blocked Punt to Hand Bengals Win |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/cowboys-blocked-punt-muffed-punt-bengals-win |access-date=December 11, 2024 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans===
On May 13, 2025, Oruwariye signed with the [[Tennessee Titans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Sign CB Amani Oruwariye and DL Carlos Watkins, Release DL Abdullah Anderson|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-cb-amani-oruwariye-and-dl-carlos-watkins-release-dl-abdullah-anderson|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=May 13, 2025}}</ref> He was released on August 26 as part of final roster cuts and re-signed to the practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyatt |first1=Jim |title=Titans Part Ways With 20 Players Ahead of Today's Deadline, While Placing RB Tyjae Spears on Injured Reserve (Designated for Return) |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-part-ways-with-20-players-ahead-of-today-s-deadline-while-placing-rb-tyjae-spears-on-injured-reserve-designated-for-return |website=TennesseeTitans.com |access-date=27 August 2025}}</ref> Oruwariye was released by the Titans on August 29.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Wyatt |first1=Jim |date=August 27, 2025 |title=Titans Sign 14 Players to Practice Squad |url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-14-players-to-practice-squad |access-date=29 August 2025 |website=TennesseeTitans.com}}</ref>

===Baltimore Ravens===
On October 1, 2025, Oruwariye signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web |author=Mink, Ryan |date=October 1, 2025 |title=Ravens Sign Veteran Cornerback to Practice Squad |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-sign-amani-oruwariye-practice-squad-2025 |access-date=May 16, 2026 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref> He signed a reserve/future contract with Baltimore on January 5, 2026.<ref>{{cite web |author=Robertson, Justin |date=January 5, 2026 |title=Ravens Sign Eight Players to Reserve/Future Contracts |url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/ravens-roster-moves-reserves-free-agency |access-date=May 16, 2026 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com}}</ref>

'''Amon-Ra Julian Heru John St. Brown''' (born October 24, 1999) is a German-American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]] for the [[Detroit Lions]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[USC Trojans football|USC Trojans]] and was selected by the Lions in the fourth round of the [[2021 NFL draft]]. St. Brown was voted to the [[Pro Bowl]] four times from 2022 to 2025, and was a first-team [[All-Pro]] in 2023 and 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Twentyman |first=Tim |date=September 18, 2022 |title=FOUR DOWNS: St. Brown continues to set records in win over Commanders |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/st-brown-continues-to-set-records-in-win-over-commanders-goff-swift#:~:text=He's%20also%20produced%20six%20straight,age%2022%2Dor%2Dyounger. |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221231180026/https://www.detroitlions.com/news/st-brown-continues-to-set-records-in-win-over-commanders-goff-swift#:~:text=He's%20also%20produced%20six%20straight,age%2022%2Dor%2Dyounger. |archive-date=December 31, 2022 |access-date=December 31, 2022 |website=Detroit Lions |language=en-US}}</ref> He is the younger brother of [[Equanimeous St. Brown]].

==College career==
[[File:College Football- UCLA at USC. November 23, 2019, Los Angeles, CA - 49129712206.jpg|left|thumb|200px|St. Brown (#8) with [[Drake London]] while at USC]]
In his first game of his college career, St. Brown had seven receptions for 98 yards and a touchdown in a win over [[2018 UNLV Rebels football team|UNLV]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Nevada-Las Vegas at USC Box Score, September 1, 2018 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2018-09-01-southern-california.html |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> On September 15, 2018, St. Brown finished with a career-high 167 yards receiving in a game against [[2018 Texas Longhorns football team|Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaufman |first=Joey |date=September 5, 2018 |title=After strong debut, USC receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown eager to face brother at Stanford |url=http://www.ocregister.com/after-strong-debut-usc-receiver-amon-ra-st-brown-eager-to-face-brother-at-stanford |access-date=September 4, 2019 |website=[[Orange County Register]] |publisher=[[Digital First Media]] |language=en-US}}</ref> St. Brown finished his freshman season with 60 catches, 750 yards, and three touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown 2018 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/amon-ra-st-brown-1/gamelog/2018 |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On November 9, 2019, St. Brown recorded a career high 173 yards in a victory over [[2019 Arizona State Sun Devils football team|Arizona State]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=USC at Arizona State Box Score, November 9, 2019 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2019-11-09-arizona-state.html |access-date=June 9, 2024 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Against Iowa in the Holiday Bowl, he had nine receptions for 163 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Holiday Bowl - USC vs Iowa Box Score, December 27, 2019 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/boxscores/2019-12-27-iowa.html |access-date=2026-03-09 |website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2019, he finished with 77 receptions for 1,042 receiving yards and six receiving touchdowns, adding seven rushes for 60 yards and another touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown 2019 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/amon-ra-st-brown-1/gamelog/2019 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220103081409/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/amon-ra-st-brown-1/gamelog/2019/ |archive-date=January 3, 2022 |access-date=December 8, 2020 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

As a junior in 2020, St. Brown finished with 41 receptions for 478 receiving yards and seven touchdowns in six games.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown 2020 Game Log |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/amon-ra-st-brown-1/gamelog/2020 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220103081412/https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/amon-ra-st-brown-1/gamelog/2020/ |archive-date=January 3, 2022 |access-date=January 12, 2021 |website=[[Sports Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Pre-draft===
On January 2, 2021, St. Brown announced on his Instagram account that he would be declaring for the [[2021 NFL draft]], and was projected by [[CBS Sports]] as a late first round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wells |first=Adam |date=January 2, 2021 |title=USC WR Amon-Ra St. Brown Declares for 2021 NFL Draft |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2925100-usc-wr-amon-ra-st-brown-declares-for-2021-nfl-draft |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221212021319/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2925100-usc-wr-amon-ra-st-brown-declares-for-2021-nfl-draft |archive-date=December 12, 2022 |access-date=December 11, 2022 |website=bleacherreport.com |language=en-US}}</ref>
After St. Brown worked out at the [[NFL Combine]], the NFL released its report on St. Brown by senior NFL analyst [[Lance Zierlein]]. The report placed St. Brown at a second to third round projection, and predicted he would be an average starter.<ref name="Zierlein">{{Cite web |last=Zierlein |first=Lance |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown Draft and Combine Prospect Profile |url=https://www.nfl.com/prospects/amon-ra-st-brown/32005354-4241-5291-a564-57e98d35161d |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220930154406/https://www.nfl.com/prospects/amon-ra-st-brown/32005354-4241-5291-a564-57e98d35161d |archive-date=September 30, 2022 |access-date=December 11, 2022 |website=NFL.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Other scouting reports, including ones by [[Pro Football Focus]] and The Draft Network, placed St. Brown anywhere from a third to fourth round selection, with emphasis on him being a WR2.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Risdon |first=Jeff |date=May 16, 2021 |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown: What scouting reports said before the draft about the Lions wide receiver |url=https://lionswire.usatoday.com/2021/05/16/lions-amon-ra-st-brown-scouting-reports-pre-draft/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221212021320/https://lionswire.usatoday.com/2021/05/16/lions-amon-ra-st-brown-scouting-reports-pre-draft/ |archive-date=December 12, 2022 |access-date=December 11, 2022 |website=Lions Wire|publisher=USA Today |language=en-US}}</ref>

===2021 season===
{{see also|2021 Detroit Lions season}}
St. Brown was drafted in the fourth round, 112th overall, by the [[Detroit Lions]] in the 2021 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Birkett |first=Dave |date=May 1, 2021 |title=Detroit Lions take Amon-Ra St. Brown, USC WR, early in Round 4 of 2021 NFL draft |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2021/05/01/detroit-lions-nfl-draft-2021/4903742001/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210501164137/https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2021/05/01/detroit-lions-nfl-draft-2021/4903742001/ |archive-date=May 1, 2021 |access-date=May 1, 2021 |newspaper=Detroit Free Press}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract with Detroit on June 17, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Levine |first=Ben |date=June 17, 2021 |title=NFL Draft Pick Signings: 6/17/21 |url=https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/06/nfl-draft-pick-signings-6-17-21#ref=home |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210618012332/https://www.profootballrumors.com/2021/06/nfl-draft-pick-signings-6-17-21#ref=home |archive-date=June 18, 2021 |access-date=June 18, 2021 |website=Pro Football Rumors}}</ref>
St. Brown played his first game in Week 1 against the [[San Francisco 49ers]], recording his first reception and finishing the game with two receptions for 23 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Detroit Lions – September 12th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202109120det.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He made his first career start during Week 5 against the [[Minnesota Vikings]], recording seven receptions for 65 yards in their 19–17 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Minnesota Vikings – October 10th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202110100min.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> St. Brown recorded his first career scoring play in a 2-point conversion attempt in their Week 6 loss of 34–11 against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Cincinnati Bengals at Detroit Lions – October 17th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202110170det.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

The Lions entered their Week 13 matchup against the Vikings with a record of 0–10–1, in a 364-day, 15-game winless streak. With 4 seconds left in the fourth quarter, down 27–23, quarterback [[Jared Goff]] threw the game-winning touchdown pass to St. Brown, his first career receiving touchdown, clinching the Lions' first win of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Walsh |first=Erin |date=December 5, 2021 |title=Jared Goff, Lions Earn 1st Win of the Season on Late Amon-Ra St. Brown TD vs. Vikings |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10020061-jared-goff-lions-earn-1st-win-of-the-season-on-late-amon-ra-st-brown-td-vs-vikings |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211205232156/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10020061-jared-goff-lions-earn-1st-win-of-the-season-on-late-amon-ra-st-brown-td-vs-vikings |archive-date=December 5, 2021 |access-date=December 5, 2021 |website=Bleacher Report |language=en}}</ref> In late December, St. Brown won the NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month award. Throughout December, he had recorded 35 receptions, 340 receiving yards, and three receiving touchdowns, all of which led the entire rookie class. In addition, he recorded 26 rushing yards.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Maakaron |first=John |date=December 30, 2021 |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown Named NFL Offensive Rookie of the Month |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/.amp/news/amonra-st-brown-wins-nfl-rookie-of-the-month-award |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211231024920/https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/.amp/news/amonra-st-brown-wins-nfl-rookie-of-the-month-award |archive-date=December 31, 2021 |access-date=December 30, 2021 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-US}}</ref>

Overall, St. Brown finished his rookie season with 90 receptions for 912 receiving yards and five receiving touchdowns, to go along with 61 rushing yards and 1 rushing touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/StxxAm00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> St. Brown finished fifth in yardage for the 2021 wide receiver rookie class, as well as having the most yardage for a non-first round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rookie Receiving Leaders 2021 |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/rookie-receiving-leaders-2021 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221212021315/https://www.statmuse.com/nfl/ask/rookie-receiving-leaders-2021 |archive-date=December 12, 2022 |access-date=December 11, 2022 |website=statmuse.com}}</ref>

===2022 season===
[[File:Amon-Ra St. Brown vs. Commanders 2022.jpg|thumb|right|225px|St. Brown playing against the Washington Commanders in 2022.]]

In their season opener against the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], St. Brown put up an eight-reception, 64-yard performance with one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Philadelphia Eagles at Detroit Lions – September 11th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209110det.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> Coincidentally, his touchdown came two minutes before his brother [[Equanimeous St. Brown|Equanimeous]] scored a touchdown in the [[Chicago Bears]]' season opener (this was his brother's first touchdown as a Bear).<ref>{{Cite web |last=Patra |first=Kevin |date=September 12, 2022 |title=Brothers Amon-Ra and Equanimeous St. Brown score TDs two minutes apart for Lions, Bears |url=https://www.nfl.com/_amp/amon-ra-equanimeous-st-brown-score-tds-two-minutes-apart-lions-bears |access-date=June 17, 2023 |website=NFL.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 2 against the [[Washington Commanders]], St. Brown became the first player in NFL history to have six straight regular season games with at least eight receptions and at least one touchdown, finishing the game with nine receptions for 116 yards and two touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chirco |first=Vito |date=September 18, 2022 |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown Sets NFL Record |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/news/amon-ra-st-brown-sets-nfl-record |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220918203555/https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/news/amon-ra-st-brown-sets-nfl-record |archive-date=September 18, 2022 |access-date=September 19, 2022 |website=si.com}}</ref> The streak began in Week 15 of the 2021 season. St. Brown was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week for his performance.<ref name="nfl.com">{{Cite web |last=Gordon |first=Grant |date=September 21, 2022 |title=Dolphins QB Tua Tagovailoa, Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown highlight Players of the Week |url=https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2022-week-2-tua-tagovailoa-amon-ra-st-brown |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221008032040/https://www.nfl.com/news/players-of-the-week-2022-week-2-tua-tagovailoa-amon-ra-st-brown |archive-date=October 8, 2022 |access-date=September 21, 2022 |website=NFL.com}}</ref> In a Week 3 matchup against division rival Vikings, his streak would end when St. Brown received 6 passes for 73 yards with no touchdowns. In the second quarter of that game, St. Brown would visit training staff with an ankle injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ricketson |first=Teddy |date=September 25, 2022 |title=Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown dealing with ankle injury in Week 3 vs. Vikings |url=https://dknation.draftkings.com/nfl-injuries-fantasy/2022/9/25/23358428/amon-ra-st-brown-injury-updates-week-3-lions-vs-vikings-how-long-out-fantasy-football-depth-chart |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221225010109/https://dknation.draftkings.com/nfl-injuries-fantasy/2022/9/25/23358428/amon-ra-st-brown-injury-updates-week-3-lions-vs-vikings-how-long-out-fantasy-football-depth-chart |archive-date=December 25, 2022 |access-date=December 24, 2022 |website=dknation.draftkings.com}}</ref> This injury would cause St. Brown to miss their Week 4 matchup against the [[Seattle Seahawks]], where the Lions would lose in a close 48–45 battle.<ref>{{Cite web |date=September 30, 2022 |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown ruled OUT ahead of Week 4 vs. Seahawks |url=https://dknation.draftkings.com/nfl-injuries-fantasy/2022/9/28/23376572/amon-ra-st-brown-injury-update-week-4-lions-vs-seahawks-fantasy-football-dandre-swift |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221225004605/https://dknation.draftkings.com/nfl-injuries-fantasy/2022/9/28/23376572/amon-ra-st-brown-injury-update-week-4-lions-vs-seahawks-fantasy-football-dandre-swift |archive-date=December 25, 2022 |access-date=December 24, 2022 |website=DKNation}}</ref> Returning in Week 5 against the [[New England Patriots]], St. Brown put up just 18 yards on four receptions, ending with the Lions getting shut out 29–0.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at New England Patriots – October 9th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210090nwe.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

With the Lions returning from their bye week to play against the [[Dallas Cowboys]], St. Brown went into concussion protocol after being tackled by Cowboys' cornerback [[Jourdan Lewis]] following his first reception of the game. St. Brown would not return in that game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Maakaron |first=John |date=October 23, 2022 |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown Leaves Cowboys Game, Ruled Out |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/news/st-brown-leaves-cowboys-game-ruled-out |url-status=live |website=SI.com}}</ref> He returned to play in Week 9 versus the [[Miami Dolphins]].<ref name="2022.games" /> In Week 10, against the Bears, he had ten receptions for 119 yards in their 31–30 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Detroit Lions at Chicago Bears – November 13th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202211130chi.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro |title=Buffalo Bills at Detroit Lions – November 24th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202211240det.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In a 40–14 victory over the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] the following week, he had 11 receptions for 114 receiving yards and two receiving touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Jacksonville Jaguars at Detroit Lions – December 4th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202212040det.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] accumulate 1,000 receiving yards in a single season, beating out [[Calvin Johnson|Calvin Johnson's]] record by eight days.<ref name="1kyards">{{Cite web |last=Meinke |first=Kyle |date=December 24, 2022 |access-date=December 24, 2022 |website=mlive.com}}</ref> For his efforts, St. Brown was named as a [[Pro Bowler]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2022/probowl.htm |access-date=June 3, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref name="2022.games">{{Cite web |title=Amon-Ra ===2023 season===
In Week 2, against the Seahawks, St. Brown made his first career fumble, which was recovered by the Seahawks.<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Booher |first=Christian |date=September 17, 2023 |title=Grades: Turnovers, Poor Coaching, Defensive Woes Topple Lions |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/news/grades-turnovers-poor-coaching-topple-lions |access-date=March 19, 2024 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en}}</ref> This was one of three turnovers committed by the team that day, resulting in a Lions loss in overtime 37–31.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pouncy |first=Colton |date=September 17, 2023 |title=Lions still have plenty of promise, but loss to Seahawks had a familiar feel |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4872044/2023/09/17/lions-seahawks-recap-jared-goff/ |access-date=July 1, 2024 |website=The New York Times |language=en-US}}</ref> He started the 2023 season with injuries that caused him to miss the fourth quarter of their Week 2 game.<ref>{{Cite web |date=October 4, 2023 |title=Lions' Amon-Ra St. Brown: Tending to abdominal injury |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/lions-amon-ra-st-brown-tending-to-abdominal-injury/ |access-date=October 5, 2023 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

In Week 11 against the [[Los Angeles Chargers]], St. Brown caught eight passes for a career-high 156 yards and a touchdown in a 41–38 win. The game also marks the fourth consecutive game in which St. Brown caught for more than 100 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Twentyman |first=Tim |date=November 12, 2023 |title=NOTEBOOK: St. Brown has career day in Lions' win over Chargers |url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/notebook-st-brown-has-career-day-in-lions-win-over-chargers |access-date=April 19, 2024 |website=Detroit Lions}}</ref> In Week 18 against the Vikings, St. Brown caught a 70-yard touchdown pass, the longest reception of his career.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Woodyard |first=Eric |date=January 7, 2024 |title=Lions' Amon-Ra St. Brown catches 70-yard touchdown pass from Jared Goff |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/39259973/lions-amon-ra-st-brown-catches-70-yard-touchdown-jared-goff |access-date=June 9, 2024 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref>

St. Brown finished the 2023 season third in the NFL with 1,515 receiving yards (behind [[Tyreek Hill]] and [[CeeDee Lamb]])<ref>{{Cite web |last=Werner |first=Barry |date=January 9, 2024 |title=2023 NFL receiving leaders by yardage |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/2023-nfl-receiving-leaders-yardage-180019125.html |access-date=June 9, 2024 |website=Yahoo! Sports |publisher=List Wire}}</ref> He was selected as a First team [[All-Pro]] and earned Pro Bowl honors.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Birkett |first=Dave |date=January 12, 2024 |title=Snubbed from the Pro Bowl, Detroit Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown earns first-team NFL All-Pro |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2024/01/12/detroit-lions-nfl-all-pro-team-amon-ra-st-brown-penei-sewell/72204443007/ |access-date=June 9, 2024 |website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 NFL Pro Bowlers |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2023/probowl.htm |access-date=June 9, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

In the [[2023–24 NFL playoffs#NFC: Detroit Lions 24, Los Angeles Rams 23|Wild Card Round]] game against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], St. Brown had eight receptions for 110 yards in his playoff debut, including a crucial first down pass from [[Jared Goff]] in the fourth quarter that secured a 24–23 victory, the Lions' first playoff win in over 30 years.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 14, 2024 |title=AMON-RA ST. BROWN HITS CENTURY MARK IN PLAYOFF DEBUT |url=https://www.thefantasyfootballers.com/news/564908/amon-ra-st-brown-hits-century-mark-in-playoff-debut/ |access-date=June 9, 2024 |website=The Fantasy Footballers}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Moran |first=Zack |date=January 15, 2024 |title=Studs & Duds for the Lions playoff victory over the Rams |url=https://lionswire.usatoday.com/lists/studs-duds-for-the-lions-playoff-victory-over-the-rams/ |access-date=June 9, 2024 |website=Lions Wire |publisher=USA Today}}</ref> He scored a receiving touchdown in the Lions' win over the Buccaneers in the [[2023–24 NFL playoffs#NFC: Detroit Lions 31, Tampa Bay Buccaneers 23|Divisional Round]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round – Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions – January 21st, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401210det.htm |access-date=July 18, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He was ranked 23rd by his fellow players on the [[NFL Top 100 Players of 2024]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 NFL Top 100 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/awards/2024-nfl-top-100.htm |access-date=September 27, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

St. Brown's 2023 season is featured in the [[Netflix]] documentary series ''Receiver'' which released on July 11, 2024.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Pouncy |first=Colton |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown ascends to stardom with Netflix cameras rolling for 'Receiver' series |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5627143/2024/07/10/netflix-receiver-amon-ra-st-brown-detroit-lions/ |access-date=July 23, 2024 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref>

===2025 season===
In a 52–21 victory over the [[2025 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]] in Week 2, St. Brown recorded nine receptions for 115 yards and three touchdowns.<ref>{{cite web | last=Risdon | first=Jeff | title=Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown wins FedEx Air & Ground Player of the Week | website=Lions Wire |publisher=USA Today| date=2025-09-18 | url=https://lionswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2025/09/18/amon-ra-st-brown-lions-fedex-player-of-week-2/86219017007/ | access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref> In Week 10, St. Brown was punched in face by [[2025 Washington Commanders season|Washington Commanders]] defensive tackle, [[Daron Payne]]. In the post-game interview, St. Brown stated the two got in a "scuffle" a few plays earlier, but admitted to no wrongdoing on his part.<ref>{{cite news |last=Manning |first=Bryan |date=November 10, 2025 |title=What did Lions WR Amon-Ra St. Brown say about Daron Payne throwing punch at him? |url=https://commanderswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/commanders/2025/11/10/washington-commanders-amon-ra-st-brown-reacts-daron-payne/87191013007/ |accessdate=November 17, 2025 |work=Commanders Wire|publisher=USA Today}}</ref> Afterwards video evidence was made public that revealed that St. Brown had punched Payne in the head a few plays earlier and was not ejected despite an [[Official (gridiron football)|official]] witnessing the strike by St. Brown.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/video-surfaces-of-amon-ra-st-brown-appearing-to-strike-daron-payne|work=NBCSports.com|title=Video surfaces of Amon-Ra St. Brown appearing to strike Daron Payne|first=Josh|last=Alper|date=November 11, 2025|accessdate=November 17, 2025}}</ref> On November 15, 2025, the NFL issued him a $12,172 fine for punching Payne, which was met with criticism due to Payne being issued a one-game suspension by the league for same offense.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/lions/onsi/news/lions-wr-fined-for-punching-commanders-defender|work=SI.com|title=Lions WR Fined for Punching Commanders Defender|first=Christian|last=Booher|date=November 15, 2025|accessdate=November 17, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/commanders/onsi/news/commanders-daron-payne-suspension-amon-ra-st-brown-podcast-admission|work=SI.com|title=Commanders player's suspension is at the center of a new controversy|first=Joanne|last=Coley|date=November 12, 2025|accessdate=November 17, 2025}}</ref> In the following game, he had nine receptions for 149 yards and a touchdown in the 34–27 overtime win over the Giants.<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Giants at Detroit Lions - November 23rd, 2025 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202511230det.htm |access-date=2026-03-09 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In Week 15, against the Rams, he had 13 receptions for 164 yards and two touchdowns in the 41–34 loss.<ref>{{cite web | title=Lions' Amon-Ra St. Brown: Posts 13-164-2 line Sunday | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-12-15 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/lions-amon-ra-st-brown-posts-13-164-2-line-sunday/ | access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref> In Week 18, against the Bears, he had 11 receptions for 139 yards in the 19–16 win.<ref>{{cite web | last=Birkett | first=Dave | title=Lions-Bears grades, Amon-Ra St. Brown, Jake Bates clutch in Lions win | website=Detroit Free Press | date=2026-01-05 | url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/nfl/lions/2026/01/04/lions-grades-vs-bears/88017181007/?gnt-cfr=1&gca-cat=p&gca-uir=false&gca-epti=z11xx98p119750c119750u114401e1121xxv11xx98&gca-ft=321&gca-ds=sophi&gnt-djm=1 | access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref> He finished the 2025 season with 117 receptions for 1,401 yards and 11 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown 2025 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/S/StxxAm00/gamelog/2025/ |access-date=2026-03-09 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> His 11 receiving touchdowns tied for second in the NFL.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2025 NFL Leaders and Leaderboards |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2025/leaders.htm |access-date=2026-03-09 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He earned Pro Bowl honors for the fourth consecutive season.<ref>{{cite web | last=DeYoung | first=Abigail | title=Meet the 6 Lions participating at 2026 Pro Bowl Games | website=Detroit Lions | date=2026-01-31 | url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/meet-the-6-lions-participating-at-2026-pro-bowl-games-campbell-gibbs-hutchinson | access-date=2026-03-09}}</ref>

==Personal life==
===Name===
St. Brown’s father chose his children's names from an interest in names he considered African, particularly Egyptian ones. Amon-Ra's name comes from [[Amun-Ra]], the god of the air, the sun, and creation {{endash}} seen as the creator of all things {{endash}} in [[Egyptian mythology]];<ref name=sportingsnews2022amon>{{cite web |url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/nfl/news/amon-ra-st-brown-name-meaning-sun-god-nickname-lions/e8i0rkjqcdsmbyrbpfdhshye |title=Amon-Ra St. Brown name meaning: How Lions WR got his 'Sun God' nickname |website=The Sporting News |last=Skiver |first=Kevin |date=November 24, 2022 |access-date=September 4, 2024}}</ref> he was seen as [[king of the gods]].<ref name=":17">{{Cite book |last=Stark |first=Rodney |title=Discovering God: The Origins of the Great Religions and the Evolution of Belief |publisher=[[HarperOne]] |year=2007 |isbn=978-0-06-117389-9 |edition=1st |location=New York |pages=405 |author-link=Rodney Stark}}</ref> Amun-Ra was also specifically worshipped as the head of the city of [[Thebes, Egypt|Thebes]].<ref name=sportingsnews2022amon/>

On his children's birth certificates, John Brown had his children's surnames listed as ''St. Brown'' rather than his last name because "There's too many of those guys" with the last name ''Brown'' on the back of their jerseys, as John had the expectation that his children would become athletes. John and Miriam considered ''Von Brown'' and ''St. Brown'' before John settled on the latter.<ref>{{cite web |title=Miram and John Brown with Netflix Sports |url=https://www.tiktok.com/@netflixsports/video/7529306720590449925 |website=TikTok |publisher=Netflix Sports |access-date=10 September 2025}}</ref>

St. Brown has been in a relationship with registered nurse and model Brooklyn Adams since 2016.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wilshere |first=Meredith |date=November 2, 2025 |title=Brooklyn Adams Talks 10-Year Amon-Ra St. Brown Romance, ‘Lonely Lifestyle' and How She Really Feels About WAG Title (Exclusive) |url=https://people.com/brooklyn-adams-talks-amon-ra-st-brown-relationship-exclusive-11835029 |access-date=2025-11-03 |website=People.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Philanthropy ===
St. Brown is a community ambassador for United Health Share Ministries, a [[Health care sharing ministry|Christian healthcare]] non-profit organization.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kerr |first=Jeff |date=July 4, 2021 |title=Lions' Amon-Ra St. Brown on his chemistry with Jared Goff, being a rookie, playing for Dan Campbell and more |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/lions-amon-ra-st-brown-on-his-chemistry-with-jared-goff-being-a-rookie-playing-for-dan-campbell-and-more/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210816102309/https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/lions-amon-ra-st-brown-on-his-chemistry-with-jared-goff-being-a-rookie-playing-for-dan-campbell-and-more/ |archive-date=August 16, 2021 |access-date=August 16, 2021 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alvin Jones Jr.''' (born December 2, 1994) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] at [[UTEP Miners football|UTEP]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.baltimoreravens.com/team/players-roster/alvin-jones/|title=Alvin Jones|website=BaltimoreRavens.com|accessdate=May 2, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nfl.com/players/alvinjones/profile?id=JON030280|title=Alvin Jones|website=Nfl.com|accessdate=May 2, 2019}}</ref> and originally signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) as an [[undrafted free agent]] in 2018. He later played for the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL).

==Professional career==
===Baltimore Ravens===
Jones signed with the [[Baltimore Ravens]] as an undrafted free agent in 2018. He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on August 31, 2018, and was released a week later. He was re-signed to the practice squad on October 15, 2018.

Jones signed a reserve/future contract on January 7, 2019. He was placed on [[injured reserve]] on August 31, 2019, and waived from injured reserve with an injury settlement on September 10.

===Saskatchewan Roughriders===
After two years away from football, Jones signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League|CFL]] on October 21, 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Chavez |first1=Felix F. |title=El Paso's Alvin Jones Jr. signs with CFL's Saskatchewan Roughriders |url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/sports/2021/10/22/cfls-saskatchewan-roughriders-signs-el-pasos-alvin-jones-jr/6131507001/ |website=ElPasoTimes.com |publisher=El Paso Times |access-date=25 October 2021 |date=22 October 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ryan |first1=Nate |title=Alvin Jones signs contract with Saskatchewan Roughriders of Canadian Football League |url=https://kvia.com/sports/utep/2021/10/21/alvin-jones-signs-contract-with-saskatchewan-roughriders-of-canadian-football-league/ |website=KVIA.com |access-date=25 October 2021 |date=21 October 2021}}</ref> He was released on June 4, 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Cutdown Tracker: Teams announce their final roster cuts |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2022/06/04/cutdown-tracker-teams-announce-their-final-cuts/ |website=CFL.ca |access-date=19 September 2022 |date=4 June 2022}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Jones is the [[fraternal twin]] brother of [[Minnesota Vikings]] [[running back]] [[Aaron Jones (running back)|Aaron Jones]]; Alvin is older than Aaron by 30 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Demovsky |first1=Rob |title=Packers rookie Aaron Jones still relies on twin brother from afar |url=https://www.espn.com/blog/green-bay-packers/post/_/id/41422/packers-rookie-running-back-aaron-jones-still-figuring-out-being-apart-from-twin-brother-alvin |website=ESPN.com |accessdate=19 September 2020 |date=13 October 2017}}</ref> Their parents, Alvin Sr. and Vurgess, were both career [[Non-commissioned officer#United States|NCOs]] in the [[United States Army|US Army]], with a combined 56 years of service.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hodkiewicz |first1=Wes |title=Family makes Aaron Jones feel at home on any football field |url=https://www.packers.com/news/longform/family-makes-aaron-jones-feel-at-home-on-any-football-field |website=Packers.com |accessdate=19 September 2020 |date=17 January 2020}}</ref>

'''Amik Robertson''' (born July 6, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Washington Commanders]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). Robertson played [[college football]] for the [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech Bulldogs]] and was selected by the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] in the fourth round of the [[2020 NFL draft]]. He has also played for the [[Detroit Lions]].

==Early life==
Robertson attended [[Thibodaux High School]] in [[Thibodaux, Louisiana]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 28, 2016 |title=LSU should extend an offer to Amik Robertson |url=https://www.houmatimes.com/sports/lsu-should-extend-an-offer-to-amik-robertson/ |access-date=October 7, 2023 |website=The Times of Houma/Thibodaux |language=en-US}}</ref> A 3-star recruit, Robertson committed to [[Louisiana Tech Bulldogs football|Louisiana Tech]] to play football over offers from [[Houston Cougars football|Houston]], [[Kansas State Wildcats football|Kansas State]], and [[LSU Tigers football|LSU]], among others.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amik Robertson 2017 cornerback Louisiana Tech |url=https://rivals.com/content/athletes/amik-robertson-67259?view=pv |access-date=July 1, 2024 |website=Rivals.com |language=en-US}}</ref>

==College career==
Robertson played at [[Louisiana Tech University]] from 2017 to 2019.<ref>{{cite web | last=Diaz | first=Cory | title=How life made Louisiana Tech's Amik Robertson grow up fast | website=The News Star| date=2018-03-16 | url=https://www.thenewsstar.com/story/sports/college/louisiana-tech/2018/03/16/meek-amik-how-life-changed-made-star-la-tech-corner-grow-up-fast/432925002/ | access-date=2025-07-06}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |first=Chris|last=Singleton|title=Chris Singleton: Amik Robertson is the best DB in the land |url=https://www.dailycomet.com/sports/20191022/chris-singleton-amik-robertson-is-best-db-in-land |website=Daily Comet}}</ref> He became a starter his freshman year and remained there throughout his college career. As a freshman he was the Defensive MVP of the [[2017 Frisco Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |first=Chris|last=Singleton|title=Robertson wins defensive award at Frisco Bowl |url=https://www.houmatoday.com/sports/20171221/robertson-wins-defensive-award-at-frisco-bowl |website=Houma Today}}</ref> As a junior he was named a first-team [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] by the [[Football Writers Association of America]] (FWAA).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Louisiana Tech star corner Amik Robertson earns First-team All-American honors |url=https://www.thenewsstar.com/story/sports/college/louisiana-tech/2019/12/09/la-tech-football-star-cb-amik-robertson-earns-all-american-honors/2632885001/ |website=thenewsstar.com}}</ref> He finished his career with 184 tackles, 14 [[interceptions]], four [[Quarterback sack|sacks]] and three [[touchdowns]]. After his junior season, he entered the [[2020 NFL draft]], forgoing his senior season.<ref name="p719">{{cite web | last=Diaz | first=Cory | title=LA Tech football star Amik Robertson enters 2020 NFL draft | website=The News Star| date=December 17, 2019 | url=https://www.thenewsstar.com/story/sports/college/louisiana-tech/2019/12/17/la-tech-football-star-amik-robertson-enters-2020-nfl-draft/2675187001/ | access-date=October 22, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Las Vegas Raiders===
====2020====
He attended the [[NFL Scouting Combine]], but chose not to participate in any physical drills. NFL draft scouts and analysts correlated the lack of interest and attention Robertson received to his lack of size although he produced well throughout his collegiate career. [[Scouts Inc.]] had Robertson listed as the ninth best cornerback (68th overall) on their big board.<ref>{{cite web| title=2020 NFL draft rankings: Scouts Inc.'s full board, grades|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/draft2020/story/_/id/41035192/2020-nfl-draft-rankings-top-prospects-scouts-inc| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=ESPN.com| author=Scouts Inc.| date=April 26, 2020}}</ref> [[NFL.com]] media analyst [[Daniel Jeremiah]] listed Robertson as the 11th best cornerback prospect (85th overall) in the draft.<ref>{{cite web| title=Daniel Jeremiah's top 150 prospects in the 2020 NFL Draft class| url=https://www.nfl.com/news/daniel-jeremiah-s-top-150-prospects-in-the-2020-nfl-draft-class-0ap3000001110012 |access-date=February 20, 2025| website=NFL.com| author=Daniel Jeremiah |date=April 20, 2020}}</ref>
Kevin Hanson of ''[[Sports Illustrated]]'' ranked him as the 14th best cornerback prospect in the draft.<ref>{{cite web | title=2020 NFL draft rankings: cornerbacks| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/2020/02/20/nfl-draft-2020-cornerbacks-rankings-best-prospects |access-date=February 6, 2025| website=SI.com| author=Kevin Hanson| date=February 20, 2020}}</ref> The majority of NFL draft analysts projected he could be selected as early as the third round, or as late as the fifth round in the 2020 NFL draft. NFL analyst [[Lance Zierlein]] projected Robertson would be selected in the fourth or fifth round.

The [[Las Vegas Raiders]] selected Robertson in the fourth round (139th overall) of the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Martin |first=Kyle |date=April 25, 2020 |title=NFL analysts rave over the Raiders' fourth-round steal, Amik Robertson |work=Raiders.com |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/nfl-analysts-rave-about-the-raiders-fourth-round-steal-amik-robertson |access-date=April 28, 2020}}</ref> He was the 16th cornerback drafted and the second of two cornerbacks selected by the Raiders in 2020, following first-round pick (19th overall) [[Damon Arnette]].

On July 25, 2020, the Las Vegas Raiders signed Robertson to a four–year, $3.78 million [[rookie]] [[contract]] that includes an initial [[signing bonus]] of $494,400.<ref name="spotrac">{{cite web| title=Spotrac.com: Amik Robertson contract| url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/player/_/id/47734/amik-robertson |access-date=May 14, 2025| website=Spotrac.com}}</ref>

He entered training camp as a candidate to earn a starting role at cornerback, but had to compete among a group that included Damon Arnette, [[Trayvon Mullen]], [[Prince Amukamara]], [[Lamarcus Joyner]], and [[Isaiah Johnson (cornerback, born December 1995)|Isaiah Johnson]].<ref>{{cite web| title=2020 Position Battle: The Raiders' youthful cornerback room will be put to the test this season| url=https://www.raiders.com/news/2020-position-battle-the-raiders-cornerback-room-will-be-put-to-the-test| access-date=May 14, 2025| website=Raiders.com| date=July 3, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web| title=Top 2020 training camp battles for Raiders: Defense takes center stage as Las Vegas era begins| url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/top-2020-training-camp-battles-for-raiders-defense-takes-center-stage-as-las-vegas-era-begins/| access-date=May 14, 2025| website=cbssports.com| date=July 30, 2020| author=Tyler Sullivan}}</ref> Head coach [[Jon Gruden]] named him a backup cornerback to begin the season, behind Trayvon Mullen, Lamarcus Joyner, Damon Arnette, Isaiah Johnson, and [[Keisean Nixon]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Raiders projected 53-man roster, depth chart for 2020| url=https://www.silverandblackpride.com/2020/9/2/21404787/raiders-projected-53-man-roster-depth-chart-2020| access-date=May 14, 2025| website=silverandblackpride.com| date=September 2, 2020| author=Kenneth Arthur}}</ref> He was able to earn the last roster spot as the sixth cornerback after [[Nevin Lawson]] was suspended.<ref>{{cite web| title=Raiders cornerback battles to continue right up until cutdown date| url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/raiders/2020/08/25/raiders-cornerback-battles-to-continue-right-up-until-start-of-cutdown-date/80232221007/| access-date=May 14, 2025| website=raiderswire.usatoday.com| date=August 25, 2020| author=Levi Damien}}</ref> 

He was inactive as a healthy scratch for the first three games (Weeks 1–3) of the [[2020 NFL season]]. On October 4, 2020, Robertson made his professional regular season debut and recorded two combined tackles (one solo) as the Raiders lost 23–30 to the [[2020 Buffalo Bills season|Buffalo Bills]]. On December 13, 2020, the Las Vegas Raiders fired defensive coordinator [[Paul Guenther (American football)|Paul Guenther]] following a 44–27 loss against the [[2020 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] in Week 14. Former [[2019 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys']] defensive line coach [[Rod Marinelli]] was appointed interim defensive coordinator. He finished his rookie season with only four combined tackles (three solo) in eight games without earning a start.<ref>{{cite web| title=Amik Robertson game logs (2020)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAm00.htm |access-date=May 15, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

====2021====
On January 12, 2021, the [[2021 Las Vegas Raiders season|Las Vegas Raiders]] announced their decision to hire [[Gus Bradley]] to be their defensive coordinator.<ref name="i293">{{cite web |last=Simmons |first=Myles |title=Raiders hire Gus Bradley as defensive coordinator |work=NBC Sports |date=2021-01-12 |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/nfl/profootballtalk/rumor-mill/news/raiders-hire-gus-bradley-as-defensive-coordinator |access-date=2025-01-28}}</ref> During training camp, he competed for the role as the starting nickelback against [[Nate Hobbs]], [[Rasul Douglas]], and [[Nevin Lawson]] following the departure of [[Lamarcus Joyner]]. Head coach Jon Gruden named Robertson a backup and listed him as the fifth cornerback on the depth chart to begin the regular season, behind Trayvon Mullen, [[Casey Hayward]], Damon Arnette, and Nate Hobbs.<ref>{{cite web| title=Raiders depth chart 2021: Las Vegas' projected Week 1 starters after roster cuts| url=https://www.cbssports.com/nfl/news/raiders-depth-chart-2021-las-vegas-projected-week-1-starters-after-roster-cuts/| access-date=May 14, 2025| website=cbssports.com| date=September 2, 2021| author=Jordan Dajani}}</ref>

In Week 4, Robertson set a season-high with seven combined tackles (six solo) during a 14–21 loss at the [[2021 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]]. On October 10, 2021, Robertson earned his first career start after Damon Arnette and Trayvon Mullen suffered injuries rendering them inactive. He recorded seven combined tackles (five solo) as the Raiders lost 9–30 against the [[2021 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]]. The following day, head coach Jon Gruden announced his resignation amid multiple controversies. Special teams coordinator [[Rich Bisaccia]] was appointed to interim head coach. He finished the [[2021 NFL season]] with only 19 combined tackles (14 solo) in ten games and two starts.

====2022====
On January 31, 2022, the [[2022 Las Vegas Raiders season|Las Vegas Raiders]] hired [[Josh McDaniels]] to be their head coach.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 31, 2022 |title=Raiders announce Josh McDaniels as next Head Coach |url=https://www.raiders.com/news/raiders-hire-josh-mcdaniels-as-head-coach |access-date=January 31, 2022 |work=[[Las Vegas Raiders]]}}</ref> Throughout training camp, he competed against Trayvon Mullen, Nate Hobbs, and [[Rock Ya-Sin]] for a role as a starting cornerback under new defensive coordinator [[Patrick Graham (American football)|Patrick Graham]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Amik Robertson on battle to make the Las Vegas Raiders| url=https://www.si.com/nfl/raiders/the-black-hole-plus/amik-robertson-davante-adams-hunter-renfrow-las-vegas-raider| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=SI.com| date=August 19, 2022| author=Hondo Carpenter}}</ref> Head coach Josh McDaniels named him a backup and listed him as the fourth cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind Nate Hobbs, Rock Ya-Sin, and [[Anthony Averett]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Raiders release first depth chart of 2022 regular season: 10 observations| url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/raiders/2022/09/06/raiders-release-first-depth-chart-of-2022-regular-season-10-observations/80017584007/| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=raiderswire.usatoday.com| date=September 6, 2022| author=Levi Damien}}</ref> 

On September 18, 2022, Robertson earned his first start of the season as a nickelback and made four solo tackles, one pass deflection, and had his first career interception on a pass attempt thrown by [[Kyler Murray]] to wide receiver [[Marquise Brown]] during a 29–23 loss against the [[2022 Arizona Cardinals season|Arizona Cardinals]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Arizona Cardinals at Las Vegas Raiders - September 18th, 2022| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202209180rai.htm| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> On October 2, 2022, Robertson recorded three combined tackles (two solo) and returned a fumble recovery that was forced by [[Duron Harmon]] by running back [[Melvin Gordon]] for 68–yards to score his first career touchdown during a 32–23 victory against the [[2022 Denver Broncos season|Denver Broncos]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Denver Broncos at Las Vegas Raiders - October 2nd, 2022| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202210020rai.htm| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> In Week 10, he set a season-high with six combined tackles (three solo), made one pass deflection, and recovered a fumble as the Raiders lost 20–25 against the [[2022 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]]. In Week 14, he recorded three solo tackles and had his first career sack on [[Baker Mayfield]] for a one–yard loss during a 16–17 loss at the [[2022 Los Angeles Rams season|Los Angeles Rams]]. The following week, Robertson recorded one solo tackle and set a season-high with three pass deflections as the Raiders defeated the [[2022 New England Patriots season|New England Patriots]] 30–24 in Week 15. On January 1, 2023, Robertson recorded two solo tackles, made one pass deflection, and set a career-high with his second interception of the season on a pass by [[Brock Purdy]] to tight end [[George Kittle]] during a 34–37 overtime loss to the [[2022 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]]. He finished the season with 38 combined tackles (29 solo), nine pass deflections, two interceptions, two sacks, one forced fumble, a fumble recovery, and a touchdown, while appearing in all 17 games with seven starts.<ref name="career">{{cite web| title=Pro-Football-Reference: Amik Robertson Career Overview| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAm00.htm| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref>

====2023====
He entered training camp as a possible candidate to earn a role as a starting cornerback, but had to compete against Nate Hobbs, [[Brandon Facyson]], [[David Long (defensive back)|David Long]], [[Duke Shelley]], [[Jakorian Bennett]], and [[Tyler Hall (American football)|Tyler Hall]]<ref>{{cite web| title=Raiders' Position Battles to Watch Ahead of 2023 NFL Season| url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10077531-raiders-position-battles-to-watch-ahead-of-2023-nfl-season| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=bleacherreport.com| date=May 29, 2023}}</ref> He also competed to earn the role as the primary backup nickelback against Tyler Hall.<ref>{{cite web| title=Cornerback position among the most competitive camp battles for Raiders| url=https://raiderswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nfl/raiders/2023/08/08/cornerback-position-among-the-most-competitive-camp-battles-for-raiders/79948453007/| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=raiderswire.usatoday.com| date=August 8, 2023| author=Marcus Mosher}}</ref> Head coach Josh McDaniels named him a backup and listed him as the fourth cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind [[Marcus Peters]], Nate Hobbs, and Jakorion Bennett.

He was promoted to the No. 2 starting cornerback after Nate Hobbs injured his ankle and was rendered inactive for four consecutive games. In Week 5, Robertson made two combined tackles (one solo), a pass deflection, and sealed the Raiders' 17–13 victory against the [[2023 Green Bay Packers season|Green Bay Packers]] by intercepting a pass thrown by [[Jordan Love]] to wide receiver [[Christian Watson]] with 51 seconds left in the game. On October 31, 2023, the Las Vegas Raiders fired head coach Josh McDaniels after they began the season with a 3–5 record. They appointed linebackers coach [[Antonio Pierce]] to interim head coach for the remainder of the season. In Week 9, Robertson recorded three solo tackles, set a season-high with two pass deflections, and intercepted a pass by [[Tommy DeVito (American football)|Tommy DeVito]] to wide receiver [[Jalin Hyatt]] as the Raiders defeated the [[2023 New York Giants season|New York Giants]] 6–30.<ref>{{cite web| title=New York Giants at Las Vegas Raiders - November 5th, 2023| url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202311050rai.htm| access-date=May 16, 2022| website=pro-football-reference.com}}</ref> Interim head coach Antonio Pierce demoted Robertson for two games (Weeks 11–12) and replaced him with Marcus Peters until benching Peters during their 17–31 loss to the [[2023 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] in Week 12.<ref>{{cite web| title=Amik Robertson game logs (2023)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAm00.htm |access-date=May 15, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He re-gained his role as a starting cornerback and remained a starter for the last five games (Weeks 14–18) of the season. On November 27, 2023, the Raiders waived Marcus Peters. He finished the [[2023 NFL season]] with a total of 50 combined tackles (38 solo), six pass deflections, two interceptions, and one sack in 17 games and 11 starts.<ref name="career"/> He received an overall grade of 63.4 from Pro Football Focus in 2023.<ref>{{cite web| title=Updated 2024 NFL roster rankings: Strengths, weaknesses and X factors for every starting lineup| url=https://www.pff.com/news/nfl-roster-rankings-all-32-teams-2024-strengths-weaknesses-x-factors| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=PFF.com| author=Jim Wyman| date=September 3, 2024}}</ref>

===Detroit Lions===
On March 14, 2024, the [[Detroit Lions]] signed Robertson to a two–year, $9.25 million contract that includes $4.50 million guaranteed upon signing and an initial signing bonus of $3.30 million.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wyatt |first=Jim |date=March 14, 2024 |title=Lions sign unrestricted free agents OLB Marcus Davenport and CB Amik Robertson|url=https://www.detroitlions.com/news/lions-sign-unrestricted-free-agents-olb-marcus-davenport-and-cb-amik-robertson|access-date=March 14, 2024 |website=DetroitLions.com}}</ref> He joined a new group of cornerbacks that the Lions had recently acquired following the departure of all of their former starting cornerbacks, including [[Cameron Sutton]], [[Jerry Jacobs (American football)|Jerry Jacobs]], and [[Will Harris (American football)|Will Harris]]. 

Under defensive coordinator [[Aaron Glenn]], he competed to earn a role as a primary cornerback, against [[Emmanuel Moseley]] and [[2024 NFL draft|2024]] first-round pick (24th overall) [[Terrion Arnold]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Detroit Lions 2024 training camp preview: Breaking down the overhauled CB room| url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2024/7/17/24198858/detroit-lions-2024-training-camp-preview-breaking-down-the-overhauled-cb-room| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=prideofdetroit.com| author=Erik Schlitt| date=July 17, 2024}}</ref> Head coach [[Dan Campbell]] named him the starting nickelback and listed him as the third cornerback on the depth chart to begin the season, behind starters [[Carlton Davis]] and Terrion Arnold.<ref>{{cite web| title=Detroit Lions updated 2024 depth chart: Week 1 vs. Rams on 'SNF'| url=https://www.prideofdetroit.com/2024/9/8/24234576/detroit-lions-updated-2024-depth-chart-week-1-los-angeles-rams-snf| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=prideofdetroit.com| author=Erik Schlitt| date=September 8, 2024}}</ref>

On September 30, 2024, Robertson set a season-high with eight solo tackles and made two pass deflections as the Lions defeated the [[2024 Seattle Seahawks season|Seattle Seahawks]] 42–29. In Week 15, No. 1 starting cornerback Carlton Davis suffered a fractured jaw and was placed on injured reserve for the remainder of the season. Robertson was subsequently promoted to being a starting cornerback for the last three games (Weeks 16–18) of the season. In Week 16, he earned his first start as an starting outside cornerback with the Lions and recorded eight combined tackles (five solo) and tied his season-high of two pass deflections during a 34–17 victory at the [[2024 Chicago Bears season|Chicago Bears]].<ref>{{cite web| title=Amik Robertson game logs (2024)|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RobeAm00.htm |access-date=May 15, 2025| website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref> He finished the season with a total of 50 combined tackles (40 solo), made eight pass deflections, and led the team with three forced fumbles, while appearing in all 17 games with four starts.<ref name="career"/> He received an overall grade of 64.5 from [[Pro Football Focus]], which ranked 87th amongst 222 qualifying cornerbacks in 2024.<ref name="PFF">{{cite web| title=Pro Football Focus: Amik Robertson| url=https://www.pff.com/nfl/players/amik-robertson/55619| access-date=May 16, 2025| website=PFF.com}}</ref>

The [[2024 Detroit Lions season|Detroit Lions]] finished the [[2024 NFL season]] a top the [[NFC North]] with a 15–2 record and earned a first-round bye. On January 18, 2025, Robertson started in his first career postseason appearance and was limited to one solo tackle and only two snaps on defense, before exiting the game in the beginning of the first quarter after suffering a broken arm as the Lions lost 31–45 against the [[2024 Washington Commanders season|Washington Commanders]] in the NFC Divisional Round. He would undergo surgery for his broken arm.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Lions' Amik Robertson breaks arm in playoff loss to Commanders|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/43472193/amik-robertson-exits-commanders-lions-elbow-injury|access-date=February 1, 2025|website=espn.com|date=January 19, 2025 |language=en}}</ref>

===Washington Commanders===
Robertson signed a two-year, $16 million contract with the [[Washington Commanders]] on March 12, 2026.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Commanders sign CB Amik Robertson|url=https://www.commanders.com/news/commanders-sign-cb-amik-robertson|website=commanders.com|date=March 12, 2026 |language=en}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Robertson credits the adversity he faced in his early life and his faith as motivations for his success. His mother Kima was 15 when he was born.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Writer |first=Chris Singleton Staff |title='They've always had my back': Local NFL draft prospect developed 'warrior' mentality from family |url=https://www.houmatoday.com/story/sports/college/2020/04/19/theyve-always-had-my-back-local-nfl-draft-prospect-developed-warrior-mentality-from-family/1323918007/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=The Courier |language=en-US}}</ref> His father, Arthur Watts was incarcerated for the first five years of Robertson's life, re-entering his son's life when Robertson was 11. Robertson became a father at age 15 when his son Aiden Miguel was born on August 18, 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Diaz |first=Cory |title=Meek Amik: How life changed, made star LA Tech corner grow up fast |url=https://www.thenewsstar.com/story/sports/college/louisiana-tech/2018/03/16/meek-amik-how-life-changed-made-star-la-tech-corner-grow-up-fast/432925002/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=The News-Star |language=en-US}}</ref>

'''Amari Jai Rodgers''' (born September 23, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[wide receiver]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Clemson Tigers football|Clemson]] and was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the third round of the [[2021 NFL draft]]. He has also played for the [[Houston Texans]] and [[Indianapolis Colts]], and in the [[United Football League (2024–present)|United Football League]] for the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]].

==Early life==
Rodgers attended [[Knoxville Catholic High School]] in [[Knoxville, Tennessee]].  As a senior, he caught 40 passes for 1,238 yards with 18 touchdowns. For his career, he had 3,498 receiving yards with 47 total touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Oliver |first=Gavin |date=July 4, 2017 |title=Fresh look at the freshmen: Amari Rodgers |url=https://theclemsoninsider.com/2017/07/04/fresh-look-at-the-freshmen-amari-rodgers/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170706215954/http://theclemsoninsider.com:80/2017/07/04/fresh-look-at-the-freshmen-amari-rodgers/ |archive-date=July 6, 2017 |access-date=April 16, 2020 |website=The Clemson Insider}}</ref> He was rated as a four star recruit and the 16th highest rated wide receiver recruit in the country by the [[247Sports.com]] Composite, which aggregates the ratings of the major recruiting services.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Rodgers, Knoxville Catholic, Wide Receiver |url=https://247sports.com/Player/Amari-Rodgers-36512/high-school-60220// |access-date=April 16, 2020 |website=[[247Sports.com]]}}</ref> Rodgers originally committed to [[USC Trojans football|University of Southern California]], but flipped to Clemson when they gave him an offer late in the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Keepfer |first=Scott |date=July 22, 2019 |title=Meet the Tigers: 3 things you probably don't know about Clemson football's Amari Rodgers |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/clemson/2019/07/22/amari-rodgers-3-things-you-may-not-know-clemson-football-wide-receiver/1499163001// |access-date=April 16, 2020 |website=[[USA Today]]}}</ref>

==College career==
As a freshman at Clemson in 2017, Rodgers had 19 receptions for 123 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 23, 2018 |title=2018 Clemson Football Season Preview: Wide Receivers |url=https://www.shakinthesouthland.com/2018/8/23/17761504/2018-clemson-football-season-preview-wide-receivers |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190806141305/https://www.shakinthesouthland.com/2018/8/23/17761504/2018-clemson-football-season-preview-wide-receivers |archive-date=August 6, 2019 |access-date=April 16, 2020 |website=[[SB Nation]]}}</ref> As a sophomore in 2018, he caught 55 passes for 575 yards and 4 touchdowns. He also returned a punt for a touchdown.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Player Stats: Amari Rodgers |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=http://stats.washingtonpost.com/cfb/players.asp?id=276271 |url-status=live |access-date=April 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201024025638/http://stats.washingtonpost.com/cfb/players.asp?id=276271 |archive-date=October 24, 2020}}</ref>

Rodgers missed the first game of his junior season in 2019 due to an [[ACL tear]] in spring practice.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Needelman |first=Joshua |date=September 10, 2019 |title=Clemson's Amari Rodgers to Dabo Swinney: 'I promise you, I'm ready |url=https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/clemson/clemson-s-amari-rodgers-to-dabo-swinney-i-promise-you/article_22e40274-d3e6-11e9-84af-2fa84b8ee47f.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210501040302/https://www.postandcourier.com/sports/clemson/clemson-s-amari-rodgers-to-dabo-swinney-i-promise-you/article_22e40274-d3e6-11e9-84af-2fa84b8ee47f.html |archive-date=May 1, 2021 |access-date=April 16, 2020 |website=[[The Post and Courier]]}}</ref> He finished the season with 30 receptions, 426 yards, and 4 touchdowns.<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 16, 2020 |title=WATCH: Amari Rodgers motivated to show out as senior |url=https://www.tigernet.com/update/WATCH-Amari-Rodgers-motivated-to-show-out-as-senior-35332 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210501040259/https://www.tigernet.com/update/WATCH-Amari-Rodgers-motivated-to-show-out-as-senior-35332 |archive-date=May 1, 2021 |access-date=April 16, 2020 |website=Tigernet.com}}</ref> After the season, Rodgers announced he was returning for his senior season rather than entering the [[2020 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite magazine |last=Senkiw |first=Brad |date=March 25, 2020 |title=Clemson's Amari Rodgers Reflects On Being Year Removed From Knee Injury |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |url=https://www.si.com/college/clemson/football/clemsons-amari-rodgers-reflects-on-being-year-removed-from-knee-injury |access-date=July 31, 2020}}</ref> As a senior, Rodgers caught 77 passes for 1,020 yards and 7 touchdowns.
