===Green Bay Packers===
Rodgers was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the third round with the 85th overall pick of the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hodkiewicz |first=Wes |date=April 30, 2021 |title=2021 NFL Draft: Packers select Clemson WR Amari Rodgers in the third round, No. 85 overall |url=https://www.packers.com/news/2021-nfl-draft-packers-select-clemson-wr-amari-rodgers |access-date=April 30, 2021 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> The Packers send their 92nd and 135th overall picks to the [[Tennessee Titans]] to move up and select Rodgers. He signed his four-year rookie contract on July 23, 2021,<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 23, 2021 |title=Packers sign WR Amari Rodgers |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-wr-amari-rodgers |access-date=July 23, 2021 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> worth $4.89 million, including a $923,000 signing bonus.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Rodgers |url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/green-bay-packers/amari-rodgers-72465/ |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=Spotrac.com}}</ref> He saw his first NFL action on September 12, 2021, against the [[2021 New Orleans Saints season|New Orleans Saints]], recording one catch for 19 yards in the 38–3 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Green Bay Packers at New Orleans Saints - September 12th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202109120nor.htm |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> He finished the 2021 season with 169 yards off punt returns and 199 yards off kickoff returns with his longest being 23 and 27 yards.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Rodgers 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RodgAm00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2021 NFL Kick & Punt Returns |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/2021/returns.htm |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

During Rodgers' second season, he proved to be inconsistent, totaling five fumbled punt returns over ten games. However, he was otherwise more efficient by nearing his 2021 totals in just over half a season, returning 139 yards off punt returns and 122 off kickoffs through week 10. In a week 10 win over the [[2022 Dallas Cowboys season|Dallas Cowboys]], Rodgers lost his seventh fumble during a punt return, and was benched afterwards, replaced by cornerback [[Keisean Nixon]]. Head coach [[Matt LaFleur]] announced they would no longer ask Rodgers to return punts, and he was released by the Packers two days after the game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Rodgers Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RodgAm00.htm |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=November 15, 2022 |title=Packers release WR Amari Rodgers, RB Kylin Hill |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-release-wr-amari-rodgers-rb-kylin-hill-2022 |access-date=November 15, 2022 |website=Packers.com |language=en-US}}</ref> Meanwhile, in his stead, Nixon was named a First-Team [[All-Pro]] as a kick returner, having tallied the most return yards in the NFL despite not winning the job until Week 10.

===Houston Texans===
The [[Houston Texans]] claimed Rodgers off waivers on November 16, 2022.<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2022 |title=Texans' Amari Rodgers: Picked up by Houston |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/texans-amari-rodgers-picked-up-by-houston/amp/ |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=[[CBS Sports]]}}</ref> On December 11, Rodgers scored his first career touchdown on a 28–yard reception from [[Jeff Driskel]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Senkiw  |first=Brad  |date=December 11, 2022 |title=Former Clemson WR Scores First Career NFL TD |url=https://www.si.com/college/clemson/tigers-in-the-nfl/former-clemson-wr-scores-first-career-nfl-td |access-date=September 23, 2023 |website=SI.com |language=en}}</ref> Rodgers finished the 2022 season with 16 receptions for 204 receiving yards and one receiving touchdown.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amari Rodgers 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RodgAm00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=May 29, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

On July 30, 2023, Rodgers was waived by the [[Houston Texans]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Houston Texans Transactions (7-30-2023)|url=https://www.houstontexans.com/news/houston-texans-transactions-7-30-2023|website=HoustonTexans.com|date=July 30, 2023}}</ref>

===Indianapolis Colts===
On August 2, 2023, Rodgers signed with the [[Indianapolis Colts]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts sign WR Amari Rodgers, waive WR Johnny King|url=https://www.colts.com/news/amari-rodgers-signed-green-bay-packers-draft-pick-houston-texans|website=Colts.com|date=August 2, 2023}}</ref> He was waived on August 29, 2023, and re-signed to the [[practice squad]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts make roster moves to form initial 53-man roster|url=https://www.colts.com/news/jonathan-taylor-reserve-pup-list-roster-moves-transactions-53-man-roster|author=Stankevitz, JJ|website=Colts.com|date=August 29, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Colts sign 16 to practice squad|url=https://www.colts.com/news/practice-squad-mike-strachan-amari-rodgers-juwann-winfree-signed-wide-receiver|website=Colts.com|date=August 30, 2023}}</ref> On October 3, Rodgers was signed to the active roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts sign WR Amari Rodgers to the 53-man roster; place cornerback Dallis Flowers on Injured Reserve; sign cornerback Darren Hall to the practice squad|url=https://www.colts.com/news/colts-sign-wr-amari-rodgers-to-the-53-man-roster-place-cornerback-dallis-flowers|website=Colts.com|date=October 3, 2023}}</ref> He was waived on October 20, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Colts claim CB Ameer Speed off waivers from Patriots; waive WR Amari Rodgers|url=https://www.colts.com/news/ameer-speed-claimed-waivers-defensive-back-cornerback-patriots|website=Colts.com|date=October 20, 2023}}</ref>

=== Birmingham Stallions ===
On December 22, 2023, Rodgers signed with the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United States Football League (2022–2023)|United States Football League]] (USFL).<ref>{{cite tweet |number=1738409863611314379 |user=JamesLarsenPFN |title=According to the FOX Sports roster page, the @USFLStallions have also added WR Amari Rodgers out of Clemson. |date=December 22, 2023 |access-date=December 22, 2023}}</ref> He re-signed with the team on September 23, 2024.<ref>{{cite tweet |user=UFL_PR |title=The #UFL has announced the following transactions |number=1838337550005707004 |date=September 23, 2024 |access-date=September 24, 2024}}</ref>

Rodgers had been left unprotected in the [[2026 UFL draft]] and claimed by the [[Columbus Aviators]]. Refusing to report to the Aviators, Rodgers instead announced his retirement on January 14, 2026, joining several of his Stallions teammates who had severed ties with the UFL that offseason.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rifino |first=Patrick |date=2026-01-14 |title=Jaryd Jones-Smith, Kai Nacua, and Amari Rodgers Among UFL Players Opting for Retirement Prior to UFL Season |url=https://uflnewshub.com/ufl/jaryd-jones-smith-kai-nacua-and-amari-rodgers-among-ufl-players-opting-for-retirement-prior-to-ufl-season/ |access-date=2026-01-14 |language=en-US}}</ref>

Bledsoe was signed by the [[Tennessee Titans]] as an undrafted free agent on April 27, 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://titanswire.usatoday.com/2019/04/27/former-oklahoma-de-amani-bledsoe-signing-with-titans/|title=Former Oklahoma DE Amani Bledsoe signing with Titans|first=Chrissy|last=Ford|website=Titans Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=April 27, 2019|access-date=September 18, 2020}}</ref> He was waived during final roster cuts and then re-signed to the team's practice squad, where he remained for the rest of the season. The Titans waived Bledsoe on July 26, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/nfl/titans/2020/07/26/titans-cut-six-players-trimming-roster-81-nfl-training-camp/5515307002/|title=Titans cut six players, trimming roster to 81|work=[[The Tennessean]]|date=July 26, 2020|access-date=September 18, 2020}}</ref>

===Cincinnati Bengals===
[[File:Amani Bledsoe (2020) (cropped).jpg|thumb|Bledsoe with Cincinnati in 2020]]
Bledsoe was signed by the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] on August 15, 2020.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://profootballtalk.nbcsports.com/2020/08/15/bengals-sign-amani-bledsoe/|title=Bengals sign Amani Bledsoe|first=Charean|last=Williams|website=[[Profootballtalk.com]]|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|date=August 15, 2020|access-date=September 18, 2020}}</ref> Bledsoe was waived during final roster cuts on September 5, and signed to the team's practice squad the next day.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Reduce 2020 Roster To 53 Players|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-reduce-2020-roster-to-53-players|website=Bengals.com|date=September 5, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Establish Practice Squad|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-establish-practice-squad-x0373|website=Bengals.com|date=September 6, 2020|access-date=September 19, 2020|archive-date=September 29, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200929052540/https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-establish-practice-squad-x0373|url-status=dead}}</ref> He was elevated to the active roster for the season opener against the [[2020 Los Angeles Chargers season|Los Angeles Chargers]] on September 13,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cincyjungle.com/2020/9/12/21434150/bengals-elevate-amani-bledsoe-and-trayvon-henderson-from-practice-squad-to-active-roster|title=Bengals elevate Amani Bledsoe and Trayvon Henderson to active roster|first=John|last=Sheeran|website=CincyJungle.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=September 12, 2020|access-date=September 18, 2020}}</ref> and reverted to the practice squad the next day. Bledsoe was promoted to the active roster on September 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/bengals-amani-bledsoe-gets-week-2-promotion/|title=Bengals' Amani Bledsoe: Gets Week 2 promotion|website=[[CBSSports.com]]|publisher=[[RotoWire]]|date=September 15, 2020|access-date=September 18, 2020}}</ref> He was placed on the reserve/[[COVID-19]] list by the team on December 6,<ref>{{cite news |title=Bengals Place Amani Bledsoe On Reserve/COVID-19 list; Elevated Kahlil McKenzie From Practice Squad |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-place-amani-bledsoe-on-reserve-covid-19-list-elevated-kahlil-mckenzie-fr |website=Bengals.com |date=December 6, 2020 |access-date=January 14, 2021 |archive-date=December 11, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201211095248/https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-place-amani-bledsoe-on-reserve-covid-19-list-elevated-kahlil-mckenzie-fr |url-status=dead }}</ref> and activated on December 16.<ref>{{cite news |title=Geno Atkins Placed On Reserve/Injured List, Amani Bledsoe Back To Active Roster |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/geno-atkins-placed-on-reserve-injured-list-amani-bledsoe-back-to-active-roster |website=Bengals.com |date=December 16, 2020 |access-date=January 14, 2021}}</ref>

Bledsoe re-signed on a one-year contract with the Bengals on March 31, 2021.<ref>{{cite news |title=Amani Bledsoe Re-Signs With The Bengals |url=https://www.bengals.com/news/amani-bledsoe-re-signs-with-the-bengals |website=Bengals.com |date=March 31, 2021 |access-date=March 31, 2021}}</ref> He was waived by Cincinnati prior to the start of the regular season on August 31.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bengals Reduce 2021 Roster To 53 Players|url=https://www.bengals.com/news/bengals-reduce-2021-roster-to-53-players|website=Bengals.com|date=August 31, 2021}}</ref>

===Tennessee Titans (second stint)===
On September 2, 2021, Bledsoe was signed to the Tennessee Titans' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Place Three Players on Injured Reserve While Waiving TE Luke Stocker|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-place-three-players-on-injured-reserve-while-waiving-te-luke-stocker|website=tennesseetitans.com|date=September 2, 2021|access-date=September 2, 2021}}</ref> He was promoted to the active roster on October 8.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Titans Place Four Players on Injured Reserve, Promote Three to Active Roster|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/roster-moves-titans-place-four-players-on-injured-reserve-promote-three-to-activ|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=October 8, 2021|access-date=October 9, 2021|archive-date=October 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211009025504/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/roster-moves-titans-place-four-players-on-injured-reserve-promote-three-to-activ|url-status=dead}}</ref> Bledsoe was waived on November 15 and re-signed to the practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Roster Moves: Titans Waive OL Bobby Hart, DL Amani Bledsoe|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/roster-moves-titans-waive-ol-bobby-hart-dl-amani-bledsoe|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=November 15, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Titans Sign DL Kyle Peko to Active Roster, Move TE Tommy Hudson to "Designated for Return from Injured Reserve" List|url=https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-dl-kyle-peko-to-active-roster-move-te-tommy-hudson-to-designated-for|author=Wyatt, Jim|website=TennesseeTitans.com|date=November 17, 2021|access-date=November 19, 2021|archive-date=January 28, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230128172612/https://www.tennesseetitans.com/news/titans-sign-dl-kyle-peko-to-active-roster-move-te-tommy-hudson-to-designated-for|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He signed a reserve/future contract with Atlanta on January 9, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|title=Falcons sign 18 players to Reserve/Future contracts|url=https://www.atlantafalcons.com/news/falcons-sign-18-players-to-reserve-future-contracts|author=Deighton, John|website=AtlantaFalcons.com|date=January 9, 2023}}</ref> Bledsoe was waived by the Falcons on April 14.<ref>{{cite tweet|user=ScottBairNFL|number=1646968177161654289|title=Official Atlanta Falcons moves from Friday. '''Ambry Thomas''' (born September 9, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[cornerback]] for the [[Philadelphia Eagles]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Michigan Wolverines football|Michigan Wolverines]] and was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the third round of the [[2021 NFL draft]]. Thomas has also been a member of the [[Indianapolis Colts]] and [[Minnesota Vikings]].

==Early life==
Thomas attended [[Martin Luther King High School (Detroit)|Martin Luther King High School]] in [[Detroit, Michigan]]. He played [[wide receiver]] and cornerback. Thomas played in the 2017 [[U.S. Army All-American Bowl]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Farrell |first=Perry A. |date=September 22, 2016 |title=Detroit King star Ambry Thomas to play in Army All-American bowl |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2016/detroit-king-star-ambry-thomas-to-play-in-army-allamerican-bowl |access-date=May 24, 2023 |website=USA TODAY High School Sports |language=en-US}}</ref> He committed to the [[University of Michigan]] to play [[college football]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Snyder |first=Mark |date=December 7, 2016 |title=Detroit King star DB Ambry Thomas commits to Michigan |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2016/12/07/michigan-football-ambry-thomas/95124070/ |access-date=May 23, 2023 |website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Lorenz |first=Steve |date=December 8, 2016 |title=King's Ambry Thomas wanted to accept Jim Harbaugh's challenge |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2016/12/08/michigan-football-ambry-thomas/95160536/ |access-date=May 23, 2023 |website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref>

==College career==
Thomas spent his first two years at Michigan in 2017 and 2018 as a backup, recording 16 tackles and an [[interception]] during the two years. Prior to the 2019 season, Thomas spent a month in the hospital after being diagnosed with [[colitis]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sang |first=Orion |date=September 17, 2019 |title=Why Michigan football's Ambry Thomas thought he'd have to 'sit out this year' |url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2019/09/17/michigan-football-ambry-thomas-colitis/2346925001/ |access-date=May 23, 2023 |website=Detroit Free Press}}</ref> After believing that he would have to sit out the year due to the condition, Thomas returned and became a starter for the first time.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Zuke |first=Ryan |date=September 16, 2019 |title=How Michigan’s Ambry Thomas went from longshot to playing in 2019 to starting Week 1 |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2019/09/how-michigans-ambry-thomas-went-from-longshot-to-playing-in-2019-to-starting-role.html |access-date=May 23, 2023 |website=mlive.com}}</ref> He started all 13 games and had 38 tackles and three interceptions that season. Thomas opted out of the 2020 season and entered the [[2021 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=VanHaaren |first=Tom |date=August 21, 2020 |title=Wolverines CB Thomas declares for NFL draft |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/29707468/michigan-cb-ambry-thomas-declares-nfl-draft |access-date=May 24, 2023 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McMann |first=Aaron |date=March 24, 2021 |title=Michigan’s Ambry Thomas confident in NFL ability: ‘I’m a top-5 cornerback’ |url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2021/03/michigans-ambry-thomas-confident-in-nfl-ability-im-a-top-5-cornerback.html |access-date=May 23, 2023 |website=mlive.com}}</ref>

===San Francisco 49ers===

==== 2021 season ====
Thomas was selected by the [[San Francisco 49ers]] in the third round (102nd overall) of the 2021 NFL draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Posey |first=Kyle |date=April 30, 2021 |title=Pick No. 102: 49ers select Michigan CB Ambry Thomas |url=https://www.ninersnation.com/2021/4/30/22413582/pick-no-102-49ers-select-michigan-cb-ambry-thomas |access-date=May 24, 2023 |website=Niners Nation |language=en}}</ref> He signed his four-year rookie contract on July 26, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 26, 2021 |title=49ers Sign CB Ambry Thomas to a Four-Year Deal; Release DL |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-cb-ambry-thomas-to-a-four-year-deal-release-dl |access-date=July 27, 2021 |website=49ers.com}}</ref>

Thomas made his NFL debut in the season-opener against the [[Detroit Lions]] and finished the 41–33 road victory with two tackles.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Detroit Lions - September 12th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202109120det.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During Week 14 against the [[Cincinnati Bengals]], Thomas recorded a season-high six tackles in 26[[2021–22 NFL playoffs|–]]23 overtime road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Cincinnati Bengals - December 12th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202112120cin.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Atlanta Falcons]], he had two tackles and a pass deflection during the 31[[2021–22 NFL playoffs|–]]13 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Atlanta Falcons at San Francisco 49ers - December 19th, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202112190sfo.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

During a Week 16 20–17 road loss to the [[Tennessee Titans]] on ''[[Thursday Night Football]]'', Thomas recorded a tackle and two pass deflections.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Tennessee Titans - December 23rd, 2021 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202112230oti.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the next game against the [[Houston Texans]], he had four tackles and a pass deflection during the 23–7 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Houston Texans at San Francisco 49ers - January 2nd, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201020sfo.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During the regular-season finale on the road against the [[Los Angeles Rams]], Thomas recorded a pass deflection and his first career interception off of quarterback [[Matthew Stafford]] in overtime with the 49ers leading 27–24, sending the 49ers to the playoffs.<ref>{{Cite web |date=January 9, 2022 |title=49ers clinch playoff berth by holding off Rams 27-24 in OT |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/recap?gameId=401326599 |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=ESPN |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=McDonald |first=Briana |date=January 11, 2022 |title=Making Skeptics Believers: Ambry Thomas' Tough Road to Storybook Ending |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/ambry-thomas-rookie-49ers-rams-interception-postseason-playoffs-cornerback |access-date=January 12, 2022 |website=49ers.com}}</ref>

Thomas finished his rookie year with 23 tackles, five pass deflections, and an interception in 12 games and five starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ambry Thomas 2021 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThomAm00/gamelog/2021/ |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs#NFC: San Francisco 49ers 23, Dallas Cowboys 17|Wild Card Round]] against the [[Dallas Cowboys]], Thomas made his postseason debut and finished the 23–17 road victory with three tackles and a pass deflection.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Wild Card - San Francisco 49ers at Dallas Cowboys - January 16th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201160dal.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During the [[2021–22 NFL playoffs#NFC Championship: Los Angeles Rams 20, San Francisco 49ers 17|NFC Championship Game]] against the Rams, Thomas had a team-high 13 tackles in the 20–17 road loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship - San Francisco 49ers at Los Angeles Rams - January 30th, 2022 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202201300ram.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2022 season ====
In 2022, Thomas struggled during preseason [[training camp (NFL)|training camp]] and was in danger of missing the final 53-man roster due to injury and the rise to prominence of rookie cornerbacks [[Deommodore Lenoir]] and [[Samuel Womack]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sanchez III |first=Luis Sanchez |date=August 23, 2022 |title=Ambry Thomas Making the 49ers Final 53–man Roster Looks Bleak |url=https://www.si.com/nfl/49ers/news/ambry-thomas-making-49ers-final-53-man-roster-looks-bleak |access-date=December 17, 2023 |website=SI.com}}</ref> Although he made the final roster,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Pallares |first=Lindsey |date=August 30, 2022 |title=Position-by-Position Breakdown of the 49ers Initial 2022 53–Man Roster |url=https://www.49ers.com/news/position-breakdown-49ers-2022-53-man-roster-lance-bosa-garoppolo-ward-kittle |access-date=December 17, 2023 |website=49ers.com}}</ref> Thomas played just 47 defensive snaps over the course of the season and did not play in the playoffs due to an ankle injury.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Branch |first=Eric |date=August 7, 2023 |title=49ers' Ambry Thomas, candid and humbled, takes blame for lost year |url=https://www.sfchronicle.com/sports/49ers/article/happened-49ers-ambry-thomas-lost-second-season-18282808.php |access-date=December 17, 2023 |website=SFChronicle.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=2022 San Francisco 49ers Injuries |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2022_injuries.htm |access-date=December 17, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

Thomas finished his second professional season with 13 tackles in 15 games and no starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ambry Thomas 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThomAm00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

==== 2023 season ====
During the season-opener against the [[Pittsburgh Steelers]], Thomas recorded five tackles and a pass deflection in the 30–7 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Pittsburgh Steelers - September 10th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202309100pit.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During a Week 10 34–3 road victory over the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], he had three tackles, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Jacksonville Jaguars - November 12th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202311120jax.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Two weeks later against the [[Seattle Seahawks]] on [[NFL on Thanksgiving Day|Thanksgiving]], Thomas recorded a tackle, two pass deflections, and an interception in the 31–13 road victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Seattle Seahawks - November 23rd, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202311230sea.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

During a Week 13 42–19 road victory over the [[Philadelphia Eagles]], Thomas set season-highs in tackles with seven and pass deflections with three.<ref>{{Cite web |title=San Francisco 49ers at Philadelphia Eagles - December 3rd, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202312030phi.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Three weeks later against the [[Baltimore Ravens]] on [[NFL on Christmas Day|Christmas Day]], he had four tackles and a pass deflection in the 33–19 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Baltimore Ravens at San Francisco 49ers - December 25th, 2023 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202312250sfo.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Thomas finished the 2023 season with 43 tackles, seven pass deflections, an interception, a forced fumble, and a fumble recovery in 15 games and six starts.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ambry Thomas 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/T/ThomAm00.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The 49ers finished atop the [[NFC West]] with a 12–5 record and qualified for the playoffs as the #1-seed.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2023 San Francisco 49ers Rosters, Stats, Schedule, Team Draftees, Injury Reports |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/teams/sfo/2023.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2023–24 NFL playoffs#NFC: San Francisco 24, Green Bay Packers 21|Divisional Round]] against the [[Green Bay Packers]], Thomas recorded five tackles during the 24–21 victory.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Divisional Round - Green Bay Packers at San Francisco 49ers - January 20th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401200sfo.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> During the [[2023–24 NFL playoffs#NFC Championship: San Francisco 49ers 34, Detroit Lions 31|NFC Championship Game]] against the Lions, he had six tackles in the 34–31 comeback victory as the 49ers advanced to [[Super Bowl LVIII]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=NFC Championship - Detroit Lions at San Francisco 49ers - January 28th, 2024 |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/boxscores/202401280sfo.htm |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the Super Bowl against the [[Kansas City Chiefs]], Thomas recorded no statistics during the 25–22 overtime loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Super Bowl LVIII - '''Amen Ogbongbemiga''' ({{Respell|AY|men}} {{Respell|awg|BONG|beh|MEE|guh}};<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=https://okstate.com/sports/football/roster/amen-ogbongbemiga/8993|title=Amen Ogbongbemiga - 2020 - Football|website=Oklahoma State University Athletics}}</ref> born 4 September 1998) is a Nigerian professional [[American football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State Cowboys]].

==Early life==
Amen Ogbongbemiga was born on 4 September 1998, in [[Lagos, Nigeria]]. His family moved to [[Houston|Houston, Texas]], in 2003 and to [[Calgary]] in 2011.<ref name="e011">{{cite web | last=Sayles | first=Damon | title=Meet Amen Ogbongbemiga, Nigerian-Born Athlete Finding Football Success in Canada | website=Bleacher Report | date=2015-06-15 | url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2496094-meet-amen-ogbongbemiga-nigerian-born-athlete-finding-football-success-in-canada | access-date=2024-10-25}}</ref> He went to high school at [[Notre Dame High School (Calgary)|Notre Dame]] in Calgary before moving back to the [[United States]]. In his junior year of high school he recorded 104 tackles, three sacks, 13 tackles for loss, four forced fumbles, and two recoveries.<ref name="auto"/> Ogbongbemiga amassed 110 tackles, 15 for loss, four sacks, five forced fumbles and three recoveries. He was named first-team all-district and team MVP his senior year. He helped his team achieve 37 consecutive victories, near the all-time Canadian record. He was thrice an Academic Honor Roll selection. He also competed in track & field at Notre Dame.<ref name="auto"/>

==College career==
He attended college at [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State University]] from 2016 to 2021. He sat out his true freshman season as a redshirt.

He was named first-team academic all-Big 12 after his freshman season, posting 16 tackles and 13 solo stops while playing in 12 games.<ref name="auto"/> His best game came against [[Pittsburgh Panthers football|Pittsburgh]], where he recorded a season-high five tackles. He was credited with tackles for loss in games against [[South Alabama Jaguars football|South Alabama]] and [[Baylor Bears football|Baylor]]. He also was credited with one quarterback hurry during the season

Ogbongbemiga played in all 13 games as a sophomore, logging 12 tackles, three for loss, 1.5 sacks, and a fumble recovery. Against rival [[Oklahoma Sooners football|Oklahoma]] he recorded a sack of [[Kyler Murray]], and a season-high three tackles. He matched that statistic against South Alabama as well. He was named team captain during both the Oklahoma, and South Alabama games. He had an important blocked punt in an Oklahoma State win over [[Boise State Broncos football|Boise State]]. He also led all Oklahoma State special teams players with six tackles.<ref name="auto"/> He was awarded the OSU Outstanding Special Teams Player award as well as named first-team academic all-Big 12 following the season.

He was voted team captain for the 2019 season and performed well, finishing the season ranked sixth in the Big 12 with 100 tackles.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://okstate.com/sports/football/roster/amen-ogbongbemiga/8993/|title=Amen Ogbongbemiga - 2020 - Football|website=Oklahoma State University Athletics}}</ref> He led the team with 15.5 tackles for loss and 5 sacks. Against [[Texas A&M Aggies football|Texas A&M]], he recorded a season-high 12 tackles, also amassing a sack and fumble recovery in the annual [[Texas Bowl]]. He also recorded his first career interception late in a win over [[Iowa State Cyclones football|Iowa State]]. In games against Texas and [[West Virginia Mountaineers football|West Virginia]] he recorded 11 tackles, also recording 10 in a game against [[Oregon State Beavers football|Oregon State]]. He was team captain in games against Oklahoma, Baylor, and [[Tulsa Golden Hurricane football|Tulsa]]. He ended the season gaining Second-team All-Big 12 and First-team Academic All-Big 12 honors, as well as the [[Leslie O'Neal]] award, for the best defensive player on the team.<ref name="auto"/>

He remained the team captain for his senior season, leading OSU in tackles in six of its eleven games. He was a semifinalist for the Lott IMPACT Trophy, an honorable mention for defensive player of the year, a First-team All-Academic selection for the fourth straight year, and a Second-team All-Big 12 selection for the second consecutive year.<ref name="auto"/> He started every game and was the game captain in games against [[Kansas Jayhawks football|Kansas]], Oklahoma, Baylor, and [[Miami Hurricanes football|Miami]]. He finished the season with 81 tackles, only one shy of their 2020 leader Malcolm Rodriguez. He led the Cowboys in tackles in the games against West Virginia (13), Kansas (5), Texas (10), Kansas State (8), Texas Tech (11), and [[TCU Horned Frogs football|TCU]] (12). His 13 tackles against West Virginia were a career-high. He also recorded 2.5 sacks and three quarterback hurries during the season. In the game against TCU, he had three forced fumbles in under 19 minutes, only one shy of the NCAA's single game record.<ref name="auto"/> He was named Big 12 Player of the Week following the game.<ref name="auto"/> He chose to forgo remaining eligibility and instead declare for the [[NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/Oklahoma-State-LB-Amen-Ogbongbemiga-NFL-draft-16069618.php|title=Oklahoma State LB Amen Ogbongbemiga poised for NFL draft|first=Aaron|last=Wilson|date=1 April 2021|website=Houston Chronicle}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/sports/college/cowboys/2021/01/10/oklahoma-state-football-amen-ogbongbemiga-leaving-for-nfl/322111007/|title=Oklahoma State football: Amen Ogbongbemiga leaving for NFL|first=Scott|last=Wright|website=The Oklahoman}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
After going unselected in the [[2021 NFL draft]], Ogbongbemiga signed as an undrafted free agent with the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.boltsfromtheblue.com/2021/5/6/22422678/chargers-news-nfl-amen-ogbongbemiga-cfl-calgary-stampeders|title=Chargers LB Amen Ogbongbemiga drafted 8th-overall in 2021 CFL Draft|first=Michael|last=Peterson|date=6 May 2021|website=Bolts From The Blue}}</ref> Three days later, he was selected with the 8th overall pick in the [[2021 CFL draft]] by the [[Calgary Stampeders]]. He made the final roster as a rookie and appeared in 15 games, recording 26 tackles.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/O/OgboAm00.htm|website=[[Pro-Football-Reference.com]]|title=Amen Ogbongbemiga Stats}}</ref>

Ogbongbemiga returned in 2022 and appeared in all 17 games, none as a starter, totaling six tackles. He also appeared in the team's one playoff game, a loss to the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]], and recovered a fumble. In his third year, he played 15 games and recorded four tackles, also recovering two fumbles.<ref name=":0" />

===Chicago Bears===
On March 14, 2024, Ogbongbemiga signed with the [[Chicago Bears]].<ref name="p418">{{cite web | last=Hajduk | first=Gabby | title=Roster Move: Bears add LB Amen Ogbongbemiga | website=Chicago Bears | date=2024-03-14 | url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-move-bears-add-lb-amen-ogbongbemiga | access-date=2024-10-25}}</ref> He played in all 17 games for Chicago, logging a sack and 13 combined tackles.

On March 6, 2025, Ogbongbemiga re-signed with the Bears on a two-year, $5 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web |date=March 6, 2025 |title=Roster Moves: Bears extend LB Amen Ogbongbemiga |url=https://www.chicagobears.com/news/roster-moves-bears-extend-lb-amen-ogbongbemiga |access-date=March 11, 2025 |website=Chicago Bears |language=en}}</ref> After solely being on special teams to start the season, he saw his first defensive action in Week 12 against the [[2025 Pittsburgh Steelers season|Pittsburgh Steelers]] due to injuries. He recorded a career-high 40 snaps in the game along with 14 tackles, the second most on the team, as the Bears won 31–28.<ref>{{cite news|last=Cronin|first=Courtney|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/47078948/bears-defensive-replacements-rise-occasion-win-steelers|title=Bears' defensive replacements rise to occasion in win over Steelers|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|date=November 23, 2025|access-date=November 25, 2025}}</ref>

On February 19, 2026, Ogbongemiga was cut by the Bears.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bears cut LB Amen Ogbongbemiga|url=https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/02/19/bears-cut-linebacker-amen-ogbongbemiga-2026-offseason-special-teams-ben-johnson-ryan-poles-nfl|work=Chicago Sun Times|date=February 19, 2026}}</ref>

'''Amaré Barno''' (born April 26, 1999) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[linebacker]]. He played [[college football]] at [[Butler Grizzlies|Butler (KS)]] before transferring to [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]]. Barno was drafted by the Panthers in the sixth round of the [[2022 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Barno grew up in [[Blythewood, South Carolina]] and attended Westwood High School. He played the safety position in high school. Barno failed to qualify academically to play [[NCAA Division I|Division I]] football and enrolled at [[Butler Community College]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McKewon |first=Sam |date=December 8, 2018 |title=In need of pass rushers, Huskers host prospect on official visit |url=https://norfolkdailynews.com/sports/husker_sports/husker_football/in-need-of-pass-rushers-huskers-host-prospect-on-official-visit/article_8af0adec-fa3c-11e8-adb1-ebb2383aba63.html |access-date=January 13, 2022 |website=[[APNews.com]] |publisher=[[Omaha World-Herald|World-Herald News Service]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Barno began his college career at [[Butler Community College]], where coaches moved him from safety to linebacker. As a sophomore, he recorded 66 tackles, 14 tackles for loss and 4.5 sacks.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sullivan |first=Tim |date=December 12, 2018 |title=Signing Day capsule: Amare Barno |url=https://virginiatech.rivals.com/news/signing-day-capsule-amare-barno |access-date=January 13, 2022 |website=[[Rivals.com]]}}</ref> In 2018, Barno committed to transfer to [[Virginia Tech Hokies football|Virginia Tech]] for his remaining eligibility.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Niziolek |first=Mike |date=December 17, 2018 |title=Virginia Tech lands verbal commit from JUCO linebacker |url=https://roanoke.com/sports/college/va_tech/virginia-tech-lands-verbal-commit-from-juco-linebacker/article_4fb1c63a-022a-11e9-b60c-d33588bb7ac8.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200304094906/https://www.roanoke.com/sports/college/va_tech/virginia-tech-lands-verbal-commit-from-juco-linebacker/article_4fb1c63a-022a-11e9-b60c-d33588bb7ac8.html |archive-date=March 4, 2020 |access-date=January 13, 2022 |website=[[The Roanoke Times]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=December 18, 2018 |title=Husker pass rushing target Amare Barno commits to Virginia Tech |url=https://omaha.com/sports/college/huskers/recruiting/husker-pass-rushing-target-amare-barno-commits-to-virginia-tech/article_b0cece87-f5b9-5501-94c8-6de06b41ed6f.html |access-date=January 13, 2022 |website=[[Omaha World-Herald]]}}</ref>

Barno played in three games in his first season at Virginia Tech in 2019 as an outside linebacker before [[redshirt (college sports)|redshirting]] the rest of the season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Niziolek |first=Mike |date=March 10, 2021 |title='There is no ceiling' for Virginia Tech defensive end Amare Barno going into 2021 |url=https://roanoke.com/sports/college/va_tech/there-is-no-ceiling-for-virginia-tech-defensive-end-amare-barno-going-into-2021/article_4afa433c-81db-11eb-b28b-4b5fe4d8585f.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210517033800/https://roanoke.com/sports/college/va_tech/there-is-no-ceiling-for-virginia-tech-defensive-end-amare-barno-going-into-2021/article_4afa433c-81db-11eb-b28b-4b5fe4d8585f.html |archive-date=May 17, 2021 |access-date=January 13, 2022 |website=[[The Roanoke Times]]}}</ref> Going into his redshirt junior season, he was again moved to a different position and played defensive end. Barno finished the season a team-high 6.5 sacks and led the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] with 16 tackles for loss.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Niziolek |first=Mike |date=October 29, 2020 |title=Virginia Tech's quiet giant Amare Barno makes noise at new position |url=https://roanoke.com/sports/college/va_tech/virginia-tech-s-quiet-giant-amare-barno-makes-noise-at-new-position/article_d3ca7b1c-19af-11eb-b71a-8b21ebb2c2ff.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210625003410/https://roanoke.com/sports/college/va_tech/virginia-tech-s-quiet-giant-amare-barno-makes-noise-at-new-position/article_d3ca7b1c-19af-11eb-b71a-8b21ebb2c2ff.html |archive-date=June 25, 2021 |access-date=January 13, 2022 |website=[[The Roanoke Times]]}}</ref> Barno recorded 5.5 tackles for loss with 3.5 sacks in 2021. Following the end of the season, Barno declared that he would be entering the [[2022 NFL draft]],<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sis |first=Matej |date=December 6, 2021 |title=Virginia Tech Hokies DL Amare Barno Declares for 2022 NFL Draft, opts out of Pinstripe Bowl |url=https://247sports.com/college/virginia-tech/Article/Virginia-Tech-Hokies-DL-Amare-Barno-Declares-for-2022-NFL-Draft-opts-out-of-Pinstripe-Bowl-177504097/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211206180132/https://247sports.com/college/virginia-tech/Article/Virginia-Tech-Hokies-DL-Amare-Barno-Declares-for-2022-NFL-Draft-opts-out-of-Pinstripe-Bowl-177504097/ |archive-date=December 6, 2021 |access-date=January 13, 2022 |website=[[247Sports]]}}</ref> and ran a 4.37 [[40-yard dash]] at the [[NFL Combine]], faster than any linebacker or defensive lineman that year.

=== Carolina Panthers ===
At the 2022 [[NFL Scouting Combine|NFL Combine]], Barno tied [[Odafe Oweh]] for the fastest [[40-yard dash]] time by a [[Lineman (gridiron football)#Defensive line|defensive lineman]] at 4.36; Oweh had recorded that time at the NFL Combine the year prior.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Schulte |first=A.J. |date=February 24, 2024 |title=Fastest Defensive Linemen 40-Yard Dash Times in NFL Combine History |url=https://www.profootballnetwork.com/fastest-defensive-linemen-40-yard-dash-times-in-nfl-combine-history/ |access-date=February 29, 2024 |website=Pro Football Network}}</ref> Barno was drafted by the [[Carolina Panthers]] in the sixth round (189th overall) in the 2022 NFL Draft.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Joyce |first=Ethan |date=April 30, 2022 |title=Panthers select defensive end Amaré Barno in sixth round |url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-select-defensive-end-amare-barno-in-sixth-round |access-date=April 8, 2023 |website=Panthers.com}}</ref> He finished his rookie season with nine tackles and two sacks in nine games played.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amare Barno 2022 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BarnAm00/gamelog/2022/ |access-date=April 8, 2023 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref> In the 2023 season, he finished with 21 total tackles in 15 games and one start.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Amare Barno 2023 Game Log |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/B/BarnAm00/gamelog/2023/ |access-date=July 8, 2024 |website=[[Pro Football Reference]] |language=en}}</ref>

Barno began the 2024 season on the reserve/[[physically unable to perform]] list.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers make moves to get to initial 53-man roster|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-make-moves-to-get-to-initial-53-man-roster|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=August 27, 2024}}</ref> He was activated on November 30.<ref name="n063">{{cite web | last=Gantt | first=Darin | title=Amaré Barno activated from physically unable to perform list | website=Panthers.com | date=November 30, 2024 | url=https://www.panthers.com/news/amare-barno-activated-from-physically-unable-to-perform-list | access-date=December 26, 2024}}</ref> He was waived on July 25, 2025.<ref>{{cite web|title=Panthers switch up outside linebackers|url=https://www.panthers.com/news/panthers-switch-up-outside-linebackers-jj-weaver|author=Gantt, Darin|website=Panthers.com|date=July 25, 2025}}</ref>

=== Columbus Aviators ===
On January 14, 2026, Barno was selected by the [[Columbus Aviators]] of the [[United Football League (2024)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Day Two of UFL Draft Introduces New Faces and Ignites the New Era of Spring Football |url=https://www.theufl.com/news/day-two-of-ufl-draft-introduces-new-faces-and-ignites-the-new-era-of-spring-football |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=www.theufl.com |language=en}}</ref>

'''Anders Bjorn Carlson''' ({{Respell|ON|dərs bee|YORN}};<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anders Carlson Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/C/CarlAn00.htm |access-date=2025-02-04 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> born June 16, 1998) is an American professional [[American football|football]] kicker for the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United Football League (2024–present)|United Football League]] (UFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Auburn Tigers football|Auburn Tigers]], and was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the sixth round of the [[2023 NFL draft]]. As a placekicker, he has been recognized as both a high school and collegiate [[College Football All-America Team|All-American]] as well as an [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) First Team and [[Lou Groza Award]] semifinalist selection.

==Early life==
Carlson attended and played football, [[Association football|soccer]], and [[basketball]] at [[The Classical Academy (Colorado)|The Classical Academy]] (Titans) in [[Colorado Springs, Colorado]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Anders Carlson – Football |url=https://auburntigers.com/sports/football/roster/anders-carlson/17270 |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Auburn University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> In 2014, as a sophomore, he made four of six [[field goal]] attempts with a long of 44 yards, as well as nine out of 10 [[Conversion (gridiron football)|extra-point attempts]] (PATs). In 2015, as a junior, he made 11 of 18 field goal attempts with a long of 52 yards, and 37 of 38 PATs. In 2016, as a senior, he made 13 of 23 field goal attempts, including a long of 51 yards, and all 49 of his PATs.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anders Carlson's High School Football Stats |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/athlete/anders-carlson/Gs51OQXDEeOZ5AAmVebBJg/football/stats.htm |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=MaxPreps.com |language=en}}</ref>

Carlson was invited to and played in the 2017 [[Under Armour All-America Game]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=All-America |url=https://underarmournext.com/football/all-america/ |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Under Armour Next Football |language=en-US}}</ref> A three-star college prospect was the highest-rated prep kicker recruit in the nation coming out of high school. [[ESPN]] rated him a top-10 overall recruit prospect in the state of [[Colorado]].<ref name=":0" /> He committed to play [[college football]] for the Auburn Tigers over scholarship offers from [[Oklahoma State Cowboys football|Oklahoma State]] and [[Vanderbilt Commodores football|Vanderbilt]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anders Carlson, 2017 Kicker |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/2017/anders-carlson-101573 |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=n.rivals.com}}</ref>

As a soccer player, Carlson helped the Titans to the 2014 and 2015 Class 4A State finals.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaniewski |first=Scott |date=November 6, 2014 |title=The Classical Academy makes 4A boys' soccer final in first year at 4A |url=https://gazette.com/sports/the-classical-academy-makes-4a-boys-soccer-final-in-first-year-at-4a/article_590aee56-6e63-51b2-85bb-92d0d585046f.html |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Colorado Springs Gazette |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Kaniewski |first=Scott  |date=November 14, 2015 |title=TCA soccer loses to Evergreen in state championship game |url=https://gazette.com/sports/tca-soccer-loses-to-evergreen-in-state-championship-game/article_c97871ba-9091-5e25-979a-01210d305287.html |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Colorado Springs Gazette |language=en}}</ref>

==College career==
===2017 season===
In 2017, Carlson [[redshirted]] his true freshman football season at [[2017 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]] as he served as the backup placekicker to his older brother, [[Daniel Carlson|Daniel]].<ref name=":0" />

===2018 season===
In 2018, prior to his redshirt freshman, Carlson gained attention after kicking a 62-yard field goal at Auburn's practice facility.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Stanford |first=Callie |date=September 29, 2021 |title=How the Carlson brothers kicked their way into Auburn history |url=https://www.theplainsman.com/article/2021/09/how-the-carlson-brothers-kicked-their-way-into-auburn-history |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=The Auburn Plainsman}}</ref> That season, he successfully converted 15 of 25 field goal attempts, including two 53-yard field goals, which were the second-longest field goals made in Auburn program history by a freshman. He also converted all 44 PATs, including going 9-for-9 in the [[2018 Music City Bowl]] against [[2018 Purdue Boilermakers football team|Purdue]]. He further forced 51 [[touchback]]s on 70 total [[Kickoff (gridiron football)|kickoffs]]. On November 24, 2018, against in-state rival [[2018 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama]], he recorded his first and only career reception, a 3-yard catch on a fake field goal play.<ref name=":0" />

===2019 season===
In 2019, Carlson entered his redshirt sophomore season as an SEC Media Preseason [[List of All-SEC football teams|All-Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) Second Team and SEC Coaches Preseason All-SEC Third Team placekicker.<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 15, 2019 |title=2019 Preseason Coaches All-SEC Football Team announced |url=https://www.secsports.com/article/27393791/2019-preseason-coaches-all-sec-football-team-announced |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=SEC Sports}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=July 19, 2019 |title=2019 Preseason All-SEC: Conference announces media picks |url=https://www.saturdaydownsouth.com/sec-football/2019-preseason-all-sec-media-picks/ |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Saturday Down South |language=en-US}}</ref> He earned SEC Special Teams Player of the Week honors after making all four of his field goal attempts – from 43 (twice), 44, and 52 yards – in [[2019 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]]’s 48–45 upset win over [[2019 Alabama Crimson Tide football team|Alabama]] in the “[[Iron Bowl]].”<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shearer |first=Jeff |date=December 2, 2019 |title=Auburn's Zakoby McClain, Anders Carlson earn SEC honors |url=https://auburntigers.com/news/2019/12/2/football-auburns-zakoby-mcclain-anders-carlson-earn-sec-honors.aspx |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Auburn University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> His 52-yard field goal attempt against Alabama tied his brother, Daniel, and [[Al Del Greco]], for Auburn’s longest field goal ever in Iron Bowl history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Shearer |first=Jeff |date=December 2, 2019 |title=Iron Bowl notebook: 'surreal moment' for Bo Nix |url=https://auburntigers.com/news/2019/12/2/football-iron-bowl-notebook-surreal-moment-for-bo-nix.aspx |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Auburn University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> His third PAT made against [[2019 Arkansas Razorbacks football team|Arkansas]] set an [[NCAA]] record for consecutive successful PATs (303) by Auburn kickers; a streak started by former Auburn kicker, [[Cody Parkey]], in 2013 and that spanned six seasons, 78 games, and five different Auburn kickers.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Ostendorf |first=Greg  |date=April 2, 2020 |title='Biggest blessing': How Auburn kicked its way into NCAA history |url=https://auburntigers.com/news/2020/4/2/football-biggest-blessing-how-auburn-kicked-its-way-into-ncaa-history.aspx |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Auburn University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He finished his 2019 campaign by making 18 out of 25 field goal attempts and 48 out of 49 PATs, as well as 47 touchbacks on 78 kickoffs.<ref name=":0" />

===2020 season===
In 2020, entering his redshirt junior season, Carlson was selected to the SEC Media Preseason All-SEC Third Team and the [[Phil Steele]] All-SEC Fourth Team.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Preseason SEC media poll, All-SEC Team announced |url=https://www.secsports.com/article/29952339/preseason-sec-media-poll-all-sec-team-announced |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=secsports.com}}</ref> That season, he made 20 out of 22 field goal attempts, including a long of 50 yards, and 24 out of 25 PATs.<ref name=":0" /> He was twice selected to the [[Lou Groza]] “Star of the Week” list for his kicking efforts against [[2020 Arkansas Razorbacks football team|Arkansas]] and [[2020 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team|Mississippi State]].<ref name=":0" />

His 2020 season performance earned him [[Lou Groza Award]] (best placekicker in college football) semifinalist,<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 15, 2020 |title=Lou Groza Award Names Semi-Finalists and Local Awards Finalists |url=http://www.palmbeachsports.com/lou-groza-award-names-semi-finalists-and-local-awards-finalists/ |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Palm Beach County Sports Commission |language=en-US}}</ref> [[American Football Coaches Association|American Football Coaches Association (AFCA)]] FBS Coaches’ [[All-America]] Second Team,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Alabama's DeVonta Smith & Tulsa's Zaven Collins Headline 2020 AFCA FBS Coaches' All-American Teams – AFCA |url=https://www.afca.com/alabamas-devonta-smith-tulsas-zaven-collins-headline-2020-afca-fbs-coaches-all-american-teams/ |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=afca.com}}</ref> Phil Steele All-America Honorable Mention, and [[Associated Press|Associated Press (AP)]] All-SEC First Team<ref>{{Cite web |last=Iacobelli |first=Pete |date=December 23, 2020 |title=AP All-SEC football team: Classical Academy grad Anders Carlson of Auburn named to first team |url=https://www.denverpost.com/2020/12/23/ap-all-sec-anders-carlson/ |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=The Denver Post |language=en-US}}</ref> honors.<ref name=":0" />

===2021 season===
In 2021, as a redshirt senior, he made 14 of 21 field goal attempts with a long of 49 yards, as well as 35 of 36 PATs.<ref name=":0" /> On November 13, in [[2021 Auburn Tigers football team|Auburn]]’s game against [[2021 Mississippi State Bulldogs football team|Mississippi State]], he suffered a season-ending [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|torn ACL]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=November 16, 2021 |title=Auburn's Carlson out for season; Nix has surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/story/_/id/32640142/auburn-tigers-kicker-anders-carlson-acl-season-qb-bo-nix-successful-ankle-surgery |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}}</ref>

Carlson’s career performance places him with the fifth-most points (275), third-most field goals made (53), and sixth-most PATs made (116) in Auburn program history.<ref name=":0" />

Carlson earned Special Teams MVP honors for Auburn’s 2018, 2019, and 2021 “A-Day” spring football games.<ref name="v178">{{cite web | last=King | first=Nathan | title=Auburn's A-Day MVPs through the years | website=Rivals.com | date=2020-04-11 | url=https://auburn.rivals.com/news/a-look-at-auburn-s-a-day-mvps-through-the-years | access-date=2024-12-09}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Rewinding Auburn's 2021 A-Day spring football game |url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/ncaafb/rewinding-auburn-s-2021-a-day-spring-football-game/ar-BB1fLhbY |access-date=February 26, 2022 |publisher=MSN |language=en-US}}</ref> Auburn's 2020 A-Day was cancelled due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=King |first=Nathan |date=March 17, 2020 |title=Auburn's 2020 A-Day game officially canceled |url=https://auburn.rivals.com/news/auburn-s-2020-a-day-game-officially-canceled |access-date=February 26, 2022 |website=Rivals.com}}</ref>

=== Green Bay Packers ===
====2023 season====
Carlson was selected by the [[Green Bay Packers]] in the sixth round (207th overall) of the [[2023 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=April 29, 2023 |title=2023 NFL Draft: Packers select Auburn K Anders Carlson in sixth round, No. 207 overall |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-auburn-k-anders-carlson-2023-nfl-draft |access-date=April 29, 2023 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> He signed his rookie contract on May 5.<ref>{{Cite web |date=May 5, 2023 |title=Packers sign eight draft picks |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-sign-eight-draft-picks-2023 |access-date=May 5, 2023 |website=Packers.com}}</ref>

In his rookie season, Carlson led the NFL in missed kicks with thirteen. In the Divisional Round playoff game against the [[2023 San Francisco 49ers season|San Francisco 49ers]], Carlson missed a field goal which would have given the Packers a seven point lead and forced the 49ers to tie the game rather than take the lead. The Packers would end up losing 24–21, ending their season.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kuhagen |first1=Christopher |title=Anders Carlson takes brunt of Packers fans' frustration after heartbreaking playoff loss |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2024/01/20/green-bay-packers-kicker-anders-carlson-takes-brunt-of-fans-frustration-after-playoff-loss-49ers/72300857007/ |website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel |publisher=USA Today |access-date=January 21, 2024}}</ref> Head coach [[Matt LaFleur]] and Carlson's Packer teammates came out in support of Carlson, with LaFleur stating that Carlson's missed kick was not the sole reason for the loss.

==== 2024 season ====
The Packers decided to bring in some competition for Carlson for in 2024, signing [[Jack Podlesny]] on January 24, 2024 and [[Greg Joseph]] on March 28.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-06-14 |title=Packers' Anders Carlson heads toward training camp in a three-way kicker competition |url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/story/_/id/40334571/packers-anders-carlson-greg-joseph-jack-podlesny-kicker-competition |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref> None of these players would end up making the final roster, and the Packers released Carlson on August 27, 2024.<ref>{{cite web |date=August 27, 2024 |title=Packers announce roster moves |url=https://www.packers.com/news/packers-announce-roster-moves-aug-27-2024 |website=Packers.com}}</ref> He would remain a free agent for the first six games of the season.

=== San Francisco 49ers ===
On October 15, 2024, the [[San Francisco 49ers]] signed Carlson to their practice squad,<ref>{{Cite web|title=49ers Sign a Safety and Kicker to Practice Squad, Release a Wide Receiver|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-sign-a-safety-and-kicker-to-practice-squad-release-a-wide-receiver|website=49ers.com|date=October 15, 2024|access-date=October 15, 2024}}</ref> and elevated him to the active roster for their game against the [[2024 Kansas City Chiefs season|Kansas City Chiefs]] on October 20. In this game, Carlson made both of his field goal attempts, including a then career-long 55-yarder, but also missed an extra point attempt.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Inabinett |first=Mark |date=2024-10-21 |title=Auburn NFL roundup: Anders Carlson comes back with career-long kick |url=https://www.al.com/sports/2024/10/auburn-nfl-roundup-anders-carlson-comes-back-with-career-long-kick.html |access-date=2024-10-22 |website=al |language=en}}</ref> On November 5, the 49ers released him.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.49ers.com/news/49ers-waive-lb-graham-release-k-carlson|work=49ers.com|title=49ers Waive LB Graham, Release K Carlson|date=November 5, 2024|accessdate=November 6, 2024}}</ref>

=== New York Jets ===
On November 8, 2024, Carlson was signed to the [[New York Jets]]' practice squad.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jets Sign DL Bruce Hector to the Active Roster, Add K Anders Carlson to the P-Squad|url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-bruce-hector-anders-carlson-practice-squad|author=Pullano, John|website=NewYorkJets.com|date=November 8, 2024}}</ref> He was elevated to the team's active roster for the game against the [[2024 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]] on November 17.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Jets Sign K Anders Carlson |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-k-anders-carlson-11-19-2024 |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=www.newyorkjets.com |language=en-US}}</ref> During this game, Carlson would beat his personal record again by kicking a 58-yard field goal.<ref name=":1" /> Carlson would remain the Jets kicker until he was designated inactive for the December 29 game,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-29 |title=Jets' Anders Carlson: Inactive Sunday |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/jets-anders-carlson-inactive-sunday/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref> and he was released by the team the next day on December 30.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-12-30 |title=Anders Carlson: Dropped by Jets |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/anders-carlson-dropped-by-jets/ |access-date=2025-01-07 |website=CBSSports.com |language=en}}</ref>

On January 14, 2025, Carlson signed a reserve/futures contract with the Jets.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Greenberg |first1=Ethan |date=January 14, 2025 |title=Jets Sign K Anders Carlson, TE Neal Johnson to Reserve/Future Deals |url=https://www.newyorkjets.com/news/jets-sign-anders-carlson--neal-johnson-reserve-future-01-14-2025 |access-date=15 January 2025 |website=NewYorkJets.com}}</ref> On June 18, Carlson was released by the Jets.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-06-18 |title=Anders Carlson: Cut loose by Jets |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/football/news/anders-carlson-cut-loose-by-jets/ |access-date=2025-06-18 |website=CBS Sports |language=}}</ref>

=== Birmingham Stallions ===
On April 14, 2026, Carlson signed with the [[Birmingham Stallions (2022)|Birmingham Stallions]] of the [[United Football League (2024–present)|United Football League]] (UFL).<ref>{{cite web |last1=Larsen |first1=James |title=Stallions Sign Anders Carlson & Joey Lombard, Cut Garibay |url=https://pfnewsroom.com/news/stallions-sign-anders-carlson-joey-lombard-cut-garibay/ |website=PFNewsroom.com |access-date=15 April 2026}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Carlson was born to parents, Jodie and Hans, in Colorado Springs, Colorado. He has two brothers, Nils and [[Daniel Carlson|Daniel]]. Daniel is the placekicker for the [[Las Vegas Raiders]] and was also an [[All-America]]n kicker at Auburn.<ref name=":0" />

In 2017, as a freshman at Auburn, he earned Academic Top Tiger and SEC First-Year Academic Honor Roll recognition. In both 2018 and 2019, he earned AD Honor Roll honors. He earned SEC Academic Honor Roll recognition every year from 2018 to 2020. In both 2019 and 2020, he earned CoSIDA Academic All-District honors.<ref name=":0" /> In 2020, he graduated from Auburn with a degree in [[aviation]] from the university's College of Business. He is now pursuing his master's degree.<ref name=":0" />

Carlson is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. He has said, "I think the biggest thing for me is just knowing my identity. I think for me, faith is a really big thing. My current thing I'm doing is football, but that's not who I am. I'm just focused on the things I can control, but knowing my identity is not in football, it's in God."<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mercer |first=Kevin |date=October 12, 2023 |title=Carlson brothers Anders and Daniel make NFL history, share deep faith in God |url=https://sportsspectrum.com/sport/football/2023/10/12/carlson-brothers-anders-daniel-history-faith-god/ |access-date=October 13, 2023 |website=Sports Spectrum}}</ref>

'''Amarius Tyron Mims''' (born October 14, 2002) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[offensive tackle]] for the [[Cincinnati Bengals]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]], where he won consecutive national championships in [[2022 College Football Playoff National Championship|2021]] and [[2023 College Football Playoff National Championship|2022]]. Mims was selected by the Bengals in the first round of the [[2024 NFL draft]].

==Early life==
Mims was born on October 14, 2002, in [[Cochran, Georgia]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nfldraftbuzz.com/Player/Amarius-Mims-OL-Georgia|title=Amarius Mims Offensive Tackle Georgia|website=nfldraftbuzz.com|access-date=July 27, 2023}}</ref> He played football at [[Bleckley County High School]] and was rated a five-star recruit before committing to play [[college football]] for the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|Georgia Bulldogs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/georgia-ol-amarius-mims-chooses-to-remain-with-bulldogs-after-testing-waters-in-transfer-portal/|title=Georgia OL Amarius Mims chooses to remain with Bulldogs after testing waters in transfer portal|first=Barrett|last=Sallee|website=[[CBS Sports]]|date=April 18, 2022|access-date=July 24, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Legge |first=Dean |date=October 14, 2020 |title=UGA football lands another five-star offensive line recruit in Amarius Mims |url=https://www.onlineathens.com/story/sports/college/2020/10/14/uga-football-lands-another-five-star-offensive-line-recruit/114844258/ |access-date=July 24, 2023 |website=[[Athens Banner-Herald]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2872654-5-star-ot-prospect-amarius-mims-commits-to-georgia-over-alabama-tennessee|title=5-Star OT Prospect Amarius Mims Commits to Georgia over Alabama, Tennessee|first=Rod|last=Goldberg|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=October 14, 2020|access-date=July 24, 2023}}</ref>

==College career==
Mims played in seven games as a freshman with the Bulldogs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://uga.rivals.com/news/amarius-mim-s-steps-fully-into-the-spotlight|title=Amarius Mims steps fully into the spotlight|first=Jed|last=May|website=[[Rivals.com]]|date=April 6, 2023|access-date=July 24, 2023}}</ref> After the season, He entered the [[NCAA transfer portal]], but ultimately decided to return to Georgia for his sophomore season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Towers |first=Chip |date=April 18, 2022 |title=OT Amarius Mims opts to stick with Georgia Bulldogs |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-bulldogs/ot-amarius-mims-opts-to-stick-with-georgia-bulldogs/L7S42G47LJHMBL4MY66HYZOIIE/ |access-date=July 24, 2023 |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]}}</ref> Mims played in the first 12 games of his sophomore season as a reserve.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/georgia/news/amarius-mims-time-has-come|title=Amarius Mims' "Time Has Come"|first=Tyler|last=Graves|website=[[SI.com]]|date=April 9, 2023|access-date=July 24, 2023}}</ref> Following an injury to starting right tackle [[Warren McClendon]], he started in the [[2022 Peach Bowl]] and the [[2023 College Football Playoff National Championship|national championship]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Roberson |first=Doug |date=December 31, 2022 |title=Ladd McConkey returns for Georgia in Peach Bowl; Amarius Mims gets first start |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-bulldogs/ladd-mcconkey-returns-for-georgia-in-peach-bowl-amarius-mims-gets-first-start/DDJWMMDHF5HKTCGA5KWCF5PVSA/ |access-date=July 24, 2023 |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/georgia/article/georgia-football-amarius-mims-named-no-6-ot-prospect-for-2024-nfl-draft-213056830/|title=Georgia football: Amarius Mims named No. 6 OT prospect for 2024 NFL Draft|first=Kipp|last=Adams|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=July 21, 2023|access-date=July 24, 2023}}</ref> Mims declared for the [[2024 NFL draft]] following the 2023 season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Backus |first=Will |date=December 31, 2023 |title=2024 NFL Draft: Georgia offensive tackle Amarius Mims declares as expected first-round pick |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-football/news/2024-nfl-draft-georgia-offensive-tackle-amarius-mims-declares-as-expected-first-round-pick/ |access-date=1 January 2024 |website=CBS Sports}}</ref> While he was playing at Georgia, Mims was injured and required treatment at [[Piedmont Hospital]] in Atlanta that was featured locally in the Atlanta area.<ref>[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bV4aoNwI9So Piedmont Hospital ad featuring Mims from 2024.] - accessed November 8, 2025.</ref>

'''Amari Henderson''' (born September 8, 1997) is an American professional [[gridiron football|football]] [[defensive back]] for the [[Ottawa Redblacks]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL). He played [[college football]] at [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest]]. He has also been a member of the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] and [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL), and the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the CFL.

==Early life==
Henderson played [[high school football]] at [[Mallard Creek High School]] in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]].<ref name="bio">{{cite web | url=https://godeacs.com/sports/football/roster/amari-henderson/4979 | title=Amari Henderson | publisher=godeacs.com | accessdate=March 4, 2024}}</ref> He recorded 25, tackles, 29 pass breakups and nine interceptions his senior year in 2014, earning [[Associated Press|AP]] first-team all-state honors.<ref name="bio"/> Henderson also helped lead Mallard Creek to 4AA state championships in 2013 and 2014.<ref name="bio"/>

==College career==
Henderson played [[college football]] at [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons football|Wake Forest]] from 2016 to 2019. He was [[redshirted]] in 2015.<ref name="bio"/> He played in 11 games, starting eight, in 2016, totaling 20 tackles, one interception and nine pass breakups.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="Db">{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/amari-henderson-hendeam01 | title=Amari Henderson | publisher=Footballdb.com | accessdate=March 4, 2024}}</ref> Henderson appeared in 12 games, starting 10, in 2017, accumulating 62 tackles, two interceptions and 12 pass breakups.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="Db"/> He played in 10 games, starting nine, in 2018, recording 47 tackles and 10 pass breakups.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="Db"/> He started 13 games in 2019, totaling 40 tackles, four interceptions, and 10 pass breakups, earning [[Phil Steele]] second team All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] honors.<ref name="bio"/><ref name="Db"/> Henderson was invited to the 2020 [[NFLPA Collegiate Bowl]].<ref name="bio"/>

===Jacksonville Jaguars===
Henderson signed with the [[Jacksonville Jaguars]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL) on April 29, 2020. He was waived on September 6 and signed to the [[practice squad]] the next day. He was released by the Jaguars on September 14, 2020.<ref name="dbt">{{cite web | url=https://www.footballdb.com/players/amari-henderson-hendeam01/transactions | title=Amari Henderson | publisher=footballdb.com | accessdate=March 4, 2024}}</ref>

===Minnesota Vikings===
Henderson was signed by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] of the NFL on June 8, 2021.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://m.startribune.com/vikings-add-another-cornerback-in-recent-tryout-amari-henderson/600065588/ | title=Source: Vikings add another cornerback in recent tryout Amari Henderson | publisher=startribune.com | date=June 7, 2021 | accessdate=March 4, 2024 | pages=Krammer, Andrew}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.si.com/nfl/vikings/news/vikings-sign-cornerback-amari-henderson-bringing-roster-maximum-90-players | title=Vikings Sign Cornerback Amari Henderson, Bringing Roster to Maximum 90 Players | publisher=si.com | date=June 7, 2021 | accessdate=March 4, 2024 | author=Ragatz, Will}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ckom.com/2022/09/16/family-a-big-part-of-amari-hendersons-football-journey/ | title=Family a big part of Amari Henderson’s football journey | publisher=ckom.com | date=September 16, 2022 | accessdate=March 4, 2024 | author=Gray, Britton}}</ref><ref name="dbt"/> He was released on August 17, 2021.<ref name="dbt"/>

===Saskatchewan Roughriders===
Henderson signed with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League]] (CFL) on January 20, 2022.<ref name="dbt"/> He was moved to the practice roster on June 5, promoted to the active roster on July 1, placed on [[injured reserve]] on July 15, activated from injured reserve on July 23, and placed on injured reserve on October 6, 2022.<ref name="dbt"/> He played in 11 games, all starts, in 2022, recording 31 tackles on defense and one fumble recovery.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cjme.com/2023/05/30/defensive-back-amari-henderson-making-strong-statement-at-rider-camp/ | title=Defensive back Amari Henderson making strong statement at Rider camp | publisher=cjme.com | date=May 30, 2023 | accessdate=March 4, 2024 | author=Clausing, Shane}}</ref><ref name="Sc"/><ref name="Db"/> Henderson started all 18 games in 2023, totaling 45 tackles on defense, one [[special teams]] tackle, and two interceptions.<ref name="Db"/><ref name="Cfl">{{cite web | url=https://www.cfl.ca/players/amari-henderson/166679/ | title=Amari Henderson | publisher=Footballdb.com | accessdate=March 4, 2024}}</ref><ref name="Sc">{{cite web | url=https://www.statscrew.com/football/stats/p-hendeama001 | title=Amari Henderson | publisher=statscrew.com | accessdate=March 4, 2024}}</ref> He re-signed with the team on December 15, 2023.<ref name="dbt"/><ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/cfl/roughriders-sign-db-amari-henderson-to-contract-extension/sn-amp/ | title=Roughriders sign DB Amari Henderson to contract extension | publisher=sportsnet.ca | date=December 15, 2023 | accessdate=March 4, 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | url=https://3downnation.com/2023/12/15/when-the-moon-hits-your-eyes-riders-extend-db-amari-henderson/ | title=When the moon hits your eyes: Riders extend DB Amari Henderson | publisher=3downnation.com | date=December 15, 2023 | accessdate=March 4, 2024}}</ref>

=== Ottawa Redblacks ===
On February 11, 2025, it was announced that Henderson had signed a one-year contract with the [[Ottawa Redblacks]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-02-11 |title=REDBLACKS sign Adeleke, Lyon, Henderson to one-year deals |url=https://www.cfl.ca/2025/02/11/redblacks-sign-adeleke-lyon-henderson-to-one-year-deals/ |access-date=2025-02-12 |website=CFL.ca |language=en}}</ref>

'''Alvin Ross''' (born May 3, 1963) is a former [[American football|football]] player in the United States. He was a running back for [[Barry Switzer]]'s [[University of Oklahoma]] Sooners and for a season with the [[Philadelphia Eagles]]. He had 54 yards and a touchdown on 14 carries for the Eagles in 1987.<ref name=pro>{{Cite web|url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/players/R/RossAl20.htm|title=Alvin Ross Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft, College|website=Pro-Football-Reference.com}}</ref>

Ross attended [[West Aurora High School]] in [[Aurora, Illinois]]. His short professional career included a stint for the [[Pittsburgh Gladiators]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pBZ3CQAAQBAJ&dq=%22alvin+ross%22+running+back&pg=PA1981|title=Aurora's East-West Football Rivalry: The Longest-Running Series in Illinois|first=Steve|last=Solarz|date=August 5, 2014|publisher=Arcadia Publishing|isbn=978-1-62585-089-8 |via=Google Books}}</ref>

He had five touchdowns at Oklahoma in 1981 as a freshman.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cfb/players/alvin-ross-1.html|title=Alvin Ross College Stats, School, Draft, Gamelog, Splits|website=College Football at Sports-Reference.com}}</ref> He transferred to [[Central State University]] in 1985, but was ruled ineligible before the start of the season because he and other University of Oklahoma players, including [[Buster Rhymes]], were alleged to have taken money from an agent.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.oklahoman.com/story/news/1986/08/16/naia-rules-alvin-ross-ineligible/62717809007/|title=NAIA Rules Alvin Ross Ineligible|website=The Oklahoman}}</ref> In 1986, Ross was allowed to rejoin the team after a court order.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.newspapers.com/article/the-daily-oklahoman/181802644/ | title=Ross Gets Court Order To Rejoin CSU's Team | work=[[The Daily Oklahoman]] | date=August 28, 1986 | accessdate=26 September 2025 | author=Colon, Bob | pages=33}}</ref>
