'''Amar Johnson''' (born January 31, 2003) is an American professional [[American football|football]] [[running back]] for the [[Los Angeles Chargers]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits football|South Dakota State Jackrabbits]].

==Early life==
Amar Johnson was born on January 31, 2003.<ref>{{cite web|title=Amar Johnson - Los Angeles Chargers Running Back - ESPN|url=https://www.espn.com/nfl/player/_/id/4878878/amar-johnson|website=ESPN|access-date = October 11, 2025}}</ref> A native of [[O'Fallon, Missouri]], he attended [[Chaminade College Preparatory School (Missouri)|Chaminade College Prep]] in [[Creve Coeur, Missouri]]. As both a junior and senior, he was named First-team All-State after back-to-back 1,000 yard seasons. Furthermore, he was a two-time All-League selection as a kick returner and was conference offensive player of the year in 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Amar Johnson - 2024 - Football - South Dakota State University Athletics|url=https://gojacks.com/sports/football/roster/amar-johnson/13084|access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref> He was rated as a two-star recruit by [[247Sports]] and committed to [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits football|South Dakota State]] over offers from [[Indiana State Sycamores football|Indiana State]], [[Miami RedHawks football|Miami of Ohio]], [[Missouri State Bears football|Missouri State]], [[Murray State Racers football|Murray State]], [[UT Martin Skyhawks football|UT Martin]], and [[Memphis Tigers football|Memphis]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Amar Johnson, Chaminade College Prep, RB|url=https://247sports.com/player/amar-johnson-46084332/|website=247Sports|access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref>

==College career==
===2021===
In his freshman season, Johnson was mainly a backup running back. However, against [[Lindenwood Lions football|Lindenwood]], a then-[[NCAA Division II]] team, he rushed for 105 yards and his first career touchdown in the 52-7 win.<ref>{{cite web|last= Zimmer|first= Matt|date= September 11, 2021|title= South Dakota State football has its way with Division II Lindenwood in home opener|url=https://www.argusleader.com/story/sports/college/south-dakota-state-university/2021/09/11/south-dakota-state-vs-lindenwood-university-college-football-score-ncaa/5765219001/#|website= Argus Leader|access-date = October 11, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Bower|first=Sean|date=September 11, 2021|title=SDSU dominates from start to finish in rout of Lindenwood|url=https://www.keloland.com/sports/sdsu-dominates-from-start-to-finish-in-rout-of-lindenwood/|website=KELOLAND.com|access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref>

===2022===
In his sophomore season, Johnson was used as part of a duo between him and [[Isaiah Davis]]. In the National championship against [[North Dakota State Bison football|North Dakota State]], he helped to secure a 45-21 win with 126 rushing yards and a touchdown.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kelley|first=Kevin|date=January 8, 2023|title=South Dakota State wins 2022 FCS Championship|url=https://fbschedules.com/south-dakota-state-wins-2022-fcs-championship/|website=FBSchedules.com|access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref>

===2023===
Again as the second part of the duo with Davis, Johnson finished with 801 yards and 4 touchdowns. He was honored as a First-team All-MVFC selection as an all-purpose back.<ref>{{cite web|title=Amar Johnson - 2024 - Football - South Dakota State University Athletics|url=https://gojacks.com/sports/football/roster/amar-johnson/13084|website=South Dakota State University Athletics|access-date = October 12, 2025}}</ref> He helped contribute to the second consecutive FCS championship for the Jackrabbits.

===2024===
As Davis was drafted by the [[New York Jets]] in [[2024 NFL draft|2024]], Johnson was left as the sole starting back for South Dakota State. He ran for 1,222 yards, 14 touchdowns, and 6.4 yards per carry. This performance led to First-team All-MVFC honors again, this time as a true running back.<ref>{{cite web|last=Williams|first=Jimmy|title=Amar Johnson, RB, South Dakota State|url=https://nfldraftdiamonds.com/2025/04/amar-johnson/#google_vignette|website=NFL Draft Diamonds|access-date=October 12, 2025}}</ref> He finished his college career with 3,196 rushing yards and 28 touchdowns on 537 carries. <ref> {{cite web|last= Kuhagen|first= Christopher|date= August 9, 2025|title= Who is Amar Johnson? What to know about Packers running back after his breakout preseason game, highlights, stats and more|url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2025/08/09/amar-johnson-green-bay-packers-running-back/85596567007/#|website= Milwaukee Journal Sentinel|access-date=October 12, 2025}}</ref> He also added 518 receiving yards on 57 receptions.<ref>{{cite web|last=Lombardo|first=Matt|date=May 27, 2025|title=Green Bay Packers’ 28 Touchdown Rookie Has Path to Making an Impact|url=https://wisportsheroics.com/amar-johnson-underrated-green-bay-packers-news/|website=Wisconsin Sports Heroics|access-date=October 12, 2025}}</ref>

===Green Bay Packers===
After going undrafted in the [[2025 NFL draft]], Johnson signed with the [[Green Bay Packers]], which was the team he had hoped to be drafted by.<ref>{{cite web|last=Boston|first=Freddie|date=May 1, 2025|title=Packers steal hidden gem RB who prayed other teams wouldn't draft him|url=https://lombardiave.com/packers-steal-hidden-gem-rb-prayed-other-teams-wouldnt-draft-him|website=Lombardi Ave|access-date=October 12, 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Huber|first=Bill|date=May 1, 2025|title=All-American Running Back ‘Felt the Love’ from Packers|url=https://www.si.com/nfl/packers/onsi/all-american-running-back-felt-amar-johnson-love-from-packers|website=Sports Illustrated|access-date=October 12, 2025}}</ref> On May 2, 2025, he signed a three-year contract worth $2.98 million with the Packers.<ref name=contractandtransactions> {{cite web|title=Amar Johnson - NFL Contracts & Salaries - Spotrac.com
|url=https://www.spotrac.com/nfl/player/transactions/_/id/98320/amar-johnson
|website=Spotrac.com|access-date=October 12, 2025}}</ref> In the Packers' first preseason game against the [[2025 New York Jets season|New York Jets]], Johnson led the team in rushing with 67 yards, 7 carries, and Green Bay’s only touchdown, a 39-yard rush, in the 30-10 loss. He also had the 3rd-highest grade of any NFL running back in the week.<ref>{{cite web|last=Reis|first=Felipe|date=August 15, 2025|title=Could We See Amar Johnson Running the Ball For Green Bay In the Regular Season?|url=https://zonecoverage.com/2025/packers/could-we-see-amar-johnson-running-the-ball-for-green-bay-in-the-regular-season/|website=Zone Coverage|access-date=October 12, 2025}}</ref>

The next week against the [[2025 Indianapolis Colts season|Indianapolis Colts]], he scored another rushing touchdown along with seven carries, second on the team behind [[Israel Abanikanda]], and one reception.<ref>{{cite web|last=Widmeier|first=Mitch|date=August 20, 2025|title=Is There A Practice Squad Battle Between Amar Johnson and Israel Abanikanda?|url=https://zonecoverage.com/2025/packers/is-there-a-practice-squad-battle-between-amar-johnson-and-israel-abanikanda/|website=Zone Coverage|access-date = October 12, 2025}}</ref> He ended the preseason with 115 yards and two touchdowns on 22 carries, along with two receptions for 21 yards.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gebrewold|first=Caleb|date=August 25, 2025|title=Packers might lose this breakout rookie if they try to stash him|url=https://lombardiave.com/packers-might-lose-breakout-rookie-try-stash-him|website=Lombardi Ave|access-date=October 12, 2025}}</ref> Despite his performance, he was waived by the Packers on August 26.<ref name=contractandtransactions/>

===Los Angeles Chargers===
On September 2, 2025, Johnson was signed to the practice squad of the [[Los Angeles Chargers]].<ref name=contractandtransactions/> On January 13, 2026, he signed a reserve/futures contract with Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite web |date=January 13, 2026 |title=Los Angeles Chargers Sign 14 Players to Contracts |url=https://www.chargers.com/news/sign-14-players-to-contracts-2026 |access-date=14 January 2026 |website=Chargers.com}}</ref>
